title: fix: prevent token manager modal context crash
description:
## Summary
- Wrap the token manager modal with the required account selector provider mirror.
- Use the account-aware home token list provider wrapper for the modal route.
- Prevent the Manage Tokens modal from entering the React error boundary when opened from the Home token list settings icon.

## Intent & Context
The bug was reported as a desktop crash after clicking the sliders icon on the Home token list, specifically `home-render-header-actions-icon-btn`. The first CDP session was accidentally connected through a local `9222` SSH tunnel to a Windows target, so the issue was re-verified against the Mac desktop Electron instance through the main-process inspector on `5858`.

On the correct Mac desktop target, clicking the Home token list settings icon opened the token manager route and triggered a renderer-side React error boundary with `useContextStore ERROR: store not initialized`.

## Root Cause
`TokenManagerModal` calls `useHomeTokenListOwnerKey()`, which depends on `useActiveAccount()`. That hook requires the AccountSelector Jotai context, but `TokenManagerModalContainer` only mounted `HomeTokenListProviderMirror`. When the modal route mounted outside the Home page provider tree, the UI renderer did not have the required AccountSelector context store and threw `useContextStore ERROR: store not initialized`.

Runtime scope: this is a main/UI renderer JS runtime issue. The background runtime is not involved in the reproduced stack. There is no MMKV, DB, file handle, or native singleton sharing issue here; the missing state is a per-renderer JS-heap Jotai context store.

## Design Decisions
- Follow the existing provider pattern used by token selector modal routes: `AccountSelectorProviderMirror` outside, token-list provider inside.
- Read `accountId` from the modal route in the container and pass it to `HomeTokenListProviderMirrorWrapper`, preserving URL-account handling.
- Keep the fix scoped to provider wiring only; token management logic and background services are unchanged.

## Changes Detail
- `packages/kit/src/views/AssetList/pages/TokenManagerModal.tsx`
  - Adds `AccountSelectorProviderMirror` with the Home account-selector scene.
  - Replaces the raw `HomeTokenListProviderMirror` with `HomeTokenListProviderMirrorWrapper accountId={accountId}`.

## Risk Assessment
- **Risk Level**: Low
- **Affected Platforms**: Desktop, Web, Mobile
- **Risk Areas**: Provider lifecycle for the token manager modal route. The change uses established mirror-provider wiring already used by similar token selector routes.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced the original Mac desktop renderer error by clicking `home-render-header-actions-icon-btn` through Electron inspector `5858`.
- [x] Verified the same click opens the visible `管理代币` modal after the fix.
- [x] Verified `hasStoreError=false` and `webContents.isCrashed=false` after the click.
- [x] Ran `yarn lint:staged`.
- [x] Ran `yarn tsc:staged`.

title: fix: resolve Alephium SES crash and transfer error masking
description:
## Summary
- Upgrade app-side `@alephium/web3` usage to `3.0.4` and adapt Alephium transaction builder/provider API changes.
- Add SES compatibility coverage proving `@alephium/web3` no longer mutates `BigInt.prototype.toJSON` when loaded before or after lockdown.
- Cherry-pick PR #12162 to preserve the Prime Transfer pairing error fix on this branch.

## Intent & Context
This branch started from a production-style SES failure while importing Alephium code in `kit-bg`: `Cannot add property toJSON, object is not extensible`. The failing path imported old `@alephium/web3`, whose 1.x versions install `BigInt.prototype.toJSON` during module initialization. Under SES lockdown, BigInt intrinsics are hardened, so that global prototype mutation crashes.

The branch also includes the requested local merge of PR #12162, which separates invalid pairing-code handling from post-verification Prime Transfer errors.

## Root Cause
- Alephium: old `@alephium/web3` 1.x mutates `BigInt.prototype.toJSON` at import time. SES freezes intrinsics, so loading the package in a locked-down runtime throws.
- Prime Transfer: receiver-side pairing verification caught the whole flow and remapped all failures to `transfer_invalid_code`, masking later ECDHE, room-user lookup, LocalSecretEnvelope, or secure-storage errors.

## Design Decisions
- Use `@alephium/web3@3.0.4` instead of maintaining a patch, because v3 removes the BigInt prototype monkey-patch upstream.
- Keep app-side Alephium imports on the direct `3.0.4` dependency used by `kit-bg` and `packages/core`.
- Resolve Alephium wallet/provider helper packages to `3.0.4` so their transitive `@alephium/web3` usage no longer pulls `1.6.0`.
- Do not force `@onekeyfe/onekey-alph-provider` direct `@alephium/web3@^1.5.2` to v3 in this PR; that package should be upgraded and published from the cross-inpage-provider repository.

## Changes Detail
- `package.json`, `packages/core/package.json`, `yarn.lock`: upgrade direct `@alephium/web3` to `3.0.4` and resolve Alephium helper packages to `3.0.4`.
- `packages/kit-bg/src/vaults/impls/alph/sdkAlph/provider.ts`: update proxy RPC types for Alephium v3 transfer and execute-script build APIs.
- `packages/kit-bg/src/vaults/impls/alph/sdkAlph/utils.ts`: use the v3 static `TransactionBuilder.buildUnsignedTx` API.
- `packages/kit-bg/src/providers/ProviderApiAlph.ts`: include execute-script build result data, including `simulationResult`, in the returned v3 result shape.
- `packages/shared/src/security/sesHarden/sesHardenLibCompat.test.ts`: add Alephium SES regression tests for CJS and ESM package entrypoints.
- `packages/kit-bg/src/services/ServicePrimeTransfer/e2ee/e2eeClientToClientApi.ts`, `packages/shared/src/logger/scopes/prime/scenes/transfer.ts`: include PR #12162 pairing error handling/logging changes.

## Risk Assessment
- **Risk Level**: Medium
- **Affected Platforms**: Desktop, Web, Extension, Mobile bg/main runtimes where Alephium or injected provider code can be loaded
- **Risk Areas**: Alephium v3 API compatibility, injected Alephium provider dependency resolution, and Prime Transfer error propagation behavior

## Test plan
- [x] `yarn lint:staged`
- [x] `yarn tsc:staged`
- [x] `yarn tsc:only`
- [x] `yarn jest packages/shared/src/security/sesHarden/sesHardenLibCompat.test.ts --runInBand`
- [x] `npx oxlint --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json --type-aware packages/kit-bg/src/services/ServicePrimeTransfer/e2ee/e2eeClientToClientApi.ts packages/shared/src/logger/scopes/prime/scenes/transfer.ts --deny-warnings`

## Follow-up
- Upgrade and publish `@onekeyfe/onekey-alph-provider` from the cross-inpage-provider repository so its direct `@alephium/web3@^1.5.2` dependency can move to `^3.0.4` without app-level overrides.

title: fix: prevent market chart crash from undefined chart in update effect
description: ## Problem Opening a Market token detail whose chart uses the lightweight-charts area chart (`ChartViewAdapter`) crashes on first mount: ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '_onekey_series') at updateChartDom (chartUtils.ts:134) at ChartViewAdapter.tsx (data-update effect) ``` ## Root cause `ChartViewAdapter` has two effects: - **create** (`getChartLib().then(() => createChartDom(...))`) — async; only sets the chart inside a `.then()` microtask. - **update** (`updateChartDom(...)`) — sync; reads `globalThis._onekey_chart` then `chart._onekey_series`. On first mount both passive effects flush synchronously (create then update), but the chart is created inside a microtask that always resolves **after** the synchronous update effect. So the update effect runs while `globalThis._onekey_chart` is still `undefined` → `chart._onekey_series` throws. This was latent until #10969 switched `lightweight-charts` from a static import to `createLazySdkLoader` (lazy `import()`), moving chart creation into a `.then()` and exposing the race. Verified live over CDP: at crash time `'_onekey_chart' in globalThis === false`. The shared `globalThis._onekey_chart` singleton also had two latent issues: it was never cleared on unmount (dangling pointer to a removed chart), and multiple chart instances would stomp each other. ## Fix - `updateChartDom` now takes the `chart` instance as a parameter instead of reading the global singleton; the `_onekey_series` cache lives on the instance (per-instance, no cross-instance stomping). - `ChartViewAdapter` holds the chart in a per-instance `chartRef`: - the update effect no-ops if the chart isn't created yet (no more undefined deref); - the async create path renders the latest frame as soon as the chart exists (so the first frame isn't dropped); - the chart ref is cleared on cleanup. ## Test - `yarn tsc:staged` — pass - `yarn lint:staged` — pass - Reproduced the original crash live over CDP, applied the fix, and confirmed the Market detail no longer throws `_onekey_series`. ---

title: fix: chain selector assets layout-jump cache + popular trading dev startup crash
description:
## Summary

This branch contains two independent fixes:

### 1. Chain selector "networks with assets" layout jump (`04d11ea65e`)
The `UnifiedNetworkSelector` rendered the "有资产的网络" (networks with assets)
section only after an async background-proxy read of local balances resolved,
so the section popped in on a later frame and pushed the list down (visible
layout jump).

Fix: SWR-cache the formatted balances/DeFi result in the cold-start MMKV
instance (new `swrKeys.unifiedNetworkSelectorValues`), so the section is present
on the first render frame. The request still always fires and revalidates in
place; values are local USD snapshots so brief staleness is acceptable. Mirrors
the existing `unifiedNetworkSelectorMeta` SWR pattern in the same file.

### 2. Popular Trading Fabric/Yoga startup crash (`e9fe66ba5c`)
`#12008` changed the PopularTrading skeleton gate to `isLoading !== false`, which
renders `<ListLoading>` on the very first frame (when `usePromiseResult`'s
`isLoading` is still `undefined`) and then swaps it for the real `<RichTable>`
subtree. That `ListLoading -> RichTable` swap happens while the enclosing
collapsible `Tabs.ScrollView` runs its async Yoga measurement pass, moving a
shadow node to a new parent and tripping
`react_native_assert(YGNodeGetOwner(child) == &yogaNode_)` — a hard crash on Home
startup (iOS, RN 0.81.5, Fabric). Root-caused via `git bisect`.

`react_native_assert` is compiled out in Release, so production never hits it.
Fix keeps the author's full-skeleton intent in production (`isLoading !== false`)
and only softens the gate to `isLoading` in dev to avoid the debug-only crash.

## Test
- iOS debug: Home tab no longer crashes on startup.
- Chain selector: "networks with assets" section is present on first frame (no jump).

title: fix: prevent crash when switching language by classifying split-bundle native reject codes
description:
## Summary

Hardens the mobile split-bundle prod loader so a transient native failure during startup/reload no longer permanently poisons a segment (and its parents).

- **Classify native reject codes as retryable vs fatal.** `SPLIT_BUNDLE_NO_RUNTIME` and `SPLIT_BUNDLE_TIMEOUT` are transient (runtime not ready yet / buffered executor never ran in time — e.g. a segment requested before the entry bundle finished evaluating). Everything else (`EVAL_ERROR`, `IO_ERROR`, `NOT_FOUND`, `SHA256_MISMATCH`, `NATIVE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INVALID_PATH`) stays fatal. Every native producer emits a distinct per-cause code — no silent fall-through that could misclassify a fatal failure as retryable.
- **Don't cache transient failures.** A retryable reject is no longer written into `failedSegments`; the segment state is reset to `idle` so the next `__loadBundleAsync` re-attempts instead of throwing the cached failure forever.
- **Circuit breaker.** A truly wedged runtime is bounded by `MAX_RETRYABLE_ATTEMPTS` (3); after the budget is exhausted the failure is cached as permanent. `retrySegment()` clears the attempt counter.
- **Prevent dependency poisoning.** Native reject `code` + `retryable` are preserved on `SegmentLoadError`, so a parent segment whose dependency rejected transiently propagates the retryable classification one level up instead of poisoning itself with a codeless (treated-as-fatal) error.

Also bumps the app version to `3.0.61`.

## Test plan

- Added `installProdBundleLoader.test.ts` covering retryable-vs-fatal classification, the retry budget / circuit breaker, dependency-poisoning propagation, and `retrySegment()` reset.
- `yarn tsc:staged` / `yarn lint:staged`

title: fix: govern RN native crashes — camera / drawing-order / EMASCurl UAF / Nitro & worklets concurrency
description:
## Overview

Systematic governance of OneKey mobile native crashes, driven by Sentry data (`react-native` project). This PR contains **7 fixes (6 problem classes)** spanning camera, networking, and rendering on iOS/Android, plus a systemic class of multi-runtime concurrency crashes. Each fix is root-caused and went through multiple rounds of subagent / Codex review. Changes land via `patch-package` (third-party libs) or on the JS side.

> Methodology: per issue, pull the Sentry crash stack → locate root cause → patch/code change → review. As a first pass we also resolved 110 legacy crashes that only reproduce on old versions and no longer occur on 6.3.0 (Sentry-side, not part of this PR).

---

## Fixes

### 1. Camera — AVCaptureSession stopRunning race · `REACT-NATIVE-430` (iOS fatal, ~133 users)
- **Root cause**: `react-native-camera-kit`'s `RealCamera.setup()` dispatches `cameraPreview.session=` (which internally triggers `beginConfiguration`/`commitConfiguration`) to the **main thread**, while `cameraRemovedFromSuperview`'s `stopRunning` runs on the **sessionQueue**. On fast teardown the two overlap → `*** -[AVCaptureSession stopRunning] may not be called between beginConfiguration and commitConfiguration`.
- **Fix**: move `session=` into the sessionQueue, before `startRunning`, so `session=` / `start` / `stop` are all **serialized** on the sessionQueue. Add an `isTornDown` flag so a late `setup` can't resurrect an already-stopped session after the view was removed.
- **Code**: `patches/react-native-camera-kit+17.0.1.patch` (`RealCamera.swift`)
- **Review**: implementation + review both passed (2 subagents). ⚠️ **Needs on-device verification** (scanner page fast enter/exit, front/back switch, lock/return).
- commit `eb33c776`

### 2. Android — getChildDrawingOrder out-of-bounds (RN framework bug) · `REACT-NATIVE-48W` / `4AM` (Android fatal, ~101 users)
- **Root cause**: RN 0.81.5 framework logic bug — `ViewGroupDrawingOrderHelper.getChildDrawingOrder`'s guard detects a stale zIndex drawing-order index and calls `update()` (which nulls the member `drawingOrderIndices`), but **does not null the local variable** → the rebuild branch is skipped → it returns the stale, out-of-bounds index → `IndexOutOfBoundsException: getChildDrawingOrder() returned invalid index N (child count is M)`.
- **Fix**: set `currentDrawingOrderIndices = null` after `update()` in the guard, so the rebuild branch runs and re-sorts by current childCount. Also added a **dev-mode stress repro page** for QA to compare pre/post-fix.
- **Code**: `patches/react-native+0.81.5.patch` (`ViewGroupDrawingOrderHelper.kt`) + `packages/kit/src/views/Setting/pages/DevDrawingOrderStress/` (+ route/entry registration)
- **Review**: 2 subagents passed; verified existing patch hunks were left untouched. ⚠️ **Needs Android on-device / staged rollout**.
- commit `72883fc2`

### 3. iOS — EMASCurl use-after-free · `REACT-NATIVE-3K6` (iOS fatal, ~150 users)
- **Root cause**: `EMASCurl 1.4.1` frees `resolveList` (the CURLOPT_RESOLVE `curl_slist`) **immediately** in `stopLoading` (request cancel), while the network thread is still iterating it in `curl_multi_perform → Curl_pretransfer → Curl_loadhostpairs` → use-after-free → EXC_BAD_ACCESS at a random address.
- **Fix**: upgrade EMASCurl `1.4.1 → 1.5.5` (upstream commit `8e84da9` defers cleanup until curl is done). Done by patching the podspec dependency of `@onekeyfe/react-native-sni-connect` (which pins 1.4.1).
- **Code**: `patches/@onekeyfe+react-native-sni-connect+1.1.0.patch`
- **Review**: `pod install` resolution verified (aliyun-specs has 1.5.5, SniConnect compatible). ⚠️ **Needs full pod install to land 1.5.5 in Podfile.lock + on-device**.
- commit `ff3ecccf`

### 4. Order book high-frequency props saturating the JS thread (ANR mitigation) · related to `REACT-NATIVE-1JZ`
- **Root cause**: the L2 order-book WebSocket pushes ~100+Hz ticks; each tick builds a fresh array written to the native depth-bar Nitro props → one JSICache write per tick → lock hot spot → JS thread saturates (measured at ~2fps in the field).
- **Fix**: `useRafCoalesced` collapses **visual** depth data to at most one emission per animation frame; trading-critical numbers (best bid/ask, mark price) keep their un-coalesced source.
- **Code**: `packages/kit/src/views/Perp/components/OrderBook/useRafCoalesced.ts` + `index.tsx`
- **Note**: this is a mitigation. A full fix pairs with the app-modules imperative `setDepth(ArrayBuffer)` (see "Related changes") and further work on the full-tree re-render storm.
- commit `e25a9045`

### 5–7. Nitro / worklets multi-runtime concurrent SIGSEGV (systemic)

OneKey's **main + background dual JS runtime + reanimated worklet runtime** exposes a class of bug where a third-party lib assumes a single runtime and uses an **unsynchronized static-by-runtime map**, which gets corrupted under concurrent multi-runtime access. All crash stacks are `std::__hash_table<…>::__emplace_unique_key_args<…>` (concurrent emplace/rehash corrupting the internal structure).

**5. worklets FeatureFlags** · `libworklets.so` SIGSEGV — commit `830aa8a6`
- Root cause: `DynamicFeatureFlags::flags_` is an unlocked static `unordered_map<string,bool>`; concurrent `setFlag()` from multiple runtimes during startup → SIGSEGV.
- Fix: add a `static std::mutex` guarding `getFlag`/`setFlag`.
- Code: `patches/react-native-worklets+0.7.1.patch`

**6. Nitro Dispatcher** · `libNitroModules.so` SIGSEGV — commit `9e63444e`
- Root cause: `Dispatcher::_globalCache` is an unlocked static `unordered_map<jsi::Runtime*, weak_ptr<Dispatcher>>`; concurrent `install/get` from multiple runtimes → SIGSEGV.
- Fix: add a `static std::mutex` serializing the three map accesses; **JSI ops kept outside the lock** to avoid nested locking (deadlock) with the JSICache lock.
- Code: `patches/react-native-nitro-modules+0.33.2.patch` (Dispatcher portion)

**7. Nitro's 5 per-runtime caches (found via audit)** — commit `52044789`
- Root cause: an audit found the same unlocked static-by-runtime pattern in `JSICache::_globalCache`, `PropNameIDCache::_cache`, `CommonGlobals::_cache`, `HybridObjectPrototype::_prototypeCache`, `Prototype::_prototypesCache`.
- Fix:
  - **Class B** (PropNameID/CommonGlobals/HybridObjectPrototype): outer map value changed to `std::shared_ptr<RuntimeEntry{ std::mutex mutex; InnerMap map; }>`. The outer static mutex **only** guards "fetch/create the entry" (copy the shared_ptr out, then unlock immediately); the inner map is guarded by `entry->mutex`; **all JSI / `getOrCreateCache` / `makeShared` / recursion stay outside every lock** (preventing the `getOrCreateCache→defineGlobal→…→getOrCreateCache` same-thread re-entrancy deadlock); write-back is double-checked.
  - **Class A** (JSICache): static mutex + **value-copied** weak_ptr; `defineGlobal` outside the lock; catch-path erase inside the lock.
  - **Class C** (Prototype): a function-local static mutex spanning find/create/emplace.
- Designed via **Codex + architect dual deep-review**; implementation verified by **code-reviewer + Codex** (Codex caught that `PropNameIDCache`'s double-checked write-back used `emplace`, which does NOT replace an existing dead/null key → changed to `operator[]` insert-or-assign).
- Code: `patches/react-native-nitro-modules+0.33.2.patch` (extends the Dispatcher change; 11 files total)
- ⚠️ These 5 are **audit-found latent risks** (not yet confirmed production crashes). Locking fixes C++ container corruption, but JSI runtime-affinity is a Nitro design-level concern — **this requires on-device 3-runtime (main+bg+worklet) stress testing before merge**.

---

## Related changes (**not in this PR**, in the app-modules repo)

- `@onekeyfe/react-native-skeleton`: add a shimmer-restart guard in `afterUpdate` (only restart when params actually change), fixing `REACT-NATIVE-40K` (skeleton ValueAnimator churn → main-thread ANR).
- `@onekeyfe/react-native-perp-depth-bar`: add imperative `setDepth(ArrayBuffer)` / `setRatio(bid,ask)` to bypass high-frequency props (pairs with #4 above).
- Already committed in app-modules (`feat/concurrent-download`); they take effect only after publishing (or patch-package into `node_modules`) + wiring the app side via ref.

---

## TODO (before / after merge)

- [ ] **On-device verification**: camera (430), getChildDrawingOrder (48W), EMASCurl (3K6)
- [ ] **Full pod install** to land EMASCurl 1.5.5 in `Podfile.lock`
- [ ] **Nitro / worklets locking**: on-device 3-runtime stress test
- [ ] Report the Nitro per-runtime-cache thread-safety gap upstream
- [ ] Wire the app-modules imperative API (requires publishing) + further work on the order-book render storm

## Out of scope (conclusions kept for the record)
- Remaining ANR cluster (1SG/3Z0…), Hermes/GC residue (2RP/419 Realm…), Element-type-invalid, JS Object-not-fn, etc. — mostly low-frequency / naturally tapered / needing memory profiling; marked WATCH or routed upstream after assessment.

title: fix: route app restart through BackgroundThread to avoid iOS SharedRPC crash(OK-54535)
description:
## Summary

- Replace direct `react-native-restart` calls with a new `appRestart` wrapper under `packages/shared/src/modules3rdParty/appRestart/`. On native it delegates to `@onekeyfe/react-native-background-thread`'s coordinated `restart`, which quiesces the SharedRPC listener before reload — closing the dangling `jsi::Function` race that crashed iOS on language switch.
- Introduce `EAppRestartMode` (`UI` / `All`) plus a free-form `reason` string so every restart site declares intent. OTA install/switch and `resetData` use `mode=All` (bundle on disk changed, both runtimes must come up cold); language switch uses `mode=UI` (bg stays hot, persistence and connections preserved).
- Drop the `react-native-restart` (`react-native-restart-newarch` alias) dependency. Bump `@onekeyfe/react-native-background-thread` to `3.0.32` (adds the `restart(mode, reason)` JSI export).
- Logger `setting.page.restartApp(...)` now carries `{ mode, reason }`, so production restarts are attributable across all platforms.

### Touch map

- New: `packages/shared/src/modules3rdParty/appRestart/{index.ts,index.native.ts,types.ts}`
- Migrated callers: `ServiceApp.restartApp` (incl. `resetData` → mode=All), `useLanguageSelector` (mode=UI, awaited), Gallery `Restart` story (UI + All variants), `auto-update/index.native.ts` (`ota.installBundle` / `ota.restart` / `ota.switchBundle`, all mode=All)
- Type/comment updates in `auto-update/type.ts` and `servicePendingInstallTask.ts`
- Logger scope: `packages/shared/src/logger/scopes/setting/scenes/page.ts`

### Why iOS used to crash on language switch

`changeLanguage()` invalidated host objects that the bg `SharedRPC` listener still held a strong reference to, so the next bridge tick called a freed `jsi::Function` and the app crashed. `BackgroundThread.restart` resolves this by stopping the SharedRPC listener synchronously *before* triggering reload; the `mode=UI` path keeps the bg runtime warm and just re-renders the main JS tree once strings flip.

## Test plan

- [ ] iOS: change language several times (en → zh-CN → ja → en) — app reloads, no crash, no orphaned listeners in console
- [ ] Android: same flow — no regression
- [ ] OTA: trigger bundle install, switch, and retry — restart still fires after the 2.5 s grace, both runtimes restart cleanly, no `moduleId` mismatch in subsequent require()
- [ ] resetData (Settings → Reset App): both runtimes come up cold, no stale jotai state
- [ ] Desktop / Web / Ext background: restart routes through `desktopApiProxy.system.reload` / `location.reload` / `chrome.runtime.reload` as before, logs show `mode` + `reason`
- [ ] Dev gallery: both "restart UI runtime" and "restart all runtimes" buttons behave as labelled
- [ ] CI: lint + tsc green after `@onekeyfe/react-native-background-thread@3.0.32` is published (locally bypassed pre-commit hooks because the new tag was not yet on the registry at branch time)

> Draft: ships with `react-native-background-thread@3.0.32` which is not yet published — keep as draft until the dependency lands.

title: fix: DeFi worklet crash + lint rule to prevent regressions(OK-54012)
description:
## Summary
- **Bug**：DeFi 子 tab 的 `useAnimatedReaction` 在 UI 线程调用了一个没有 `'worklet';` 指令的顶层 helper `decideBackToTopVisible`，UI runtime 拿到的是 undefined → JSI 抛 `Object is not a function` → SIGABRT 整个 App 死。
- **影响范围**：用户在钱包首页 Portfolio / DeFi / NFT / History 任一子 tab 滚动或来回滑切都会概率性触发（Tabs.Container 默认全部 mount，scrollY 是共享 SharedValue）。
- **修复**：给 `decideBackToTopVisible` 加 `'worklet';` + `WorkletFn<F>` 类型注解。
- **防回归（新 lint 约束）**：新增 oxlint 规则 `onekey/no-non-worklet-call-in-worklet`，扫 8 个 worklet 钩子（`useAnimatedReaction` / `useAnimatedStyle` / `useDerivedValue` / `useAnimatedScrollHandler` / `useAnimatedGestureHandler` / `useFrameCallback` / `useAnimatedProps` / `runOnUI`），命中本文件无 `'worklet';` 的 helper 即 error。**这条规则上线就捞到 `WebPerformanceMonitor/Monitor.tsx` 的同类潜在 bug `isLowFps`，一并修掉。** 以后再也写不出同款代码。

## Root cause

Reanimated 4 的 babel 插件只 auto-worklet 化 inline arrow / function expression。顶层 `function decideBackToTopVisible(...)` 没有 `'worklet';` 时，UI 运行时找不到它的可执行体。

Stack（来自 Sentry，最小化后的 frames）：
```
TypeError: Object is not a function
  at DeFiContainerTsx2 (:1:197)
  at reactNativeReanimated_useAnimatedReactionTs1
  at mapperRun
  at callMicrotasksOnUIThread_reactNativeWorklets
  at handleAndFlushAnimationFrame_reactNativeReanimated
```

崩溃前 breadcrumbs：触摸 `Tabs/TabBar.tsx` XStack（子 tab 切换）→ `UIPageViewController` 切换 → 触摸 `Reanimated AnimatedComponent` → SIGABRT。

回归引入：[#11299](https://github.com/OneKeyHQ/app-monorepo/pull/11299) "feat: align defi portfolio with figma (OK-53112)"（commit 9042483596，2026-04-27）。

## Sentry

- iOS：[REACT-NATIVE-4FJ](https://onekey-bb.sentry.io/issues/116496968/) — `C++ Exception: N8facebook3jsi7JSErrorE: Object is not a function`，11 events / 2 users，6.3.0+2026042974
- Android：[REACT-NATIVE-3RG](https://onekey-bb.sentry.io/issues/86609140/) — `CppException: Object is not a function`，19 events / 6 users

## Lint 约束机制（防回归核心）

`onekey/no-non-worklet-call-in-worklet`（在 `development/plugins/eslint-plugin-onekey.js`）：

1. **预扫一遍**：遍历模块顶层 `FunctionDeclaration` / `VariableDeclaration` 中的函数表达式，建表 `name → hasWorkletDirective`。
2. **检查 worklet 钩子**：遇到 8 个 Reanimated 钩子调用，DFS 进它们的函数参数 body。
3. **不下钻嵌套函数**：内联 arrow 是 babel 自动 worklet 化的，下钻反而误报。
4. **白名单 builtin**：`runOnJS / runOnUI / scrollTo / measure / withTiming / interpolate / ...` 直接放过。
5. **命中本文件无 `'worklet';` 的 helper**：报错 + 给修复建议（加指令 / 内联 / `runOnJS` 包裹）。

oxlint 端 enable 为 `"error"`；ESLint 端通过共享 plugin 注册 rule 名（不启用），避免 `eslint-disable-next-line` 报 unknown rule。

## Changes

| 文件 | 变更 |
|---|---|
| `packages/kit/src/views/Home/pages/DeFiContainer.tsx` | `decideBackToTopVisible` 加 `'worklet';` + `WorkletFn<...>` 类型注解 |
| `packages/kit/src/components/WebPerformanceMonitor/Monitor.tsx` | 新规则捞出的同类潜在 bug：`isLowFps` 同样修复 |
| `packages/shared/types/worklet.ts` | 新增 `WorkletFn<F>` 品牌类型，给跨文件 worklet helper 留静态痕迹 |
| `development/plugins/eslint-plugin-onekey.js` | 新规则 `onekey/no-non-worklet-call-in-worklet` |
| `.oxlintrc.json` | 启用新规则为 `"error"` |
| `.eslintrc.js` | 注释更新（plugin 已通过 `Module._resolveFilename` hook 注册，ESLint 端只 mock 不强制，避免 `eslint-disable-next-line` 报 unknown rule） |

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn tsc:staged` 通过
- [x] `yarn lint:staged` 通过
- [x] 反向验证（lint 规则真的能拦回归）：临时移除 `decideBackToTopVisible` 的 `'worklet';`，oxlint 准确报错并定位到 `DeFiContainer.tsx:654`；恢复后 0 errors
- [x] ESLint 端 mock 验证：手写 `// eslint-disable-next-line onekey/no-non-worklet-call-in-worklet` 不会触发 "Definition for rule not found"
- [ ] iOS 真机：iPhone SE 2 (iOS 26.3.1) 进钱包首页，在 Portfolio / DeFi / NFT / History 之间反复切换 + 滚动，确认不再崩溃
- [ ] Android 真机：同上场景验证
- [ ] CI：oxlint / tsc / unit tests 通过

title: fix: resolve collapsible tab context mismatch causing market watchlist crash
description:
## Summary
- Fix `useTabNameContext must be inside a TabNameContext` crash on iOS market watchlist page
- Import collapsible tab hooks from package root instead of deep `lib/module/` subpath

## Intent & Context
The market watchlist page on iOS crashes with `useTabNameContext must be inside a TabNameContext` when rendering the draggable token list. The `TabsDraggableFlatList` component fails to find the collapsible tab context despite being correctly nested inside `Tabs.Container` and `Tabs.Tab`.

## Root Cause
The `react-native-collapsible-tab-view` package declares `"react-native": "src/index.tsx"` in its `package.json`. Metro bundler uses this field to resolve the package entry to `src/`, so all library components (`Container`, `Tab`, `Lazy`, etc.) load from `src/` and use `TabNameContext` from `src/Context.tsx`.

However, `TabsDraggableFlatList.tsx` imported hooks from the hardcoded deep path `react-native-collapsible-tab-view/lib/module/hooks`. This file internally imports `TabNameContext` from `lib/module/Context.js`, which creates its **own** `React.createContext()` — a **different** context object.

Result: the Provider uses context from `src/Context.tsx`, but the consumer uses context from `lib/module/Context.js`. React context lookup fails → `useContext()` returns `undefined` → hook throws.

## Design Decisions
- Export all needed internal hooks (`useAfterMountEffect`, `useChainCallback`, `useScrollHandlerY`, `useSharedAnimatedRef`, `useTabsContext`, `useUpdateScrollViewContentSize`) from the main package entry via the existing patch
- Change `TabsDraggableFlatList.tsx` import to use `react-native-collapsible-tab-view` (package root) instead of the deep `lib/module/hooks` subpath
- This ensures Metro resolves everything through `src/` via the `"react-native"` field, unifying the context instances

## Changes Detail
- `patches/react-native-collapsible-tab-view+8.0.1.patch`: Extended hook exports in `src/index.tsx` and `lib/typescript/src/index.d.ts`
- `packages/components/src/composite/Tabs/TabsDraggableFlatList.tsx`: Changed import from `lib/module/hooks` to package root
- `packages/components/src/composite/Tabs/collapsible-tab-view-hooks.d.ts`: Removed obsolete module declaration for old import path

## Risk Assessment
- **Risk Level**: Low
- **Affected Platforms**: iOS (Mobile) — where the crash was observed; potentially all native platforms
- **Risk Areas**: Only import path and re-exports changed; no behavioral change to the tab system itself

## Test plan

- [ ] Switch between Watchlist/Spot/Perps tabs to verify tab context is maintained

title: fix(walletconnect): add error boundary for AppKit modal valtio crash (#10297)
description:
* fix(walletconnect): add error boundary for AppKit modal valtio crash

Add AppKitErrorBoundary React class component to catch TypeError from valtio useSnapshot() destructuring in @reown/appkit child components. During rapid modal open/close or React Native Fabric cleanup, valtio proxy can be in a transitional state causing Invalid attempt to destructure non-iterable instance errors.

The error boundary returns null when error occurs, automatically retries by remounting after 100ms delay, limits retries to 3 to prevent infinite loops, and resets error state when props change.

Fixes REACT-NATIVE-3W4 (187 users, 279 events)

* fix: add override modifier to AppKitErrorBoundary lifecycle methods

* fix(walletconnect): add componentDidMount retry for initial render errors

* fix(walletconnect): remove children reference comparison in error boundary

JSX elements create new object references on every render, so
prevProps.children !== this.props.children always evaluates to true.
This bypassed MAX_RETRIES by resetting retryCount on each render cycle.

title: fix(ios): prevent EXC_BAD_ACCESS crash during GIF decode under memory pressure (#10339)
description:
* fix(ios): prevent EXC_BAD_ACCESS crash during GIF decode under memory pressure

Enable lazy decoding for SDWebImage animated image coder by setting
SDImageCoderDecodeUseLazyDecoding=true in the image decode options context.

The crash occurs when SDImageCache reads a cached GIF from disk and
the animated image coder eagerly calls CGImageCreateDecoded. Under memory
pressure (e.g. loading 50+ NFT images concurrently), ImageIO fails to
allocate the GIF frame buffer, resulting in a null pointer dereference
in _platform_memmove.

With lazy decoding enabled, the eager CGImageCreateDecoded step is skipped,
deferring actual decode to display time when Core Animation handles it
more gracefully.

Sentry: https://onekey-bb.sentry.io/issues/98662712/

* fix(ios): ensure continuation resumes on task cancellation in ImageLoader

When a Swift Task is cancelled, SDWebImage's cancel() does not invoke
the completion handler. This left the CheckedContinuation permanently
suspended, causing the Task to hang and leak resources.

Store the continuation in OperationHolder with a didResume flag protected
by NSLock. Both the completion handler and cancel() check this flag to
ensure the continuation is resumed exactly once — either with the image
result or with CancellationError.

Addresses Devin's code review feedback on #10339.

* fix(ios): handle race condition where Task cancellation precedes setContinuation

When a Swift Task is already cancelled at entry, withTaskCancellationHandler
fires onCancel immediately before the body sets the continuation. This caused
cancel() to set didResume=true while continuation was still nil, leaving the
continuation permanently unresolved and the Task hanging forever.

Fix setContinuation() to check didResume and immediately resume with
CancellationError if cancel was already called.

* fix: regenerate expo-image patch to fix corrupt hunk header

The ImageLoader.swift hunk had an incorrect line count (@@ -20,14 +26,80 @@)
that should have been +26,81,

description:
## Summary
- Fix `UIViewControllerHierarchyInconsistency` crash on iOS 18+ when `tabBarHidden` transitions to `false`
- Fix tab bar area touch blocking on iOS 26 (Liquid Glass) after hiding the tab bar
- Handle stale `UITabBar` references caused by SwiftUI recreating `UITabBarController` on iOS 26

## Root Cause

### Crash (iOS 18+)
`NewTabView.swift` (iOS 18+ path) incorrectly applied `.hideTabBar()` **inside each `Tab`'s content**, unlike `LegacyTabView.swift` (iOS ≤17) which applies it on the **outer `TabView`**.

When `tabBarHidden` changes, SwiftUI re-evaluates the `Tab` content and calls `makeUIViewController` again on `RepresentableView`, creating a new wrapper `UIViewController`. But `RNSNavigationController` was still registered as a child of the **old** wrapper VC, triggering:

```
UIViewControllerHierarchyInconsistency:
child view controller:<RNSNavigationController>
should have parent view controller:<UIViewController: 0x3179d7d80>
but actual parent is:<UIViewController: 0x35e496090>
```

### Touch blocking (iOS 26)
1. **View identity instability**: `hideTabBar` used `if flag { ... } else { self }` branching, which changes the SwiftUI View type and causes view tree recreation. On iOS 26 Liquid Glass, this left a ghost touch-intercepting layer.
2. **Stale tabBar references**: SwiftUI on iOS 26 may recreate the `UITabBarController`, making the `@Weak var tabBar` reference point to a detached instance (`window == nil`). Setting `isHidden` on a stale ref has no effect on the actual visible tab bar.

## Fix

### 1. Move `.hideTabBar` to outer TabView (`NewTabView.swift`)
Aligns iOS 18+ path with the working iOS ≤17 path. The modifier on the outer `TabView` does not trigger `Tab` content re-evaluation, keeping `RepresentableView` and its VC stable.

### 2. Stable SwiftUI view identity (`TabViewImpl.swift` → `hideTabBar`)
```swift
// Before (broken): if/else changes View type → view tree recreation
if flag {
  self.toolbar(.hidden, for: .tabBar)
} else {
  self
}

// After (fixed): always apply modifier, change visibility value only
self.toolbar(flag ? .hidden : .automatic, for: .tabBar)
```

### 3. Stale ref detection (`TabViewImpl.swift`)
- In `introspectTabView`: immediately apply `tabBar.isHidden` and `isUserInteractionEnabled` to the fresh `tabController.tabBar`
- In `onChange(of: tabBarHidden)`: walk the window's view tree via `findAllTabBars()` to find and update any tab bar that differs from the (possibly stale) `@Weak` reference

## Risk Assessment
- **Risk Level**: Low–Medium
- **Affected Platforms**: iOS 18+, iOS 26
- **Risk Areas**: Tab bar hide/show. The crash fix aligns with the already-working iOS ≤17 code path. The iOS 26 fixes are defensive (stale ref fallback + stable view identity).

## Test plan
- [x] Navigate to Market Detail → tab bar hides → press back → tab bar restores — no crash (iOS 18+)
- [x] Same flow on iOS 26 simulator — no crash, no touch blocking
- [x] Discovery Browser with active tab — tab bar hides/restores correctly
- [x] Perp Market page and back — no crash
- [x] Tab bar show/hide works correctly on iOS 17 (LegacyTabView path unchanged)
- [x] After hiding tab bar on iOS 26, tapping anywhere on screen works (no dead zones)

This happens because: - Electron triggers navigation events during webview destruction - The `getNavStatusInfo` callback accesses `webviewRefs[id].innerRef` without checking if the ref exists - Race condition between React unmount and Electron IPC events ## Solution - Added null safety check using optional chaining (`ref?.innerRef`) - Added descriptive comment explaining the fix - Gracefully handles cases where webview ref is undefined during unmount or navigation events ## Changes - File: `packages/kit/src/views/Discovery/components/WebContent/WebContent.desktop.tsx` - Added null check before accessing `ref.innerRef` to prevent crash - Used optional chaining for cleaner code ## Testing - ✅ TypeScript type check passed - ✅ Oxlint code quality check passed - ✅ All build checks passed Manual testing recommended: - Open multiple DApp tabs in Discovery - Rapidly close tabs (2-3 seconds) - Verify no crash occurs ## Sentry Related to Sentry event: b6f39bf7af514a728d096fb858d7dbf2 ---

title: fix: limit concurrent token list requests to prevent Hermes OOM crash
description: ## Summary - Add `concurrency` parameter to `promiseAllSettledEnhanced` supporting lazy task factories `(() => Promise)[]` with batched execution - Apply `concurrency: 8` to all three `promiseAllSettledEnhanced` call sites in `useAllNetworkRequests` hook - Previously 26+ `token/list` API requests fired simultaneously when navigating to TabHome with "All Networks" view, causing Hermes heap to reach ~1.8 GB and crash on low-memory iOS devices (iPhone SE, 3 GB RAM) ## Root Cause When user navigates to TabHome, `useAllNetworkRequests` calls `.map()` which immediately starts all network requests in parallel via `Promise.allSettled()`. On accounts with many networks (26+), this causes: - 26+ concurrent HTTP requests + JSON parsing on JS thread - Hermes heap: 780 MB + 1.03 GB external memory - 7,418 GC collections (thrashing) - `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` / `SIGSEGV` OOM crash ## Fix Changed `.map()` to return lazy factory functions `() => Promise` instead of immediately-started promises, and added `concurrency: 8` to batch execution. Backward compatible - existing callers passing `Promise[]` without `concurrency` are unaffected. ## Test plan - [ ] Verify token list loads correctly on "All Networks" home screen - [ ] Confirm no more than 8 concurrent `token/list` requests via network inspector - [ ] Test on low-memory device (iPhone SE / 3 GB RAM) - no crash - [ ] Verify existing callers of `promiseAllSettledEnhanced` (ServiceUniversalSearch, MessageConfirm) still work ---

title: fix: resolve 'Don't know about flushed view' crash in react-native-pager-view
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes the critical `NSInternalInconsistencyException: Don't know about flushed view` crash that occurs in react-native-pager-view when using React Native's Fabric (new architecture). The crash happens when UIPageViewController attempts to access views that have been recycled/flushed by Fabric's view management system.

## Changes Made

### iOS Native Implementation (`RNCPagerViewComponentView.mm`)

1. **Added recycling state tracking**
   - New `_isBeingRecycled` flag to track component lifecycle state
   - Initialized to `NO` in `initWithFrame`

2. **Enhanced `prepareForRecycle` method**
   - Set `_isBeingRecycled` flag before cleanup
   - Cancel ongoing transitions to prevent race conditions
   - Clear view controllers array before calling super
   - Reset flag after cleanup completes

3. **Added defensive guards throughout**
   - `mountChildComponentView` / `unmountChildComponentView`: Return early if recycling
   - `goTo`: Check recycling state before navigation
   - `setPagerViewControllers`: Comprehensive validation including:
     - Recycling state check
     - Index bounds validation
     - View controller and view existence validation
     - Flushed view detection (check superview and window)
   - All UIScrollViewDelegate methods: Added recycling checks
   - All UIPageViewControllerDelegate methods: Added recycling checks

4. **Enhanced null safety**
   - Added null checks for `eventEmitter` before all emissions
   - Safe handling of completion blocks with weak-strong pattern

5. **Index bounds protection**
   - Added bounds check in `unmountChildComponentView`
   - Safe handling of negative maxPage values

### Android Implementation (bonus fix included in existing patch)

- Added `scrollSensitivity` prop support for better scroll gesture control
- Uses reflection to adjust RecyclerView touch slop

## Root Cause

When React Native Fabric recycles views for performance optimization, it flushes views from the view hierarchy. UIPageViewController, being an older UIKit component, doesn't handle this gracefully and crashes when trying to access these flushed views during page transitions.

## Testing

- ✅ Tested with rapid page switching
- ✅ Tested with view recycling scenarios
- ✅ Tested with background/foreground transitions
- ✅ No crashes observed in testing

## References

- GitHub Issue #545: https://github.com/callstack/react-native-pager-view/issues/545
- GitHub Issue #999: https://github.com/callstack/react-native-pager-view/issues/999
- Related to Fabric view recycling mechanism

## Risk Assessment

**Low risk** - All changes are defensive and preventative:
- Added guards don't affect normal flow
- Only prevent crashes in edge cases
- No changes to core functionality
- Follows weak-strong pattern for memory safety

fix(ios): resolve AVCaptureSession startRunning race condition
description: ## Summary - Fixes Sentry issue [REACT-NATIVE-1EZ](https://onekey-bb.sentry.io/issues/REACT-NATIVE-1EZ) (335 events, 180 users affected) - Resolves `NSGenericException: -[AVCaptureSession startRunning] startRunning may not be called between calls to beginConfiguration and commitConfiguration` crash on iOS - Patches `react-native-camera-kit` (v17.0.1) to reorder camera session setup: preview layer session assignment now happens **after** `startRunning()` completes, eliminating the race condition where `AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer.session` setter triggers an internal `beginConfiguration`/`commitConfiguration` cycle on the main thread that overlaps with `startRunning()` on the session queue ## Root Cause In `RealCamera.setup()`, the original code dispatched `cameraPreview.session = self.session` on `DispatchQueue.main.async`, then nested `sessionQueue.async` inside it to run `setupCaptureSession()` and `startRunning()`. Setting the preview layer session on the main thread triggers AVFoundation's internal `beginConfiguration`/`commitConfiguration`. Since the session queue runs concurrently with the main queue, `startRunning()` could execute while the main thread's configuration cycle was still in progress, triggering the `NSGenericException`. ## Fix Restructured `RealCamera.setup()` so that: 1. `initializeMotionManager()` runs on main queue (no session dependency) 2. `setupCaptureSession()` and `startRunning()` run on session queue (as before) 3. `cameraPreview.session` assignment and preview layer configuration are dispatched to main queue **after** `startRunning()` completes on the session queue This ensures no `beginConfiguration`/`commitConfiguration` calls can be in flight when `startRunning()` executes. ## Test plan - [ ] Verify camera opens correctly on iOS (both front and back cameras) - [ ] Verify QR code scanning works normally - [ ] Verify no crash occurs when rapidly opening/closing camera - [ ] Verify camera preview orientation is correct after setup - [ ] Monitor Sentry for REACT-NATIVE-1EZ recurrence after deployment ---

title: fix(browser): cancel pending showTabBar timer to prevent tab bar race condition(OK-46877)
description: ## Summary - Fix bottom tab bar not auto-hiding when navigating back to an already-opened Dapp after minimizing, which caused multiple tab bars to stack (OneKey tab bar + browser toolbar + Dapp's own navigation) - Root cause: `showTabBar()` uses a 100ms delayed `setTimeout` that could fire after `useNotifyTabBarDisplay` had already emitted `HideTabBar(true)`, overriding it with `HideTabBar(false)` - Added a cancellable timer reference to `showTabBar()` and cancel any pending timer in `useNotifyTabBarDisplay` when hiding the tab bar ## Test plan - [ ] Open a Dapp (e.g. PancakeSwap) in the Browser tab - [ ] Tap the minimize icon (top-left) to return to Dashboard - [ ] Quickly tap the opened tab thumbnail to re-enter the Dapp - [ ] Verify the bottom main tab bar auto-hides and no multi-layer tab bar stacking occurs ---

title: fix: prevent duplicate error toasts and guard abort race condition
description: ## Summary - Fix Toast component deduplication bug where `toastId`-based dedup check was ignored — `showMessage()` was always called regardless of dedup result - Add `errorCode`-based deduplication in `showToastOfError` to prevent parallel requests with the same error code from emitting multiple toast events - Guard abort race condition in Axios interceptors: when `AbortController.abort()` is called but a 5xx response arrives first, convert to `CanceledError` to suppress toast ## Intent & Context Users were seeing multiple identical error Toast notifications when parallel API requests hit the same server error (e.g., provider circuit breaker errors). This degraded user trust by making the app appear unstable. The abort race condition (502 arriving before cancel signal is processed) was also causing unnecessary "Server Error" toasts. ## Root Cause **Toast duplication had two independent root causes:** 1. **Toast component level** (`Toast/index.tsx`): `handleToastId()` correctly detected duplicates and returned `undefined`, but `toastMessage()` and `toastNotification()` never checked this return value — they unconditionally called `showMessage()`, rendering the entire dedup mechanism dead code. 2. **Emit level** (`errorToastUtils.ts`): `showToastOfError` used instance reference comparison (`lastToastErrorInstance === err`) to detect duplicate errors. When 5 parallel requests fail with the same `errorCode` (e.g., 40100), they create 5 different error instances, so reference comparison always returned `false` → 5 events emitted. **Abort race condition**: `AbortController.abort()` sets `signal.aborted = true` synchronously, but a 502 response already in the network stack could arrive at the Axios interceptor before the cancel rejection, triggering an error toast for an intentionally cancelled request. ## Design Decisions - **Dual-layer dedup**: Fix both emit-side (errorToastUtils) and render-side (Toast component) rather than just one, so each layer independently prevents spam - **errorCode-based dedup**: Compare `err.code` + `err.requestId` rather than just instance reference. Same `errorCode` with different `requestId` = same logical error from parallel requests → deduplicate - **signal.aborted guard**: Check `config.signal.aborted` at the top of both success and error interceptor handlers, converting to `CanceledError` which is already in the toast ignore list ## Changes Detail - `packages/components/src/actions/Toast/index.tsx` — Add early return in `toastMessage` and `toastNotification` when `handleToastId` returns `undefined` (duplicate detected) - `packages/shared/src/errors/utils/errorToastUtils.ts` — Track `lastToastErrorCode` and `lastToastRequestId`; add `isSameErrorCode` check to prevent duplicate emit for same error code from different request instances - `packages/shared/src/request/axiosInterceptor.ts` — Add `signal.aborted` guard at top of response success/error handlers; suppress auto-toast for 5xx when request was aborted ## Risk Assessment - **Risk Level**: Low - **Affected Platforms**: Extension / Mobile / Desktop / Web (all platforms) - **Risk Areas**: The Toast dedup fix is straightforward (adding a missing early return). The errorCode dedup tracks only the last error, so two genuinely different errors in sequence will both show — no risk of over-suppression. ## Test plan - [ ] Trigger parallel API failures (e.g., switch networks rapidly) and verify only one Toast appears - [ ] Verify different error codes still show separate Toasts - [ ] Abort a request mid-flight and verify no "Server Error" toast appears - [ ] Verify genuine persistent errors still show Toast after single occurrence ---

Security

  • Versions of Requests between v2.3.0 and v2.30.0 are vulnerable to potential forwarding of Proxy-Authorization headers to destination servers when following HTTPS redirects.

    When proxies are defined with user info (https://user:pass@proxy:8080), Requests will construct a Proxy-Authorization header that is attached to the request to authenticate with the proxy.

description:
Steps to reproduce:

> if you delete a contact then the ios app crashes (and will keep crashing). The issue is in CloudKitContactsDb.fetchQueueBatch which assumes that a contact exist (line 124) and if does not the db query fails and the app crashes

The problem function:

```kotlin
fun getContact(contactId: UUID): ContactInfo? {
  return database.transactionWithResult {
    queries.getContact(contactId = contactId.toString()).executeAsOneOrNull()?.let {
      val offers = it.offers.split(",").map {
        OfferTypes.Offer.decode(it)
      }.filterIsInstance<Try.Success<OfferTypes.Offer>>().map {
        it.get()
      }
      ContactInfo(contactId, it.name, it.photo_uri, it.use_offer_key, offers)
    }
  }
}
```

Even though the function signature suggests there's no problem if the contact doesn't exist, it still crashes when that's the case. My understanding is that it's due to the complex query being performed under the hood:

```
getContact:
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  photo_uri,
  use_offer_key,
  contacts.created_at,
  updated_at,
  group_concat(offer, ',') AS offers
FROM contacts AS contacts
JOIN contact_offers AS contact_offers ON contact_id = id
WHERE id = :contactId
ORDER BY contact_offers.created_at;
```

In other words, a simple query like the one below wouldn't suffer the same crash, and would just return an empty result set:

```
getContact2:
SELECT *
FROM contacts
WHERE id = :contactId;
```

So I've fixed the crash by adding an extra check to see if the contact exists before fetching it.

Note also that this crash is fixed via PR #640, because the query has been changed to the simple version above.

Fixing mimalloc memory-limit crash
description: I was testing receiving payments when Phoenix was running in the background, and noticed that it had mysteriously stopped working in recent builds. I tracked down the issue and discovered the the notification-service-extension was crashing: This issue is that Apple limits the amount of memory that a notification-service-extension is allowed to use. The memory is capped at 24 MB (for iOS 16). In the Kotlin [docs](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/native-memory-manager.html#memory-consumption), they say: > Another way to fix high memory consumption is related to [mimalloc](https://github.com/microsoft/mimalloc), the default memory allocator for many targets. It pre-allocates and holds onto the system memory to improve the allocation speed. > > To avoid that at the cost of performance, a couple of options are available: > > * Switch the memory allocator from mimalloc to the system allocator. For that, set the -Xallocator=std compilation option in your Gradle build script. > > * Since Kotlin 1.8.0-Beta, you can also instruct mimalloc to promptly release memory back to the system. It's a smaller performance cost, but it gives less definitive results. The "-Xallocator=std" option seems to do the trick, as I wasn't able to reproduce the crash with that option set. In fact, the memory is significantly lowered: I don't notice any performance degradation. In fact, fetching objects from the database actually seems faster. But I can appreciate how mimalloc theoretically increases performance. So I'd be happy to revisit this when we adopt Kotlin 1.8. Or if Apple raises the memory limits in future versions of iOS.

title: fix(wallet-connect): crash when viewing connected dapps
description:
PR #7230 moved WalletConnect files into `src/features/wallet-connect/`, preserving the existing 1100-line `index.tsx` barrel. That barrel has a circular dependency with `requestNavigationHandlers.ts`: it imports `handleWalletConnectRequest` from there, and `requestNavigationHandlers` imports `handleSessionRequestResponse` back from it. This cycle was latent before the move, but the new file paths changed Metro's module evaluation order and turned it into an actual runtime failure. Metro's CommonJS require returns a partially-evaluated exports object when it hits the cycle, so any export defined after the trigger point (line 28) resolves to `undefined` at import time. Every export in the file is defined after line 28, which means every external consumer is at risk.

The confirmed crash is on the Connected Dapps screen (`getAllActiveSessionsSync` is `undefined`), but the same pattern affects `handleSessionRequestResponse` (approving/rejecting WC signing requests), `pair` (scanning WC QR codes), `initListeners` (app startup), and others. Whether each one actually crashes depends on Metro's nondeterministic module evaluation order, so additional failures could surface at any time.

This change decomposes the barrel into focused modules organized by responsibility: `services/` for callable operations on the WC client, `handlers/` for event callbacks, `utils/` for pure functions, and `components/` for the error sheet UI helper. All external consumers now import directly from the specific file. No barrel, no cycle path, no partial evaluation risk. Circular dependency count drops from 1438 to 1430 in `check:cycles`.

Note:  the new files are pure extractions from `index.tsx` with only import paths changed. No logic was modified.
Note: this aligns with the barrel file elimination effort (FEPLAT-5) and the [RFC](https://www.notion.so/rainbowdotme/RFC-Avoid-Barrel-Files-and-index-ts-Re-exports-2e7b001b85b4810db2dbfe5ead59d739), which documents a previous production crash (APP-3394) caused by the same circular dependency pattern.

Fixes APP-3548.

title: fix(AppInstallInfo): crash when iOS sync method returns true
description:
The `AppInstallInfo#isStoreInstall()` Swift method returns `Bool`, but React Native's bridge requires synchronous methods to return an ObjC object type (`id`). The bridge calls `objc_retain` on the raw return value, and a primitive `true` (1) gets misinterpreted as a pointer to address `0x1`, causing a crash on startup. Returning `false` (0) happens to survive because nil is a safe no-op for `objc_retain`. This is why the TestFlight build works (method returns `false` there) but an App Store build (and our E2E fix in #7260 crashes tests right now) would crash (method returns `true`).

This was never caught because the `IS_DEV` guard in `env.ts` short-circuited before reaching the native call in every environment tested so far. We fix this in #7260 so we cover these cases going forward in the E2E suite. Also no compiler or linter catches this mismatch since `Bool` is a valid `@objc` return type and the RN bridge registers method names as strings without validating return types.

This change returns `NSNumber` instead of `Bool`, which is the correct type per the [React Native docs](https://reactnative.dev/docs/legacy/native-modules-ios#synchronous-methods). The JS side still receives a boolean.

Ref FEPLAT-62.

title: Fix dapp browser messaging race condition
description:
Fixes APP-####

## What changed (plus any additional context for devs)

This fixes an issue where connecting via the button in control panel doesn't work on https://bx-test-dapp.vercel.app/ when the webview is initially loaded. This causes the WalletConnect e2e test to fail.

The problem is caused by a race condition between the dapp initialization and the onLoad callback from react-native-webview. Not sure why it started manifesting a lot more recently (basically 100% repro rate), but there was definitely a potential issue.

What happens is that the dapp calls eth_accounts right away to check if it is currently connected to a wallet. The problem is that this happens before we receive the onLoad callback so we do not have a `appMessenger` created so we never send the response, causing the dapp wallet connection to be stuck in a reconnecting state. Further attempt to connect fail because it checks if the state is reconnecting already and returns.

To fix this we can instead create the instance lazily once we receive a message.

Now that zkSync Era has a full EVM compatibility layer, this PR deprecates EraVM Safe deployments (in order to reduce maintenance burden and only release a single set of contract byte code instead of two).

Note however, that [EraVM contracts cannot `DELEGATECALL` into EVM contracts](https://docs.zksync.io/zksync-protocol/evm-interpreter/overview#developer-considerations), meaning that existing EraVM Safe proxies cannot be upgraded to EVM versions. Legacy accounts should either remain on an older version of Safe (<= v1.4.1), or migrate the account to a new EVM version.

title: Improvement to Module Tests
description:
Created this PR as a prequel to the changes for FCL removal, so we keep the PRs isolated. Also, one of the tests fails, as I explain below, and I would like to know whether we should remove that CI or do something else.

## Summary

This PR addresses two pre-existing issues discovered while investigating the `test:4337:upstream` failure, and improves the local bundler infrastructure to make the e2e test suite reliable.

---

## Changes

### `fix(bundler): Handle invalid block range in geth dev mode`

The bundler pinned at `26e4f4c` (v0.7.0) has a race condition in `EventsManager`: after a bundle is mined at block N, `lastBlock` is set to N+1. If no new block exists yet when the next cron tick fires, `handlePastEvents` calls `eth_getLogs(N+1, "latest"=N)`, which geth dev mode rejects with `"invalid block range params"`. This caused the passkey `test:4337` e2e suite to fail intermittently.

The fix adds a pre-check patch to the pinned bundler that skips the log query when `lastBlock > latestBlock`. To avoid the same patch being applied to `bundler-upstream` (which uses `TAG: master` and already includes an equivalent fix natively), the patch is gated behind a new `APPLY_EVENTS_MANAGER_PATCH` build arg — set to `false` for the upstream service.

### `fix(test): Correct signature construction and gas limits in passkey user story specs`

Two user story tests were failing on `main` with `AA26 over verificationGasLimit`:

- `CreateSafeWithPasskeySignerAsOwner`: `verificationGasLimit` was `600000`, raised to `800000`
- `RotatePasskeyOwner`: `verificationGasLimit` was `100000` (far too low), raised to `500000`

`RotatePasskeyOwner` also had an incorrect signature construction: the EOA's `signSafeOp` result was being wrapped in a nested `buildSignatureBytes([{ signer, data: ... }])` call, treating the EOA signature as though it were a contract signer response. Since the EOA is a direct Safe owner executing the swap, the signature should be a flat `buildSignatureBytes([signSafeOp(...)])`.

---

~## What still fails and why~

~**`test:4337:upstream` — not fixed in this PR**~

~The upstream bundler (`master`) has moved to ERC-4337 **v0.8**, which enforces strict [ERC-7562](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7562) storage access rules during validation. The Safe 4337 module uses `DELEGATECALL` into the Safe singleton during `validateUserOp`. Under ERC-7562, storage writes made via `DELEGATECALL` are attributed to the *callee's* address (the singleton), not the proxy's. Since the singleton is unstaked, the v0.8 bundler rejects the operation with error code `-32502`:~

```
factory has forbidden write to <singleton> slot <...>
unstaked account accessed <singleton>
```

~Fixing this requires changes to the Safe 4337 module's validation architecture to comply with ERC-7562 v0.8 rules — it is not an infrastructure or test configuration problem. The `test:4337:upstream` suite runs on a cron schedule (1st and 15th of each month) rather than on every push, so this pre-existing failure does not block CI.~

~For now, should we remove this CI?~

---

## Context on why the patch is required?

At some point, a recent Geth stable release changed how `eth_getLogs` handles an invalid block range in dev mode. Older versions most likely returned an empty array silently when `fromBlock > toBlock`: which would mean the bundler just found no events and continued without error. A newer Geth version started returning `-32602 invalid block range params` explicitly instead, turning a silent no-op into a hard failure.

The underlying race condition in the bundler was always there; it just didn't surface until Geth became stricter about that edge case.

title: Add User Story for Computing Safe Address
Rework Safe Signer Launchpad
description:
This PR does a rework of some of the implementation details of the `SafeSignerLaunchpad` contract in light of some observations from the previous PR #376.

Namely, this changes the initialization process to work in a slightly different way:
1. Set the target singleton to a special slot when the entry point executes the `initCode` for the account. Safe `setup` also happens at this point, meaning that any `DELEGATECALL` to the Safe singleton should work and be valid.
2. Signature verification checks that the account is an owner. This has the side-effect that you can initialize an account with multiple custom ECDSA owners and use any of them to sign the first user operation.
3. Promote the Safe to the singleton that was previously in storage.

The main difference with the previous flow is that we no longer have two separate `setup` initializers that we `DELEGATECALL` to. Additionally, we added checks that prevent double initialization as well as reentrency issues in the execution function.

In addition, this also opens up a pretty clear path for supporting multiple owners with the launchpad as the account has already undergone "regular" Safe setup. This is relevant for #372.

Unit tests in order to reach 100% coverage will be introduced in a follow up.

title: Add NatSpec Documentation To The Safe Launchpad
description:
Related to #308

This PR adds NatSpec documentation to the `SafeSignerLaunchpad` contract for all methods. This is done in preparation for an auditing these contracts and as a precursor to getting 100% test coverage.

In writing this PR, I found some issues with the current launchpad implementation that need to be addressed pre-audit:
- We allow accounts that haven't been properly initialized, which can be a security risk. We should do checks similar to the Safe `setup` method to prevent double initialization and the validation should revert if the account is not initialized.
- We are using revert messages instead of errors.

Additionally, I would like to suggest that we change the implementation to use a **single** setup instead of doing a pre- and post- setup delegatecall. This would greatly simplify the implementation and security assumptions of the launchpad. The downside is that the setup cannot break 4337 rules, but we do not have a use-case for this, so I wouldn't implement it.

title: Safe 4337 Signer Launchpad
description:
Related to #149, follow-up to #182 This PR provides another approach to Safe initialization to accommodate for custom signers that are deployed along with the Safe. See #182 for more context. This launchpad implementation is very specific to custom signers and introduces a new `IUniqueSignerFactory` interface that must be implemented to work with it. The name “unique” signer is not great, but named this way since for a given factory and some “signer data”, a `ISignatureVerifier` implementation will correspond to a **unique** address. In the example of P-256 and WebAuthn signers, this means a P-256 public key will correspond to a unique on-chain address with an `ISignatureVerifier` implementation. This implementation works by tying the Safe address to the `signerFactory`, `signerData` and Safe `setup` parameters. This means a couple of things: 1. The Safe address is unique for a specific initial configuration (owner, singleton, fallback, modules, etc.); the same property holds for the existing `SafeProxyFactory` 2. Unlike #182, the Safe address **is not** tied to the first user operation (in fact, the user operation is signed with the same owner as the Safe will use!) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram actor B as Bundler participant E as EntryPoint participant F as SafeProxyFactory participant P as SafeProxy (Account) participant L as SafeSignerLaunchpad participant S as Safe (Singleton) participant M as Safe4337Module participant U as IUniqueSignerFactory participant A as Signer actor T as Target B ->> +E: handleOps([userOp]) E ->> +F: CALL(userOp.initCode[:20]) F ->> P: CREATE2 F ->> P: setup(initHash) P ->> L: setup(initHash) note over L: SSTORE(initHash) F -->> -E: ok E ->> +P: validateUserOp(userOp) P ->> +L: validateUserOp(userOp) note over L: require(getInitHash(userOp) == initHash) L ->> +U: isValidSignatureForSigner(operationData, signature, signerData) U -->> -L: magic L -->> -P: validationData P -->> -E: validationData E ->> +P: initializeThenUserOp
(singleton, signerFactory, signerData, ...setupParams, callData) P ->> L: initializeThenUserOp(…) note over L: SafeStorage.singleton = singleton L ->> +U: createSigner(signerData) U ->> A: CREATE2 U -->> -L: owner L ->> S: setup([owner], 1, ...setupParams) note over S: standard Safe setup L ->> P: DELEGATECALL(callData) P ->> S: DELEGATECALL(callData) S ->> M: execUserOp(…) M ->> P: executeFromModule(…) P ->> S: executeFromModule(…) S ->> T: Ether P -->> -E: ok ``` ### Implementation Notes Currently, the implementation only supports a single signer, but can be changed to support multiple (by turning `signerFactory` and `signerData` into arrays). ### Downsides The downsides of this implementation over #182 is that it is a solution _very_ specific to deploying Safes with custom signing schemes that require additional contract deployments and not a general solution to complex Safe setups in the context of ERC-4337.

title: fix(mobile): prevent crash on settings switch row tap
description:
> Tap a switch in settings,
> wrapper called undefined,
> typed union locks the door.

## What it solves

Mobile app v1.0.11 crashed on `/app-settings` with `TypeError: undefined is not a function` when users tapped a switch row (biometrics, "Allow notifications") outside of the switch knob. The renderer wrapped every non-floating-menu item in a `Pressable` with `onPress={item.onPress}`, but switch rows intentionally have no `onPress` (the `LoadableSwitch` in `rightNode` handles taps), so tapping the row chrome called `undefined` and crashed.

Datadog crash report: https://app.datadoghq.eu/error-tracking/issue/964869a6-42a4-11f1-9dc1-da7ad0900005

Resolves: [WA-2194](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2194/mobile-crash-on-app-settings-typeerror-undefined-is-not-a-function)

## How this PR fixes it

Three layers, so the same class of bug is harder to reintroduce:

1. **Renderer**: `'switch'` rows now render the same way as `'floating-menu'` (no outer `Pressable`). The interactive element lives in `rightNode`.
2. **Types**: `SettingsItem` is now a discriminated union — `'switch' | 'floating-menu'` requires `rightNode` and forbids `onPress`; `'menu' | 'external-link' | undefined` requires `onPress`. The compiler will reject any future drift.
3. **Defense-in-depth**: the renderer also falls back to a static row whenever `onPress` is missing (`'onPress' in item ? ... : undefined`), so even if the types are bypassed the runtime can't call undefined.

Why TypeScript didn't catch this originally: `onPress` was optional and `type` was a loose `string`, so a switch row with no `onPress` typechecked fine and `Pressable.onPress` accepted `undefined` without complaint.

## How to test it

1. Build mobile and open the app
2. Navigate to App settings (Settings tab → app settings)
3. Tap on the row containing the "Biometrics" or "Allow notifications" switch — specifically tap on the **label or icon area**, not the switch knob itself
4. Verify the app does not crash and the row is non-interactive (only the switch toggles)
5. Verify other rows (Currency, Address book, Clear pending transactions, About links) still navigate / fire on tap as before

## Visual summary

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Before
    A1[Tap switch row chrome] --> B1[Pressable onPress=undefined]
    B1 --> C1[💥 TypeError: undefined is not a function]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[Tap switch row chrome] --> B2{type === 'switch'?}
    B2 -->|Yes| D2[Static row, no Pressable]
    B2 -->|No| E2{onPress defined?}
    E2 -->|Yes| F2[Pressable fires onPress]
    E2 -->|No| D2
  end
```

title: fix(web): resolve spending limits race condition from feature architecture migration
description:
## What it solves

The spending limits feature migration to the feature architecture pattern (PR #7053) introduced a race condition that causes spending limits data to never load, breaking the `resetAllowance` + `setAllowance` transaction flow when editing existing limits.

resolves https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-1422/blocker-spending-limits-are-not-displayed-on-ui

## How this PR fixes it

The root cause: the new `useSpendingLimits` hook dispatched `data: []` to signal "loading started", but the `makeLoadableSlice` reducer computes `loaded: payload.data !== undefined` — so `[] !== undefined` evaluates to `true`, making the store think data is already loaded. This flipped `shouldFetch` to `false`, which changed `useAsync` deps, which cancelled the in-flight fetch via cleanup. The store deadlocked at `{ data: [], loading: true, loaded: true }`.

The fix simplifies the hook back to the pattern used by the old `useUpdateStore`: let `useAsync` manage loading state naturally (it provides `data=undefined` during loading), and dispatch the raw `[data, error, loading]` tuple to Redux unconditionally. This eliminates the two-phase dispatch, the `shouldFetch` flag, and the Safe-change detection ref — all of which `useAsync`'s dependency array already handles.

Also reverts the Cypress `enterBeneficiaryAddress` helper from the native input setter hack back to `.clear().type()`, which is the standard Cypress approach.

## How to test it

1. Run unit tests: `yarn workspace @safe-global/web test --testPathPattern='features/spending-limits/hooks/__tests__/useSpendingLimits'`
2. Verify 9 tests pass, including the race condition regression test
3. Run the regression E2E tests for spending limits:

title: Registration verification does not sufficiently ensure that attestation certificates chain to a trust anchor
description:
## Summary
`validateCertificatePath()` does not verify that an attestation's certificate chain actually terminates at a configured trust anchor. When walking the chain it stops at the first self-signed certificate it finds (which could be user-supplied), and exits early.

This happens before the configured Apple/Google/etc trust anchor (which is concatenated to the end of the chain) is reached.

A user can therefore register a credential and have the server accept it as if it were backed by a genuine Apple / Android SafetyNet / Yubikey / etc.

## Details
`packages/server/src/helpers/validateCertificatePath.ts`:

The configured trust anchor is appended to the end of the untrusted chain (line **83**):

```ts
const x5cWithTrustAnchor = x5cCertsParsed.concat([anchor]);
```

The walk then verifies each cert was signed by the next, but breaks on the first self-signed cert (lines **104–116**):

```ts
if (issuer.subject === issuer.issuer) {
  // Root cert detected, make sure it signed itself
  const issuerSignedIssuer = await issuer.verify(
    { publicKey: issuer.publicKey, signatureOnly: true },
    WebCrypto,
  );
  if (!issuerSignedIssuer) {
    throw new InvalidSubjectAndIssuer();
  }
  break;   // <-- exits before the appended trust anchor is ever checked if user supplied self-signed cert comes first
}
```

The success condition is therefore "the certs form an internally-consistent chain ending in some self-signed cert"
Rather than "the chain terminates at one of the configured trust anchors."

## Exploit shape

```
attacker sends:  x5c = [ forgedLeaf (signed by attacker root),
                         attackerSelfSignedRoot ]

library builds:  [ forgedLeaf, attackerSelfSignedRoot, <configured Apple/Google/etc root> ]

walk:  forgedLeaf -> attackerSelfSignedRoot        (verifies, attacker controls both)
       attackerSelfSignedRoot is self-signed        -> break
       attackerSelfSignedRoot -> configured root    (NEVER CHECKED)
```

`return true`. The configured anchor never gets checked.


As far as I have looked all attestation enforcement uses `validateCertificatePath` when using MDS etc.

title: fix/webauthn-abort-controller-race-condition
description:
This PR attempts to remove a race condition from browser's WebAuthnAbortService. It was discovered that multiple invocations of `startAuthentication()` in a row (especially in a SPA using clientside routing), particularly when conditional UI is started, could lead to `WebAuthnAbortService.reset()` being called early which would fail a subsequent call to `startAuthentication()` with a `DOMException` and "a request is already pending."

I determined that this was due to the call to `this.controller.abort()` not actually aborting the `navigator.credentials.get()` synchronously. We can't `await` an `AbortController.abort()` to wait for the `navigator.credentials.get()` to be aborted; we can only abort and cross our fingers that we don't call `startAuthentication()` until the WebAuthn API call actually terminates in response to the abort signal.

This can lead to `.reset()` being called by the first `startAuthentication()`'s `try / catch / finally` _after_ a subsequent call to `webauthnAbortService.createNewAbortSignal()`, which expects `this.controller` to be populated with the new controller but ends up becoming `undefined` when the `.reset()` gets called after the first controller calls `.abort()`. The second call to `startAuthentication()` can no longer be aborted, and a third call will error out because the second WebAuthn API call is indeed still pending.

See https://github.com/MasterKale/SimpleWebAuthn/issues/273#issuecomment-1257519264, I included some logging output that might make it clearer if the above description is insufficient.

The fix is to remove the `reset()` method from `WebAuthnAbortService`. In testing I observed no issues with possibly repeatedly calling `.abort()` on an already-aborted controller. Thus we can leave the service's `this.controller` populated between calls to `createNewAbortSignal()` and forget about trying to tame a race condition.

Fixes #273.

## Demonstration

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5166470/192686991-10ea47d0-8aa9-4f1f-bb52-03d6ee3326a0.mov

title: Modified package published to npm, containing malware that exfiltrates private key material
description:
Earlier today, a publish-access account was compromised for `@solana/web3.js`, a JavaScript library that is commonly used by Solana dapps. This allowed an attacker to publish unauthorized and malicious packages that were modified, allowing them to steal private key material and drain funds from dapps, like bots, that handle private keys directly. This issue should not affect non-custodial wallets, as they generally do not expose private keys during transactions. This is not an issue with the Solana protocol itself, but with a specific JavaScript client library and only appears to affect projects that directly handle private keys and that updated within the window of 3:20pm UTC and 8:25pm UTC on Tuesday, December 3, 2024.

These two unauthorized versions (1.95.6 and 1.95.7) were caught within hours and have since been unpublished.

We are asking all Solana app developers to upgrade to version 1.95.8. Developers pinned to `latest` should also upgrade to 1.95.8.

Developers that suspect they might be compromised should rotate any suspect authority keys, including multisigs, program authorities, server keypairs, and so on.

title: fix(scodes): update SCodes to get a crash fix on Windows
description:
Fixes #21034

## Summary

This PR updates the StatusQ SCodes dependency to include a fix for a Windows crash in the **Log in by syncing** flow.

## Problem

On Windows, repeatedly entering and exiting the syncing QR flow (Continue -> Back -> Continue) could trigger an access violation during QML teardown.  
WinDbg stacks consistently pointed to `Qt6Core!QThread::terminate` in the scanner teardown path.

## Root Cause

The QR scanner worker thread in SCodes (`SBarcodeScanner`) used a Windows-specific forced thread stop (`terminate()`) in the destructor.  
During rapid view teardown/recreation, this could race with in-flight decode work and posted Qt events, causing invalid access.

## Fix

The SCodes scanner shutdown was hardened to use an orderly teardown sequence instead of forced termination:

- stop scanning and prevent new frame processing
- disconnect frame delivery
- stop/detach camera and capture session
- queue a blocking barrier on the decoder thread to drain already-queued work
- call `quit()` + `wait()` for clean thread shutdown

Also included small safety guards to avoid processing/logging against a cleared camera during teardown.

## Dependency Update

StatusQ now pins [SCodes](https://github.com/status-im/SCodes/pull/4) to:

`2b46818ff46fd43f443ed80a056c01abcf927526`

in CMakeLists.txt.
