Simplify function type signatures (#198)
description:
* Simplify function type signatures

The type signatures of many public functions were complex and
misleading. This was primarily due to the widespread use of the types
`TypedData` and `TypedMessage<T>`, which where inappropriate in most of
the places they were used.

The `TypedMessage<T>` type is used by the `signTypedData` function when
the version is 'V3' or 'V4'. All references to this type outside of V3
and V4 of `signTypedData` have been removed. This also resulted in the
`T` generic parameter being removed from many functions.

The `TypedData` type didn't represent the actual type signature of any
function, yet it was used to represent the input data for most
functions. In most cases we had no specific expectations for the input
type, so `unknown` is now used instead. In the case of `V1` of
`signTypedData`, the expected type was always `EIP712TypedData[]`. The
`TypedData` type has been reduced to just that one case where it was
useful and accurate.

* Rename `TypedData` to `TypedDataV1` and add docs

The `TypedData` type has been renamed to `TypedDataV1` to indicate that
this type is only intended to represent the data being signed with `V1`
of `signTypedData`.

JSDoc documentation has been added for the two message types,
`SignTypedDataV1Data` and `TypedMessage`.

title: Consolidate the data encoding for `signTypedData` V3 and V4 (#197)
description:
The encoding logic for `signTypedData` was nearly identical between V3
and V4, but each version was a completely separate implementation. This
complicated my efforts to replace `ethereumjs-abi`. The logic for each
version has been consolidated into one function.

The main differences are:
* `undefined` values are skipped in V3.
* `undefined` values are encoded as zero on V4 for custom types, but
  they throw an error for non-custom types.
* `null` types are encoded as zero on V4 for custom types, but are the
  same between versions for non-custom types.
* V3 does not support arrays.

* fix(evm,vm): correct EIP-7928/EIP-8037 gas accounting for static CREATE

Make the 10 previously-failing Amsterdam v7.3.0 blockchain fixtures pass
(eip7928_block_level_access_lists, eip8037_state_creation_gas_cost_increase)
with no regressions across the v730 fixture set.

- Defer the CREATE/CREATE2 static-context check into create7928Gas so it
  fires AFTER the new-account state-gas pre-charge, matching the EELS
  amsterdam (tests-bal) reference. On the resulting exceptional halt the
  per-frame state-gas snapshot refills the pre-charged
  STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT * CPSB to the parent reservoir, lowering the
  transaction's cumulative receipt gas by that amount.
- Track the gas burned by a static CREATE/CREATE2 trap in
  EVM.exceptionalHaltRegularPenaltyGas and exclude it from the block-level
  regular-gas dimension in runTx. The reference reserves the (never-entered)
  child create frame's gas before raising WriteInStaticContext, so that gas
  is not counted in execution_regular_gas_used even though the sender still
  pays it via tx_gas_used. This is specific to CREATE/CREATE2; SSTORE,
  CALL-with-value and SELFDESTRUCT static traps still count their burned gas.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* revert(evm,vm): drop non-spec CREATE/CREATE2 static-trap carve-out

Remove the EVM.exceptionalHaltRegularPenaltyGas mechanism that excluded a
static CREATE/CREATE2 trap's burned gas from the block-level regular-gas
dimension. That carve-out was not derivable from EIP-8037 and existed
solely to satisfy the v7.3.0 `bal_create_in_static_context` fixture, whose
asserted block header gas_used (97,920) is mathematically impossible under
the EIP-8037 formula `gas_used = max(block_regular, block_state)` (for a
single-tx block that implies gas_used >= cumulativeGasUsed/2 = 471,574).

The client now follows the canonical EIP. The four divergent
`test_bal_create_in_static_context` cases are skipped via SKIP_FIXTURES in
executionSpecBlockchain.test.ts wit

title: tx: Fix EIP-155 transaction encoding on chain ID 0
description:
When preparing Ethereum data for RLP encoding, you must convert all values to either byte arrays or lists.  Scalar values (positive integers) are converted to byte arrays by using the fewest bytes possible to represent the value in big endian format.  The canonical form of any scalar value prepped for RLP encoding is that any leading `0` bytes stripped.  In the case of `0`, this means that the only byte (`0x00`) is stripped and you are left with an empty array.

Most of the values in this code are properly 0-stripped using `bigIntToUnpaddedBuffer`.  Unfortunately, it appears that the `chainId` was added without stripping leading zeros.  In most cases this doesn't matter, but if someone is running a chainId 0 blockchain and they want to EIP-155 encode their transaction, the previous code would result in an invalid transaction because only the canonical form is allowed.

This change fixes this bug and correctly prepares the chainId in EIP-155 transactions for RLP encoding.

description:
[v5.8.0] This is a security update for the **legacy** Ethers v5 branch, addressing two security fixes.

- A bug in `elliptic`, which **does not affect ethers** but triggers a *critical security warning* during `nom audit` [see: [missing signature length check](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f7q4-pwc6-w24p), [missing check for leading bit](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-977x-g7h5-7qgw), [allow BER-encoded signatures](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-49q7-c7j4-3p7m), [false negative verification](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fc9h-whq2-v747), [signing malformed input](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-434g-2637-qmqr)]
- A bug in `ws` which can be used as DoS vector when communicating with malicious WebSocket service providers, triggering a *high security warning* during `nom audit` [see: [too many HTTP headers](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3h5v-q93c-6h6q)]

For those that wish to audit the specific changes in the the bundled version between v5.7 and v5.8, see [this gist](https://gist.github.com/ricmoo/05da10dd949940614d5ba506617bca42).

title: Replace 24h absolute auto-lock with configurable idle timer (#2802)
description:
* Replace 24h absolute auto-lock with configurable idle timer

Replaces the hardcoded 24-hour 'session length' alarm with a pure
idle-based auto-lock timer. The browser session locks after a
configurable number of minutes of user inactivity (1, 5, 15, 30, 60),
defaulting to 15. Genuine user interaction in any extension page pings
the background via a new USER_ACTIVITY message, which rearms the alarm.

- @shared/constants/autoLock.ts: single source of truth for valid
  timeouts, default, and coercion helpers.
- SessionTimer: rewritten as a class that reads the persisted timeout
  on every reset; same-name browser.alarms.create atomically replaces
  the in-flight deadline.
- saveSettings: validates and persists the new field; when the new
  timeout is shorter than the elapsed idle time on an unlocked wallet,
  locks immediately rather than scheduling an alarm in the past.
- userActivity handler: gated by isFromExtensionPage in
  popupMessageListener so dApp content scripts cannot extend a session.
  Rejects pings when the wallet is locked.
- useActivityPing + ActivityTracker: mousedown/keydown/touchstart/wheel
  listeners on window with 5s leading-edge throttle; only active when
  the wallet is unlocked.
- Preferences UI: dropdown driven by VALID_AUTO_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MINUTES.
- Tests cover SessionTimer, userActivity, save/load validation, and
  the elapsed-idle short-circuit; mock fixtures updated to include
  the new field.

Closes #2082

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

title: Throw FetchError with HTTP status from fetchJson (#2748)
description:
* Throw FetchError with HTTP status from fetchJson

`fetch.ts` was throwing `new Error(res.statusText)` on non-2xx responses.
Over HTTP/2 (Cloudflare and most modern backends), `statusText` is empty
in Chrome, so every `fetchJson` failure surfaced as `Error` with no
message. Sentry groups by stack-trace fingerprint, so distinct failure
modes (rate-limit 429, bad request 400, header bloat 431, etc.) all
collapsed into a single issue ("No error message" — FREIGHTER-DMQ).

Replace the bare throw with a `FetchError` subclass that includes the
status code (and optionally response body, capped at 200 chars) in the
message. This:

- restores grouping fidelity in Sentry — separate issues per status code
- preserves the original status/body on the error object for callers
  that want to inspect them
- keeps the existing catch + setError UX unchanged

Verified against `useScanTx`'s catch path in `blockaid.ts`, which
re-throws via `Sentry.captureException(err instanceof Error ? err : ...)`
— a `FetchError` is an `Error`, so capture behavior is unchanged but
event messages are now informative.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address review: structured FetchError, Sentry plumbing, broader cleanup

Review on the initial commit (#2748) flagged adjacent error-reporting
gaps in the same surface. This addresses them in one shot:

- `FetchError` now carries url (sanitized — query string dropped),
  method, and a `kind` discriminator (`http-error` | `non-json`).
  Stable, status-coded message format for Sentry grouping.
- Non-JSON content-type branch throws `FetchError` too (was the
  inverse grouping bug — body interpolated into `error.message`,
  fragmenting Sentry on every Cloudflare interstitial).
- New `captureFetchError` helper unpacks `FetchError` into Sentry
  tags (`http.status`, `http.method`, `http.kind`) and a `setContext`
  block, so the new fields are filterable. Routing the body through
  `setContext` also runs Sentry's data scrub

title: rename sign_transaction->user_sign_transaction, add service_sign_transaction stub
description:
Prior to the experimental PSBT signing interface, 'sign_transaction'
implied signing the users inputs with the users keys, while
'send_transaction' implicitly signed the servers side for multisig.

Going forward we wish to be able to:

- Sign the users inputs with multiple devices/mnemonics (e.g. recovery
keys for 2of3 subaccounts, multiple signers for generic multisig, and
private keys in sweep txs that can be merged with normal txs)
- Sign externally held keys with multiple services (likely pluggable,
initially just the Green backend and external to gdk signers via PSBT)
- Choose which inputs to sign in a tx

As a first step, split the session level interface into user and service
signing.

title: sign_tx: remove the bespoke signing path for sweep transactions
description:
Handle sweep inputs in transactions to be signed by pre-signing them up
front with the provided private key, then marking them to be skipped by
the regular user/backend signing machinery using skip_signing=true.

This has 2 benefits: Firstly, we eliminate the bespoke signing path for
sign_ga_transaction(), which had unused and incomplete logic for setting
signatures into the tx.

Secondly, sweep UTXOs can now be freely mixed into regular transactions,
allowing for spending them as part of a normal payment (optionally with
other wallet UTXOs provided) rather than having to sweep them into the
wallet first.

This first cut is a minimal changeset designed to make reviewing easier.

title: create_tx: remove old_used_utxos, rename signing_inputs->transaction_inputs
description:
Also, for sweeping, restore the private key before returning the signed
tx to the caller, so the caller can determine which inputs are from a
sweep.

With these changes, all tx creation flows now result in the complete set
of inputs being placed in "used_utxos". This corresponds to the
behaviour of the "transaction_outputs" element, and removes the need for
callers to look outside of these 2 elements for details on the
txin/txouts. It also means that the tx creation result much more closely
approximates the structure of PSBT now.

Since the inputs are collated by create_transaction, there is no longer
any need for get_ga_signing_inputs() to do so, and the inputs for signing
can be used directly in HWWI's "required_data/transaction_inputs"
(renamed from "signing_inputs").

As a result, we simplify the places where we previously had to account for
both old and new used utxos.

Finally, make some minor comment/documentation fixes.

of execution regardless of whether keys are external or internal.

This initial change implements just enough of the HW interface for login
to succeed using the internal software interface. This requires some
restructuring including:

- Deriving the software signer from the hardware signer class
- Moving the responsibility of holding the mnemonic into the signer
- Implementing an auth_handler wrapper to automatically advance the

title: sign: allow caller-provided anti-exfil host entropy
description:
Allow callers to provide their own host entropy. This allows for example
using a deterministic scheme to generate the entropy and thereby verify
anti-exfil signatures across multiple devices at any point in time. It
further allows testing of the anti-exfil signing paths and (by copying
out the host entropy for re-signing) to ensure that on signing failures
re-signing uses the same entropy to differentiate transient signing failures
from malicious behaviour.

title: watch only: share entropy calculation, mix server entropy into the local cache key
description:
Sharing the entropy calculation speeds up watch only login, while using
the server provided entropy prevents attackers with acces to the local
cache file from brute forcing username and password guesses offline.

title: blob: unify rich watch only blobserver credential handling
description:
RWO blobserver credentials now consist of username/password/watch_only_data,
with the latter being encrypted to the username and password so they can
be stored.

Note we maintain username and password instead of just encrypting with a
password because a password alone is unlikely to have sufficient entropy
to protect the local watch only data from offline attack.

title: watch only: simplify enabling/disabling watch only
description:
Creating watch only sessions is disallowed on the server during 2fa
reset, so catch that case client side. Also avoid the expensive entropy
derivation when we are disabling an existing watch only session.

title: psbt: add signatures when creating psbt from json.
psbt: use PSBT-provided user signatures if present
description:
In the event that an input is already user signed, this will carry the
user signature through and prevent re-signing of the input.

Note that PSBT inputs are currently finalized even if only user (and
not server) signed; this will be fixed in an upcoming change.

title: psbt: add signatures from signing to the PSBT instead of directly finalizing
description:
Once all signatures (and scripts) have been added, finalize all inputs that
we have a full set of signatures for.

This allows multisig inputs that have only been user-signed to remain
un-finalized after signing, compared to the previous behaviour of
finalizing the input with a dummy (invalid) server signature. This in
turn allows server-only signing of the inputs at a later time.

PSBTs with user-signed inputs can now also be server-signed without the
user having to re-sign (i.e. re-user-sign) the input at the same time,
which is undesirable and impossible/impractical in some scenarios such
as offline signing.

This also ensures that all finalization of PSBTs is performed using the
same wally finalization logic rather than bespoke handling.

Previously, PSBT signing did not require a correctly populated PSBT in
order to sign, in that the inputs scripts could be missing. We now
populate the scripts when signing so that external finalization of
non-finalized inputs can be performed outside of gdk if desired.

title: tx: estimate using low-s signatures for non-grinding signers.
description:
When a signer does not produce Low-R signatures (for example, HWW using
Anti-Exfil), the signature produced must still be Low-S, in order to
satisfy standardness rules. Thus we should produce our dummy script
and estimate the fee based on a signature 1 byte shorter than the DER
maximum which is High-R, High-S.

Update the code to do this, and rename the input script functions for
clarity.

title: script: further improve fee estimation for non-low-r signers
description:
Previously the code assumed the green backend signature had the same
low-R status as the users signer. In fact the backend always produces
low-R, low-S signatures in order to reduce on-chain usage and user fees.

Clean up the code around dummy scripts and witnesses slightly, with the
aim of fully encapsulating it in due course.

title: taproot: support signing non-wallet inputs
description:
Taproot signatures commit to the scriptpubkeys of all inputs in the
transaction, compared to segwit/pre-segwit which only commit to the
script of the input being signed.

So, for non-wallet or "skip_signing"=true inputs in a tx that we are
taproot signing, we need to provide the scriptpubkey.

Allow providing it in the UTXOs/tx inputs as "scriptpubkey", and
populate this for PSBT signing (where we have already ensured that
the inputs UTXO is populated). Since singlesig still doesn't cache
looked up txs, this avoids a network roundtrip for each such input.

If the caller doesn't provide it, then fetch the UTXO and grab the
scriptpubkey from it instead.

title: psbt: make the converted tx hex more accurate to the sign_transaction flow
description:
PSBT signing works by converting the PSBT into tx JSON compatible with
sign_transaction. Make sure that we:

- Retain any existing finalized inputs signatures and scriptsig in the tx hex
- Add a dummy scriptsig and witness to wallet inputs in the tx hex if needed
- Correctly mark expired inputs in the tx JSON to sign them with only the user key
- Only provide the redeem script for segwit-ness checking for non-wallet inputs

This ensures that the fee/fee rate reported by GA_psbt_get_details is
more accurate, and that the signing flow (a) has signatures to evaluate to
determine if the tx is already signed and (b) can sign expired CSV
outputs from PSBTs.

Note at this stage we don't yet set and restore any actual signatures in
the PSBT, so GA_psbt_sign does not yet gain support for the re-signing or
split user-then-server signing flows now allowed without 2fa by sign_transaction.

title: tx: use DER encoded signatures to pass around sig + sighash bytes

title: psbt: expose get_signatures_from_input

title: tx: expose scriptsig and witness computation for re-use

by [webauthn.Config.validate] to
[protocol.TopOriginExplicitVerificationMode]; the strictest active
mode, which accepts a Top Origin only if it matches an entry in
[webauthn.Config.RPTopOrigins]. The opt-out mode
protocol.TopOriginIgnoreVerificationMode has been removed entirely;
[protocol.CollectedClientData.Verify] returns an "unknown Top Origin
verification mode" error if it is ever encountered.

Together these changes align the library with the W3C WebAuthn Level 3
guidance that Cross-Origin embedding and Top Origin acceptance should
be explicit relying-party decisions rather than defaults.

BREAKING CHANGE: The Cross-Origin verification semantics have changed
significantly due to the stabilization of the WebAuthn Level 3
specification. It is no longer possible to disable verification, and
Cross-Origin ceremonies must explicitly be allowed in this release.

- protocol.TopOriginIgnoreVerificationMode has been removed. Code that
  referenced it must switch to one of the other constants as there is
  no longer a mode which disables the Top Origin verification such as:
    - TopOriginExplicitVerificationMode; match against RPTopOrigins only
      (recommended, and the new coerced default)
    - TopOriginAutoVerificationMode; match against the union of
      RPTopOrigins and RPOrigins
    - TopOriginImplicitVerificationMode; match against RPOrigins only

- webauthn.Config.validate now rewrites a zero-valued
  RPTopOriginVerificationMode to TopOriginExplicitVerificationMode.
  Integrators that left the field unset previously got ignore-mode
  semantics (any Top Origin accepted); they now get strict matching
  against RPTopOrigins and must populate th

title: feat(protocol): validate native app origins (#468)
description:
This enables matching native application origins using simple string comparison. Effective web origins are still matched using case-insensitive matches provided they are valid web origins per HTML5 Section 5.3 (https://www.w3.org/TR/2011/WD-html5-20110525/origin-0.html) and/or simple string comparison per RFC3986 Section 6.2.1 (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-6.2.1). It is important to note that this function completely ignores Apple Associated Domains entirely as Apple is using an unassigned Well-Known URI in breech of Well-Known Uniform Resource Identifiers Section 3 (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8615#section-3).

Closes #462, Closes #463

title: fix(protocol): validate packed attca country (#656)

title: fix(webauthncose): validate keys earlier (#615)

title: fix(webauthn): skip mds validation for none format (#497)
description:
* fix(webauthn): skip mds validation for none format

The attestation format none does not include attestation data and therefore cannot be validated against MDS3 metadata. Previously the login flow attempted to validate it, which caused unnecessary failures for authenticators using the none format. This change ensures that none is explicitly exempt from MDS3 validation, allowing logins with such authenticators to succeed as expected. The registration flow already implements this measure.

Fixes #387

This allows both validating a discoverable credential and deterministically finding the user in question. This is effectively missing tooling making it more difficult for people to perform this specific action.

title: fix(webauthn): empty aaguid fails login (#398)

title: fix: validate configuration on all begin methods (#125)
description: This adjusts the BeginLogin, BeginDiscoverableLogin, and BeginRegistration methods to invoke the Config.validate() function ensuring implementers who create a new Config manually still go through the validation process. This has potential to be a breaking change as validation can no longer be skipped but it's preferable that we account for those specific use cases in our validations. This allows us to make it easy to ensure deprecated options to be properly remapped.

title: fix(protocol): attestation type attca not validated correctly (#153)
description:
For purposes of determining if an authenticator has produced a full attestation when the MDS entry for the authenticator indicates cannot produce a full attestation, treat attca and basic_full both as full attestation types. Add test data with an authenticator aaguid that only has attca type. Make production metadata available for use in tests.

Fixes #149

title: fix!: split attestation type and format (#658)
description:
The Credential.AttestationType field previously stored the attestation
statement format identifier (e.g. "packed") rather than the attestation
type conveyed by the authenticator (e.g. "basic_full"). This corrects
the semantics and adds a dedicated AttestationFormat field for the
format. The same split is applied to protocol.CredentialDescriptor and
is populated automatically by Credential.Descriptor().

A custom Credential.UnmarshalJSON migrates records written by prior
releases: when attestationType holds a known format identifier and
attestationFormat is absent, the value is moved to AttestationFormat
and AttestationType is cleared so the true type can be re-derived via
Credential.Verify.

Fixes #476

BREAKING CHANGE: An bug with the Credential Record which was
introduced early in the libraries lifecycle has resulted in a
breaking change to the Credential struct. If you are manually
serializing this struct instead of using encoding/json you
will be required to make manual changes; though Integrators
should consider these notes regardless.

- protocol.CredentialTypeFIDOU2F has been removed;
replace uses with protocol.AttestationFormatFIDOUniversalSecondFactor
(cast to string where the destination field is a plain string).

- The semantics of the AttestationType field on webauthn.Credential
  and protocol.CredentialDescriptor have changed. Integrators that
  inspect this field to detect a format (typically checking for
  "fido-u2f") must switch to the new AttestationFormat field; the
  FIDO-U2F AppID and AppIDExclude extension helpers now key on
  AttestationFormat, so a descriptor literal constructed with
  AttestationType: "fido-u2f" will no longer trigger them.

- Stored Credential JSON records are migrated transparently by the
  new UnmarshalJSON, but re-marshaled records will carry
  attestationFormat rather than a format string in attestationType;
  downstream consumers that parsed the legacy shape directly should
  be updated.

title: fix(metadata): prevent panic corrupt blob (#698)

caused an index out of range or type assertion panic instead of a parse
error. Guard the chain before use and return a descriptive error.

libs shipped with each app version. There is no scenario where a new
client parses old-format output or vice versa. The hex→Base64 encoding
change is therefore a seamless, non-breaking upgrade for imToken users.

the hash internally before signing, the ETH sign message interface
cannot produce valid BTC message signatures.

- Add explicit note that ETH Applet reuse is not viable
- Confirm BIP-137/Standard for imKey requires Bitcoin Applet upgrade
- Add launch strategy section with two options (phased vs unified)
- Recommend phased approach (Phase 1 without Applet dependency)

title: input: release touch handles before deleting the i2c bus
description:
Since ESP-IDF v5.5 (espressif/esp-idf@e73d78ba) i2c_del_master_bus()
refuses to delete a bus that still has devices attached and returns
ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE. The touchscreen task registers a panel IO
device on the bus but never releases it, so under IDF 5.5.4 the first
touchscreen_deinit() fails and aborts via ESP_ERROR_CHECK.

On boards that panic with PRINT_HALT, such as the Waveshare S3 Touch
LCD 2, this freezes the device on the boot splash screen while
gathering camera entropy, and also hangs the QR scanner and the
camera exit path, since the touchscreen is restarted around every
camera start/stop (see #306).

Releasing the touch handle and the panel IO device (which removes it
from the bus) before deleting the bus restores the deinit/init cycle,
and also fixes a heap leak present under IDF 5.4 where both handles
leaked on every cycle.

jadepy: do not use the legacy flow for non-AE signing
description:
Prior to this change, requesting non-AE signing would use the legacy
flow which is deprecated. We now instead use the AE flow without
opting-in to AE signatures, and return the results in the format that
the legacy flow did (i.e. just the signatures with no signer commitments).

This change is API compatible(*), and means that jadepy users will no
longer use the legacy flow which will facilitate its removal in the future.

However, we still need to be able to test the legacy flow until its
removal. Add a 'use_legacy' parameter to enable this specifically for
test_jade.py to use.

(*) There is a small difference: if legacy signing was used, AE host
data could previously be passed and would be ignored - this is now an
error. If a caller is affected it can only mean either (a) they
intended to use AE signing but are not, or (b) they are not validating
the resulting AE signatures (because they are not receiving signer
commitments). Both need to be fixed by the caller, and this is
unavoidable if we wish to make Schnorr AE signing available later.

omitted and inferred. Note that it is also possible to explicitly sign such
inputs with SIGHASH_ALL too.

implemented, now that we detect them.

title: qrmode: fix potential memory leak in psbt failure case
descriptor: fix small memory leak when registering descriptor wallet

sign_tx: split out updating output info from validating it
description:
Removes some confusion from having validation change the data, but
primarily this will allow psbt signing to share the output validation
code without using the commitment update code (since pset commitments
are validated already during parsing and not passed separately like the
sign_tx case).

title: sign_tx/sign_psbt: share code to validate supported sighash flags
sign_tx: move output/commitment validation into its own function
sign_psbt: use shared signing tx validation code
description:
This means we don't have to find the fee ourselves, and ensures that
the checks we perform (e.g. duplicate fees) are consistent whether we
are signing a tx or psbt.

title: sign_tx: remove blind proofs from commitment data
description:
As with the asset and value commitments, these are not required once the
commitment data has been validated.

Re-order the commitment struct members to further lower the memory size
required to hold commitments.

title: sign_tx: call summary update/validate unconditionally
description:
This makes the calling sites simpler, and fixes a bug where validation
would be skipped if only one of input/output summary arrays was given.
Note it is currently valid (and seems reasonable to allow) passing only
one of the arrays for standard payments.

title: sign_tx: Strengthen liquid commitment checks against the tx being signed
description:
This change ensures that the transaction and any commitment values
match, if an asset/value commitment pair are given.

Commitments given as part of tx input data must have these fields, while
they are optional (and should be discouraged) for tx outputs.

We move the validation checking which was spread over several unrelated
areas into the function fetching the commitment data. This ensures that
when fetching it, it is either fully validated from that point on or an
error is returned.

Following this we remove the commitment fields from the commitment_t struct
since they are now redundant for the remainder of sign_tx processing.

From experience debugging tests where the commitments mismatched, the
old error messages were not helpful. Update these to include 'trusted
commitment' in all messages to make it clearer when a mismatch is
detected.

Note This commit is deliberately minimal to make the core logic changes
easier to review.

description:
When the user already has sufficient ERC20 allowance, Skip returns
required_erc20_approvals as an empty array. amountConfig.getTx() still
attaches it as metadata on the unsigned tx (apps/hooks-internal/src/

v5 serialize() rejects the unknown key with "invalid object key -
requiredErc20Approvals", failing the bridge broadcast.

The follow-up sendEthereumTx (after the approval onFulfill) already
strips the field via `delete tx.requiredErc20Approvals`. Apply the
same strip earlier so the no-approval branch is also safe. The
existing strip below becomes idempotent.

title: @metamask/key-tree 3.0 (#25)
description:
This PR attempts to refashion this package from an experimental key derivation module into something that we and our users can trust in production. This is accomplished by (1) adding numerous reference implementation tests (see `test/reference-implementations.test.ts`) and (2) adding new abstractions over our low-level key derivation functions. 

(2) is accomplished by the addition of two new classes, `BIP44Node` and `BIP44CoinTypeNode`, and associated utility functions. The API isn't perfect, but it's extremely easy to use on the address key derivation end, i.e. by our users. See the updated README and unit tests for details. Unit test coverage is at 100%.

This PR will be followed up by an ESLint update to add JSDoc linting, as well as release automation actions and completing repository standardization.

title: Allow zero private key for `ed25519`
description:
`0x000...000` is a valid private key for `ed25519` (since all private keys are valid). Previously we would always reject this private key, due to the function used to validate bytes. I've updated it to use the curve function to check if a private key is valid.

Related to MM-02-007.

title: Validate tweak passed to `privateAdd`
description:
If the tweak equals zero, the generated child private key is the same as the parent private key. We have to validate that it has at least one non-zero byte.

Related to MM-02-002.

title: Validate that master private key and seed are within bounds
description:
This validates that:

- The master private key is greater than zero and less than the order of the curve.
- The seed is within 16 and 64 bytes, as per the BIP-32 specification.

Related to MM-02-003 and MM-02-004.

title: Add extended public (`xpub`) and private (`xprv`) keys

Closes #44.

This PR adds a getter to the `BIP44Node` class to get an extended public or private key, and expands the `fromExtendedKey` function to make it possible to create a node from a stringified extended public or private key.

To make this possible, two new fields are introduced in `SLIP10Node`, `index` and `parentFingerprint`. These are part of the extended keys, so need to be kept track of. Additionally, to reduce complexity in the derivation code, all derivation functions now retur

title: Add support for public key derivation
description:
Closes #46.

Additional to adding support for public key derivation, I changed the signatures for some functions to use objects, rather than tuples or parameters. This prevents situations where we need to pass `undefined` in place for a private key, for example.

title: Add convenience methods for public keys and addresses
description:
~~Needs to be rebased after #43 is merged.~~ Done.

This PR adds convenience methods to get the (Ethereum) address and public key from an HD node.

**Why use a function instead of a getter?**
The method for deriving a public key from a private key can be async (in the case of `ed25519` for example), so it had to be an async function.

Closes #45.

title: Add `fromSeed` function to `SLIP10Node`, `BIP44Node`, `BIP44CoinTypeNode`
description:
This adds a new function to initialise a `key-tree` node from a BIP-39 seed. This can be used to skip the step from mnemonic phrase to seed, and can improve performance if the seed is already available.

This function is only supported for `secp256k1` and `ed25519` for now. `ed25519Bip32` may be added in the future.

Closes https://github.com/MetaMask/key-tree/issues/210

title: Fix multipath RegEx
description:
This updates the multipath validation to allow for a broader range of sub-paths, and adds unit tests for the input validation. Paths starting with `bip32` segments will still require a `parentKey` to be specified, and paths starting with `bip39` will still require that **no** `parentKey` is specified. Paths longer than 5 `bip32` segments will not be accepted, because [BIP-44](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0044.mediawiki) only defines paths of length 5, excluding the seed.

description: Fixes a bug in input validation where BIP-39 seed phrases could contain non-lowercase letters.

title: Accept BIP-39 mnemonic phrase as Uint8Array
description:
This adds support for passing mnemonic phrases as `Uint8Array`, in all places where we accept them. The expected format is the same as the format we use in `@metamask/scure-bip39`.

The derivation path can now look like `[new Uint8Array(), 'bip32:...', ...]`. Only the first BIP-39 segment can be a `Uint8Array`, it's not supported for BIP-32 segments.

Closes #106.

title: Validate CIP-3 master node entropy size

This means that you can now use something like `["slip10:44'", "slip10:60'", /* ... */]` as derivation path, as well as the current `bip32:` derivation paths. This simplifies the BIP-32 derivation logic, and separates SLIP-10 and BIP-32 specific logic to a separate file.

While BIP-32 and SLIP-10 are mostly the same, there are some subtle differences. Projects that require full compatibility with one or the ot

title: Add extended key property to `SLIP10Node`

I've also updated `SLIP10Node.fromExtendedKey` to accept a serialised extended key, instead of an options object.

Depends on #124.

title: Restore compatibility with QR Keyring (#252)
description:
The `KeyringController` method `addNewKeyring` was changed in v11 to
initialize the keyring options to an empty object. These options are
passed to the `deserialize` method of the keyring. This broke
compatibility with the QR keyring because its `deserialize` method does
not expect to be passed an empty object.

The `KeyringController` has been updated to no longer initialize the
`addNewKeyring` options to an empty object. It should now work the same
as it did prior to v11. The one functional difference is that it now
throws an error when `addNewKeyring` is used to add a simple keyring
without supplying any private keys, however that path would have
already thrown an error.

Zcash requires 256-bit seed entropy to avoid the seed becoming a
security bottleneck, potentially enabling multi-target attacks below
2^125 operations. (The same argument applies to BIP 32-like hierarchical
key derivation in general —preserving full entropy in the chain code
and public key at any tree node requires 256 bits to start with— but
for other coins this has not been a specified requirement, or depended
on in their security analysis.)

SLIP 39 requires all implementations to support both 128-bit and 256-bit
master secrets, so compliant software should accept 33-word shares.

- Add IsZcashSupportedForCurrentMnemonic() to centralize entropy check
- Use conditional checks in both CYPHERPUNK_VERSION and WEB3_VERSION
  (home widget, connect wallet coin list, public key derivation in
  AccountPublicSavePublicInfo and TempAccountPublicInfo)
- Call SetupZcashCache and SetupZcashSFP in CreateNewSlip39Account for
  supported wallets
- Update Rust error messages to describe the actual requirement
- Show notice in asset manager when 20-word shares lack Zcash support
- Fix bug in AccountPublicHomeCoinGet where the "manage" JSON key was
  omitted (rather than set to false) for Zcash when the mnemonic type
  was not BIP 39

title: fix(zcash): sign shielded PCZTs without RoleSigner to fit the device stack
description:
The cypherpunk shielded PCZT signing path used the upstream pczt RoleSigner,
which reconstructs a full TransactionData for every bundle just to compute the
32-byte ZIP-244 sighash. That setup alone needs ~61 KB of stack, well over the
26 KB UiDisplayTask budget, so signing an Orchard->Ironwood migration batch
overflowed the task stack and the device reset into firmware verification.

Replace RoleSigner with the lean signer used before Ironwood: low_level_signer
driven in place, with the sighash computed by the in-repo byte-level
pczt_ext::shielded_sig_commitment instead of a TransactionData rebuild. Extend
that hasher to the v6 (NU6.3) Orchard and Ironwood commitment domains so it
stays correct for migration transactions. This restores the pre-Ironwood
signing footprint (~45 KB on host, the same as the path that already signs
shielded Orchard on shipping Keystones) while supporting Ironwood.

pczt_ext (zcash_vendor):
- digest_orchard_v6 / digest_ironwood_v6 and a v6 branch in
  shielded_sig_commitment: v6 bundle personalizations, anchor omitted from the
  effects digest, the 5-node to_hash_v6 layout.
- sign_ironwood driver mirroring sign_orchard; a shared sign_orchard_action
  that defers the sign/skip decision to the signer (wallet-controlled
  zero-value spends are still signed; tx_modifiable is cleared only when a new
  signature is added).

app_zcash:
- A lean SeedSigner (PcztSigner) deriving keys and signing actions in place,
  preserving the strict per-action validation from the removed collect path
  (ZIP 32 derivation shape, dummy_sk rules, already-signed skip, per-account
  key cache, PcztNoMyInputs).
- validate_supported_pczt rejects v6 PCZTs carrying a Sapling spend: the lean
  hasher implements the Orchard/Ironwood v6 domains but not the v6 Sapling-spend
  domain (distinct noncompact personalization, anchor omitted). Keystone never
  signs Sapling spends; Sapling outputs are version-independent and remain
  supported.

Oracle tests assert the lean sighas

title: Fix multiple vulnerabilities
fix: Validate Exchange address_parameters before dereferencing
description:
handle_check_address() read params->address_parameters[0] without
first checking that the pointer was non-NULL or that
address_parameters_length covered at least the length byte. The
function is reachable only from the Exchange app via os_lib_call(),
so this isn't exploitable from a host APDU today, but the contract
between the two libraries lives across a trust boundary and would
silently OOB-read on any future caller that wires up the same
interface less carefully.

Reject params->address_parameters == NULL and
address_parameters_length < 1 early so the function is safe
regardless of who calls it.

title: fix: Zeroize ETH2 BLS12-381 private scalar on every exit path
description:
get_eth2_public_key() derived an EIP-2333 BLS12-381 private scalar
into the stack buffer privateKeyData but never erased it before
returning. The neighboring locals (tmp, privateKey) were explicitly
scrubbed in the end: cleanup block, which indicates the omission was
accidental.

On embedded targets, residual stack contents can persist across calls
and become recoverable through later memory-disclosure bugs, crash
dumps, or forensic extraction. Exposure of validator private keys can
lead to unauthorized signing or loss of staking/account control.

Add explicit_bzero(privateKeyData, sizeof(privateKeyData)) to the
existing cleanup block.

title: fix: Require user confirmation for P2_SHARED_SECRET privacy export
description:
INS_PERFORM_PRIVACY_OPERATION (0x18) accepted P1_NON_CONFIRM for both
the public encryption key (P2=0x00) and the shared secret (P2=0x01).
The shared secret is computed via X25519 from the device-derived
private key and an attacker-supplied Curve25519 public key, so it is
secret material that should never leave the device without the user
physically approving the action. The non-confirm path turned the device
into a silent ECDH oracle reachable by any host that could send APDUs.

Reject P2_SHARED_SECRET + P1_NON_CONFIRM with
SWO_CONDITIONS_NOT_SATISFIED. The P2_PUBLIC_ENCRYPTION_KEY path keeps
its existing non-confirm semantics — that operation only exposes a
public key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: fix: Make HAVE_CHALLENGE_NO_CHECK builds noisy at compile time

the rolling challenge with a hardcoded constant and (b) skip the
verification of host-supplied challenges. The flag is meant for test
runs, but nothing in the source surfaced its presence to a release
build — a stray CHALLENGE_NO_CHECK=1 in a Makefile invocation would
ship a binary that accepts arbitrary challenge values without any
trace in the build log.

Emit a `#warning` whenever the macro is defined, so the build log
shows the bypass and CI can grep for it before promoting an artifact
to release.

test(unit): Pin ledger_pki signature-check dispatcher (CWE-347)
description:
check_signature_with_pubkey at src/ledger_pki.c is THE crypto gate
behind every host-supplied descriptor that affects what the user
sees on screen: trusted-name resolution, proxy-info, safe-account,
plugin registrations, gating payloads, network metadata,
tx-simulation. A silent regression here is CWE-347 (improper
signature verification) -- fake "vitalik.eth", fake "Uniswap V3"
plugin name, fake risk score reaches the user.

The function is a thin dispatcher on the SDK lib_pki's
check_signature_with_pki status_t, with a legacy ECDSA fallback
when no certificate is loaded:

  PKI_SUCCESS                   -> true   (short-circuit)
  PKI_MISSING_CERTIFICATE       \  cx_ecfp_init_public_key_no_throw
  PKI_WRONG_CERTIFICATE_USAGE   /  + cx_ecdsa_verify_no_throw
  PKI_WRONG_CERTIFICATE_CURVE   -> false  (no legacy fallback)
  PKI_WRONG_SIGNATURE           -> false  (no legacy fallback)
  default                       -> false  (fail closed)

Eight tests pin every status_t branch plus the two sub-failures of
the legacy fallback (key init fails, ecdsa verify fails). The SDK
lib_pki/ledger_pki.c is NOT linked into the test target -- we
provide check_signature_with_pki, cx_ecfp_init_public_key_no_throw
and cx_ecdsa_verify_no_throw locally so cmocka's mock() drives the
outcome per case. cmocka also asserts that the legacy path is NOT
entered on SUCCESS / WRONG_CURVE / WRONG_SIGNATURE / default --
leaving will_return queues empty for those tests is the safety
net.

Coverage: src/ledger_pki.c 0% -> 100% of 23 lines.

title: fix: Propagate hash_filtering_path() failures instead of swallowing them
description:
The 11 EIP-712 filter command handlers (calldata value/callee/chain-
id/selector/amount/spender, plus the various other filter kinds)
called hash_filtering_path() purely for its side effect on the
signature-verification hash and ignored its bool return. When the
helper bails on path_get_nth_field()/ui_712_get_discarded_path()
returning NULL, the hash context is left mid-update; the subsequent
sig_verif_end() then verifies an incomplete hash against the host-
supplied signature. The downstream signature check still catches the
mismatch in practice, so this isn't a bypass, but it produces a
generic "signature failed" error several lines later instead of
identifying the actual problem.

Wrap each call site in `if (!hash_filtering_path(...)) return false;`
so the failure is surfaced at the point where the inconsistency
appears.

test(unit): Pin SET_EXTERNAL_PLUGIN handler
description:
SET_EXTERNAL_PLUGIN registers a (contract, selector) tuple as
handled by a named external plugin so the device can route
subsequent calldata-bearing transactions to the right plugin
binary. The host-supplied payload is signed by a Ledger PKI key.
A bug here lets an attacker pair an attacker-controlled plugin
name with a victim contract address, hijacking how the user sees
subsequent dApp interactions.

Pin:
 - the empty-plugin-name reject (defence in depth on top of the
   PKI signature -- a backend should never sign an empty name but
   the device enforces the bound itself rather than trusting the
   backend invariant),
 - dataLength <= payload_size rejected (no room for signature),
 - name_len that would overrun the pluginName slot rejected,
 - check_signature_with_pubkey failure keeps pluginType = NONE,
 - the happy path writes (name, address, selector) into
   dataContext.tokenContext, sets pluginType = EXTERNAL, and
 - binds pluginChainId to PLUGIN_CHAIN_ID_ANY (intentional: the
   external-plugin descriptor is chain-unbound, see the in-source
   comment about the CWE-345 follow-up tracked separately).

The TRY/CATCH path that fires when os_lib_call THROWs (plugin not
present -> SWO_FILE_NOT_FOUND + pluginName cleared) is not
exercised here. Driving a real longjmp through the SDK try-context
chain would require reproducing struct try_context_s faithfully;
the same accepted limitation applies to test_cmd_set_plugin.

Coverage of cmd_set_external_plugin.c rises from 0% to 90.9% of
33 lines (the THROW branch accounts for the remaining 9%).

title: fix: Reject typed-transaction chain IDs longer than 64 bits
description:
process_chain_id() accepted chainId fields up to INT256_LENGTH (32
bytes) for EIP-2930 / EIP-1559 / EIP-7702 transactions, but downstream
get_tx_chain_id() converts the stored value to uint64_t via
u64_from_BE() which silently consumes only the first 8 bytes. The
signature hash still covers the full original encoding, so a malicious
host could craft a transaction whose signature applies to one chain
while the device displays / validates only the truncated 64-bit prefix.

Restrict the field length validation to sizeof(uint64_t). Any chain ID
that does not fit in a uint64_t is now rejected at the parser level
rather than being truncated, keeping the UI / network selection / chain
consistency checks aligned with what gets signed.

title: fix: Reject pre-EIP-155 legacy transactions to prevent cross-chain replay
description:
The legacy signing path accepted transactions that omit the EIP-155
chain_id encoding (vLength == 0) and produced a signature with the
legacy v base 27/28. Such signatures are not domain-separated by chain
and can be replayed on any EVM-compatible chain that still accepts
unprotected legacy transactions. The existing chain-consistency check
in finalize_parsing_helper only enforced strict matching for non-mainnet
app configurations, so on Ethereum mainnet the replayable mode was
never rejected.

Reject any LEGACY transaction whose RLP V field is empty, regardless of
app configuration. EIP-155 has been mandatory for safe replay protection
since 2016, and no current ragger tests rely on the unprotected form.

description:
Three TLV-use-case dispatchers share the same handle_xxx(p1, lc, data)
shape: forward to tlv_from_apdu() with the FIRST_CHUNK bit, and on the
callback path run handle_xxx_tlv_payload + verify_xxx_struct. The
inner TLV parsers + signature verifiers are pinned by test_proxy_info /
test_trusted_name / test_enum_value; these three new test files cover
only the APDU framing.

Pin per file (8 tests each):

  - p1 == P1_FIRST_CHUNK forwards first_chunk=true to tlv_from_apdu
  - p1 != P1_FIRST_CHUNK forwards first_chunk=false
  - TLV_APDU_ERROR   -> SWO_INCORRECT_DATA  (+ proxy_cleanup() for proxy)
  - TLV_APDU_PENDING -> SWO_SUCCESS (more chunks expected, no cleanup)
  - TLV_APDU_SUCCESS -> SWO_SUCCESS
  - inner callback: payload-parse failure short-circuits BEFORE verify
  - inner callback: verify failure also yields false
  - inner callback: happy path -- both succeed

cmd_trusted_name additionally pins a CWE-294 invariant:
roll_challenge() MUST burn the per-session nonce after verify
regardless of outcome -- otherwise an attacker could brute-force
signatures against a stable challenge. The matching test fails if
a future refactor short-circuits roll_challenge on verify-failure.

tlv_from_apdu / handle_xxx_tlv_payload / verify_xxx_struct /
proxy_cleanup / roll_challenge are linker-wrapped per target;
cmocka's mock() drives each leaf outcome. The wrap can optionally
invoke the callback (g_invoke_handler toggle) so tests can exercise
the inner static handle_tlv_payload or stay at the outer dispatcher.

Coverage:
  src/features/provide_proxy_info/cmd_proxy_info.c     0% -> 100% (14 lines)
  src/features/provide_trusted_name/cmd_trusted_name.c 0% -> 100% (13 lines)
  src/features/provide_enum_value/cmd_enum_value.c     0% -> 100% (13 lines)

title: fix: Reject empty plugin name in handle_set_external_plugin
description:
handle_set_external_plugin() trusted the host-supplied length byte
end-to-end: a zero-length name passed every existing check, the
SHA-256 hash was computed over an empty name prefix, and only the
Ledger PKI signature verification stood between the request and a
plugin registration with pluginName = "". The downstream alias
matching uses strcmp() against entries like "-erc20", so an empty
alias would never match any internal plugin and the registration
would be inert — but the device would still have stored a useless
plugin context and surfaced a stale name on subsequent screens.

Reject pluginNameLength == 0 explicitly before any further work.
This is defense in depth against a backend that signs a malformed
payload, not a bypass of the PKI gate.

title: fix: Drop misleading `const` on TLV-populated descriptor fields
description:
safe_descriptor_t::address and four gating_t fields (hash_selector,
intro_msg, tiny_url, address) were declared `const` to document that
they should not change after parsing, but the TLV handlers wrote
into them through `(uint8_t *)` / `(char *)` casts that strip the
qualifier. The underlying storage comes from APP_MEM_CALLOC() so
this is not strict undefined behaviour, but it is a pattern several
static analyzers flag and it weakens the type signal at every read
site.

Remove the `const` from the five fields and drop the corresponding
casts at the parser call sites where they were stripping the
qualifier. The two remaining `(uint8_t *)` casts on `char` fields
stay since they still perform a char->uint8_t conversion required by
the TLV helper signatures.

title: fix: Lock EIP-712 type system at FILT_ACTIVATE to prevent post-hash schema injection
description:
handle_eip712_filtering() under P2_FILT_ACTIVATE computes the schema
hash that downstream filter signatures are issued against, but left
the EIP-712 type system unlocked: the host could continue sending
INS_EIP712_STRUCT_DEF APDUs after the activate, append fields or
even entire structs to the schema, and then sign a typed message
whose actual schema differs from the one the filter metadata was
issued for.

Compute the schema hash first, and only on success switch the UI
into filtering-full mode and set struct_state to DEFINED so
subsequent handle_eip712_struct_def() calls are refused by the
existing gate at commands_712.c:94. The whole branch is inside the
`!N_storage.verbose_eip712` check (verbose mode never computes the
hash). All three state changes (hash, filtering mode, type-system
lock) move together, so a transient compute_schema_hash() failure
leaves the handle clean and the host can retry the activate.

title: fix: Rotate challenge after Safe account descriptor processing
description:
handle_safe_tlv_payload() and handle_signer_tlv_payload() verify the
signed CHALLENGE field of their respective descriptors but never call
roll_challenge() afterwards. The global challenge issued by
INS_GET_CHALLENGE stayed valid until the next explicit GET_CHALLENGE,
so any previously captured signed Safe / Signer descriptor could be
replayed within the same app session and the device would display
stale signer / threshold information as freshly authorized.

Roll the challenge at the end of both TLV payload handlers, on both
success and failure, mirroring the pattern already used by the trusted
name and proxy info flows.

title: fix: Bound MAP_ENTRY descriptor list to prevent memory pool DoS
description:
verify_map_entry_struct() appended every validly-signed map entry to
g_map_entry_list without bound. The list is cleared on
reset_app_context() between transactions, so the growth isn't
permanent, but a host with N legitimately-signed descriptors can call
INS_PROVIDE_MAP_ENTRY repeatedly during a single signing flow and
exhaust the shared app-memory pool, denying allocation to other
features (trusted_name, enum_value, safe_account, gating, GCS).

Cap the list at MAX_MAP_ENTRIES (32). 32 distinct
(chain, contract, selector, id, key) tuples is well above realistic
per-transaction clear-signing needs while keeping the worst-case
footprint around ~3.5 KB.

This only addresses the DoS component of the finding. Replay
protection (binding the descriptor to a per-session challenge in its
signed TLV) requires a backend payload change and is left out of
scope.

title: fix: EIP-7702 authorization signing state confusion / hidden BIP32 path swap
description:
The EIP-7702 authorization handler kept no signing state. handle_sign_
eip7702_authorization() accepted a new P1_FIRST_CHUNK at any time and
immediately overwrote tmpCtx.authSigningContext7702.bip32 before the
TLV payload was complete. Because tlv_from_apdu() returns success for
buffered partial payloads, a hostile host could start a second
authorization mid-review, swap the BIP32 path, and have auth_7702_ok_cb
sign the displayed authorization hash with a different derivation path
than the one shown on screen.

Introduce a dedicated APP_STATE_SIGNING_EIP7702 and gate the handler
on it: refuse P1_FIRST_CHUNK unless idle, refuse continuation chunks
without an active session, and clear the state on error or on
approval (auth_7702_cancel_cb already resets via send_status).

fix: Release EIP-712 type dependency list on every type_hash exit path
description:
type_hash() allocated a sorted dependency list via
get_struct_dependencies() to enumerate the structs that need to be
hashed alongside the root type. The list was only freed at the very
end of the happy path: any early return after the allocation -
including a partial population on get_struct_dependencies() failure
- skipped the flist_clear() and leaked nodes into the shared
app-memory pool for the rest of the session.

Restructure with a single `end:` label that runs flist_clear()
unconditionally. The two pre-allocation early returns (missing
struct lookup, keccak init failure) keep their direct returns since
no list exists yet.

title: fix: Memory leak of g_tx_hash_ctx on aborted signing flows
description:
handle_first_sign_chunk() allocates the global keccak context
g_tx_hash_ctx via APP_MEM_CALLOC and only the success path
(finalize_parsing_helper) and a subset of post-init parsing errors
(handle_sign:180) release it. Other early-error returns inside
handle_first_sign_chunk (init_tx failure, invalid data offset,
unsupported tx type, cx_hash_no_throw failure) propagate the SW
directly to handle_sign and out to main.c without freeing the
allocation. Likewise, reset_app_context() never released the context,
so app_quit() and the implicit reset at the top of
handle_first_sign_chunk left previous-session allocations dangling. A
host repeatedly triggering aborted INS_SIGN first-chunk APDUs could
exhaust the device's app heap.

Add a NULL-checked APP_MEM_FREE_AND_NULL of g_tx_hash_ctx to
reset_app_context(). Errors that bubble out of handle_sign reach
main.c with reset=true, which now centrally releases the context. The
existing late-error free in handle_sign is kept as defense in depth;
the NULL check makes the double path safe.

title: fix: Validate P1/P2 explicitly in INS_PROVIDE_MAP_ENTRY handler

handle_map_entry() compared P1 to P1_FIRST_CHUNK to decide whether
to reset the TLV state, but any other P1 value silently fell into
the "following chunk" branch — including reserved/unknown values
that should be rejected. P2 was explicitly discarded via `(void)
p2;` and any non-zero P2 was accepted as well.

Reject P1 values that are neither P1_FIRST_CHUNK nor
P1_FOLLOWING_CHUNK, and reject any non-zero P2. Returns
SWO_WRONG_P1_P2 in both cases, matching the convention used by the
other multi-chunk handlers (privacy_operation, sign_tx,
safe_account, eth2_withdrawal_index, network_icon).

title: test(unit): Cover tx_ctx.c (current-context lifecycle + validate hash)

into the freshly-pushed node.

- Getters on an empty list return NULL / 0 / false.

fix: Scrub X25519 shared secret from global RAM after privacy op
description:
handle_perform_privacy_operation() stores the derived X25519 shared
secret in tmpCtx.publicKeyContext.publicKey and, on the confirmation
path, copies a hex view of the secret into strings.common.fullAmount
for UI rendering. Neither global was scrubbed before returning:
set_result_perform_privacy_operation() only copied the secret into the
APDU reply buffer, successful synchronous APDUs were not followed by
reset_app_context(), and reset_app_context() itself did not clear the
strings buffer.

As a result, the last derived shared secret could remain resident in
RAM across later APDU exchanges, where a memory-disclosure bug, crash
dump, fault injection, or forensic extraction could recover it.

Two changes, kept together so the residue is closed end-to-end:

  * logic_perform_privacy_operation.c: scrub tmpCtx.publicKeyContext
    immediately after the secret has been copied to G_io_tx_buffer.
  * main.c: zero the whole strings struct in reset_app_context() so
    any UI-formatted view of secrets (and other transient strings)
    does not persist across resets.

into the APDU buffer and is not guaranteed to be 2-byte aligned,

risks a bus fault depending on incoming chunk boundaries.

endian decode and works regardless of alignment, removing both the

title: fix: Iterate the internal plugin table by length instead of a phantom sentinel
description:
The PLUGIN_TYPE_OLD_INTERNAL branch of eth_plugin_call() walked
INTERNAL_ETH_PLUGINS with an open-ended `for (i = 0;; i++)` loop and
broke out when `alias[0] == 0`. The array initializer never emits a
zero-byte sentinel — its last entry is "-eip7251" — so the only way
the break could fire was the loop reading past the end of the array
into adjacent .rodata and happening to land on a zero byte. Any
non-zero byte in that adjacent memory turns the loop into an out-of-
bounds dereference and an attempt to call PIC() on garbage.

Bound the loop by ARRAYLEN(INTERNAL_ETH_PLUGINS) so iteration stays
inside the table regardless of how its initializer is extended.

title: fix(desktop): prevent DISABLE_TRANSACTION_BROADCAST env leak between e2e tests
description:
The 'without broadcast' e2e suites (swap, delegate, earn, earn v2, send-to-ENS)
mutated the shared, per-worker process.env.DISABLE_TRANSACTION_BROADCAST in
beforeAll/afterAll. Because Playwright reuses workers and reschedules retries,
these mutations leaked into unrelated tests (e.g. Send) running later in the same
worker, launching the app with transaction broadcast unexpectedly disabled (and
corrupting direct process.env reads such as subAccount).

Scope the broadcast override to each suite via the app-only 'env' fixture instead
of mutating process.env, so no test can pollute another.

title: fix(e2e): fix mobile swap deeplink leak from account-selection drawer

openViaDeeplink's internal wait required the wallet-api-webview to be ~75%
visible right after opening the deeplink. For scenarios with an ambiguous
fromToken/toToken, a native "Select account" drawer legitimately covers the

Relax the check to existence-only (checkVisibility: false); every caller
already asserts visibility itself afterward (expectSwapLiveApp/Form, drawer
handling), so this only needs to confirm the deeplink was delivered.

title: feat(wallet-cli): NTTVS-406 ring destroy handles non-destructive deactivation
description:
Adapt `ring destroy` to the per-application close introduced in #18568. It now
calls destroyApplication directly (dropping the redundant restoreTrustchain
round-trip, since it resolves the trustchain itself and is idempotent on an
already-closed stream) and treats a caught TrustchainEjected as "this member is
no longer on the ring" (removed by another owner, or the trustchain destroyed
remotely) — the remote is already gone, so it proceeds to the local credential
wipe instead of aborting as a transient network failure. The outcome is
reported via a memberEjected flag (member_ejected in JSON), guarded by
remoteSucceeded so a failed teardown never reports it.

`ring encrypt`/`ring decrypt` (loadDomainKey) now rethrow a closed-stream
TrustchainEjected as actionable guidance pointing at the ring destroy + init
recovery path, preserving the original error as `cause`.

title: fix(coin-cosmos): make cryptoFactory resilient to uninitialized coinConfig
description:
Background
----------
The lazy require() registry PR replaced eager barrel-file imports with a
Map<family, CoinModuleLoader>. Family setups (setup.ts) now load on first call
to getCurrencyBridge() / loadSetupForFamily(). Previously, barrel files imported
setup.ts eagerly at module-parse time, so createBridges() — which calls
cosmosCoinConfig.setCoinConfig(getCurrencyConfig) — always ran before any
component rendered.

The bug
-------
cryptoFactory() in chain/chain.ts is imported directly by the Delegation UI
component (Delegation/index.tsx:127) and called unconditionally on every render:

    const crypto = cryptoFactory(account.currency.id);

cryptoFactory() calls cosmosCoinConfig.getCoinConfig(currencyId) on line 93.
buildCoinConfig() (from @ledgerhq/coin-module-framework) throws MissingCoinConfig
when getCoinConfig() is called before setCoinConfig() has been invoked. After the
lazy registry change, setCoinConfig() is only called when setup.ts loads (i.e.,
when getCurrencyBridge("cosmos") is triggered by a bridge/sync operation).

If the Delegation component renders before any bridge operation runs — for
example, when a user opens the app with cosmos accounts already in persisted
storage and the account page renders from cache before any sync starts —
cryptoFactory() throws, crashing the page.

Secondary caching bug
---------------------
The previous code cached cosmosChainParams[currencyId] (the chain instance)
BEFORE applying coinConfig. When getCoinConfig() threw:
  1. The cache entry was set to `new Cosmos()` (in the switch)
  2. getCoinConfig() threw and the function propagated the error
  3. On the next call, `!cosmosChainParams[currencyId]` was false (cache hit)
  4. getCoinConfig() was NEVER retried, even after setup.ts loaded later

This meant coinConfig enrichment (e.g. remote-config overrides for gas prices,
unbonding period, etc.) would be permanently skipped for currencies first
accessed before bridge setup.

The fix
-------
Use a local `chain` variab

title: fix(coin-evm): drop non-value-transferring internals and dedup root traces in getBlock
description:
`getBlock` was surfacing every EVM frame reported by Blockscout (and
Etherscan-like explorers) as an independent native operation, which caused
two kinds of double-counting:

1. The explorer's first internal transaction for each tx is the root call,
   with `from`/`to`/`value` identical to the coin tx itself. Merging it
   naively emitted the same native transfer twice.
2. `delegatecall`, `staticcall`, and `callcode` frames inherit `msg.value`
   from their enclosing frame but do not move native ETH. Blockscout still
   reports a non-zero `value` on those frames, so they were being converted
   into native operations on top of the root-trace duplicate — up to three
   identical OUTs for a single proxy-contract interaction.

Downstream, indexers like A4 add operations to compute balances, so these
duplicates drove balances negative (BACK-11037 on Somnia).

Fix is a layered defence:

- Semantic filter in `internalTxsToOperationsByHash` (Etherscan/Blockscout)
  and `traceBlockItemsToOperationsByHash` (RPC `trace_block`) drops frames
  whose `callType` (Blockscout) / `type` (Etherscan) matches the set of
  non-value-transferring call types. `EtherscanInternalTransaction` gains a
  `callType?` field since Blockscout exposes it separately from `type`.
- Structural dedup in `mergeInternalTransactions` via a new
  `dropRootTraceDuplicates` helper: any internal native op whose
  `(address, peer, amount)` tuple matches one of the coin tx's own native
  ops is dropped. Acts as a safety net for future explorer variants that
  surface the root call in a shape the adapters don't anticipate.

Unit tests cover both filters independently (parametric tests for each
non-value-transferring call type in both adapters) and the end-to-end
`getBlock` path (root-trace duplicate dropped, nested subcalls kept).

title: tools(valground): refine leak detection and tidy summary output
description:
The memory-profiling parser raised false leaks and printed noisy summaries when
an app reset its heap in bulk via mem_utils_reset_app_heap() (logged as "init").
This reworks how those boundaries are handled:

- Reset-reclaimed vs genuine leaks: an "init" reclaims the whole heap, so
  allocations still live at that point were effectively freed. Such leaks are
  now a yellow warning (non-fatal) when the reset happens *within the same
  test*, and only count as a real leak (red, fail) at the final summary or when
  a *new test* had to reset the heap to reclaim them -- i.e. the previous test
  never cleaned up. The distinction is driven by a reclaimed_by_reset flag on
  Memory.summary(), computed from whether test_name changed at the "init".
  Free errors (free without malloc / double free) still fail unconditionally.

- Print the test name once per test: a test can span several Memory segments
  (each in-test/post-test heap reset starts a new one). A Memory.printed_test_name
  class attribute tracks the last printed name so the header is shown only on the
  test's first content-bearing segment, instead of being repeated on -- or
  detached onto -- the empty segments left by resets.

- Drop the leading blank-line separator for segments that have nothing to show
  in quiet mode, so the empty reset segments no longer pile up blank lines.

- Ignore failed allocations: an out-of-memory alloc may be logged with address
  0x0; it is not a live allocation and has nothing to free, so skip it to avoid
  a phantom leak.

Peak/overtime statistics are unchanged.

title: zcash_transparent: reject zero threshold in zip48 FullViewingKey::standard
description:
`FullViewingKey::standard` validated that `threshold <= key_info.len()`
but not that `threshold >= 1`. Because `key_info` is `NonEmpty`,
`key_info.len()` is always >= 1, so the existing
`usize::from(threshold) > key_info.len()` check can never reject
`threshold == 0`. A zero threshold produces a 0-of-N P2SH multisig
redeem script (`OP_0 ... OP_CHECKMULTISIG`), which is anyone-can-spend:
funds sent to the resulting address can be swept by the first observer.

No current caller feeds a user-controlled threshold into this function
(the only non-test caller hardcodes `threshold = 2`), so this is a
defense-in-depth fix for the recently-added ZIP 48 multisig public API
rather than a live vulnerability.

seed and ZIP 32 account index actually reproduce the unified full
viewing key recorded for the account; a derivation record inconsistent
with the recorded key is now rejected rather than silently importing an
account for a different key.

title: zcash_client_sqlite: Add feature-gated ZeWIF wallet import (accounts)
description:
Add a `zewif` feature exposing `zewif::import_wallet`, which populates a
WalletDb from a ZeWIF (Zcash Wallet Interchange Format) document. All
spending key material carried by a document is delivered to a
caller-provided SecretSink for persistence outside the wallet database
(e.g. in zallet's age-encrypted keystore); the wallet database receives
only viewing keys and public metadata.

Accounts whose recorded key source names a seed present in the
document's secret store are imported with import_account_hd, preserving
the recorded ZIP 32 account index (and zcashd legacy address index,
where applicable) after verifying the seed material against its
recorded fingerprint. Other accounts are imported from their viewing
keys, as spending accounts when corresponding spending material was
delivered to the sink and as view-only accounts otherwise. Account
birthdays are built from the prior-block tree-state frontiers carried
by the document (including the Ironwood frontier); documents without
tree state fall back to the recorded birthday height, and accounts
with no birthday information scan from Sapling activation so that no
history can be missed.

Sprout accounts and address-book entries are not representable in this
crate's schema; they are recorded in the import report and their data
remains with the caller. The feature enables `zcash_keys/unstable` for
UnifiedFullViewingKey::from_sapling_extended_full_viewing_key, which is
needed to import standalone Sapling viewing keys.

The zewif crate is pulled in via a git patch until its first crates.io
release; supply-chain policy marks it audit-as-crates-io = false, with
exemptions recorded for its minicbor dependencies.

title: zcash_pool_migration: end-to-end chain-simulation proving test
description:
Add a full chain-simulation test that proves a migration against a real,
scanned wallet commitment tree instead of a hand-seeded one. Over an in-memory
zcash_client_sqlite WalletDb driven by the zcash_client_backend testing
framework (with NU6.3 active), it funds an account, commits a migration through
the WalletMigration adapter, then for real: proves each preparation transaction
against the wallet's Orchard tree, extracts it, mines it, and scans it so its
minted funding notes become genuine received notes; advances the chain until
each transfer's drawn boundary checkpoint is settled (staying within the
wallet's checkpoint-pruning window); proves each transfer; and extracts every
transaction, checking the Orchard and Ironwood proofs verify (preparations
extract Orchard-only, transfers carry both bundles).

Because the transfer spends the exact note its preparation minted, the prover's
wallet-resolved position lookup only succeeds if the scanned note's nullifier
matches the transfer spend's, so a green run confirms the whole prove/mine/scan
loop end to end. The harness supplies a small DataStoreFactory and TestCache
(zcash_client_sqlite's own are pub(crate)); it is gated on wallet plus
test-dependencies and adds the test-only dependencies it needs.

title: Stamp ZIP 32 derivation on migration builders' wallet-controlled spends
description:
build_prep_tx and build_transfer_pczt do not go through
create_pczt_from_proposal, so the fix that stamped ZIP 32 derivation on
wallet-controlled zero-value spends did not reach them. A preparation
transaction pairs one such spend with every internal change output (the
post-NU6.3 vanilla-Orchard-pool cross-address rule precludes the
random-keyed dummies used for padding, so these are spent with the
account's own key), and both builders leave their real spends unstamped
too. A Signer matching by derivation path skips all of them as "not
ours", nothing else can sign them, and extraction fails with a missing
spend-auth signature. This is reachable: the engine's Signing::External
path hands these very PCZTs to an outside signer.

Stamp in finalize_pczt, which both builders funnel through, using the
same predicate as create_pczt_from_proposal: after IO finalization, set
the derivation on every action whose spend still lacks spend_auth_sig,
in both the Orchard and Ironwood bundles. That covers the real spends
and the wallet-controlled zero-value spends while excluding the padding
dummies the IO Finalizer has already signed.

The derivation crosses the API as a new AccountDerivation, holding only
the seed fingerprint and account index; the builders compose the
m/32'/coin_type'/account' path from their own consensus parameters, so a
caller cannot address a migration to the wrong coin type. The migration
crate keeps its own type rather than taking zcash_client_backend's, which
would pull the wallet layer into the backend-agnostic core that
MigrationCrypto exists to keep at arm's length; a From conversion behind
the `wallet` feature bridges the two.

MigrationCrypto gains a required account_derivation method, threaded to
all three build sites. It is required rather than defaulting to Ok(None)
so an implementor cannot silently reintroduce the bug.

title: zcash_client_sqlite: infer ZeWIF address exposure from the gap window
description:
Addresses review feedback on #2666.

An address recorded without an exposure height is no longer classified by an
ad-hoc set of transaction recipients collected during `import_transactions`.
Instead `mark_addresses_exposed` reads the wallet's own exposure state, which
`import_transactions` has already updated (via `update_gap_limits`) for every
address the document's transactions show to have been used on-chain — receive
addresses and wallet-owned change addresses alike.

On top of that, exposure is now inferred down the gap window: transparent
addresses are handed out in child index order, so an address that the document
exposes at a higher child index under the same account and key scope implies
that every lower index was handed out before it. Such an address is marked
exposed at the lowest height at which any higher index is known to have been
exposed, which is an upper bound on its own exposure height. Leaving those
indices unexposed would strand them inside the gap window.

Only the exposures the document accounts for imply exposure below them. Account
import exposes each account's default address, which sits at whatever child
index the account's default unified address diversifier happens to select (index
8 for the test seed); treating that as evidence of sequential hand-out would
mark the seven indices below it exposed and recreate the gap exhaustion this
change set exists to fix. The exposure state is therefore snapshotted before the
document is applied, and pre-existing exposures are excluded from the inference.
