description:
## **Description**

Reverts #33304 (`ci: cache eslint and tsc results between ci runs`) and
#33327 (`fix(ci): use content-based eslint cache strategy for reliable
CI hits`).

Those PRs persisted `.eslintcache` across CI runs via `actions/cache`
and switched ESLint to `--cache-strategy content` so the cache would
actually be reused (previously it was a no-op in CI, since nothing
restored it between fresh checkouts). It worked as intended and cut
`yarn lint` from ~13 min to ~2-3 min on cache hits.

However, per the [typescript-eslint
FAQ](https://typescript-eslint.io/troubleshooting/faqs/eslint/#can-i-use-eslints---cache-with-typescript-eslint),
ESLint's `--cache` is not recommended with typescript-eslint: it
invalidates per-file based on that file's own content/mtime, with no
awareness of cross-file dependencies. Any rule that checks relationships
across files (this repo has several active `eslint-plugin-import-x`
rules — `no-unresolved`, `no-extraneous-dependencies`,
`no-restricted-paths`, `no-duplicates` — plus a narrow set of type-aware
rules scoped to `app/**/*-method-action-types*.ts`) can produce stale
results once caching is actually effective: a false negative if a
dependency's change should now cause an unchanged file to fail, or a
false positive if a previously-real cross-file error was fixed elsewhere
but the cached, unchanged file still replays the old failure.

Before #33304/#33327, this repo's CI never persisted the cache, so it
never hit this failure mode in CI (it just wasted a fraction of a second
writing a cache nobody read). Making the cache actually effective is
what turns this from a dormant, documented ESLint limitation into a live
risk. Given this is a security-sensitive wallet app, reverting to the
safe (if slower) from-scratch lint in CI until we can revisit with a
caching approach that doesn't carry this risk (e.g. a cache scoped only
to non-cross-file rules, or none at all).

title: fix(confirmations): ignore injected Permit2 value sibling in revoke detection (#32758)
description:
## **Description**

Fixes a confirmation-UI spoofing issue in Permit2 typed-data signing.

**Reason for the change:** When rendering a Permit2
`PermitBatch`/`PermitSingle` signature request, three rendering hooks
read `message.value` directly from the raw wire payload and treated
`value === '0'` (or `=== 0`) as a "revoke". Because a canonical Permit2
`PermitBatch`/`PermitSingle` has no top-level `value` field in its
EIP-712 type schema, a malicious dapp could inject a `value: "0"`
sibling that survives `JSON.parse` but is stripped from the signed
digest during EIP-712 type-walk. This flipped the confirmation title to
"Remove permission" and the estimated-changes section to "Revoke" while
the user actually signed a max-allowance (`uint160.max`) grant, and
could also suppress address trust-signal (Blockaid) alerts.

**Solution:** Revoke detection is centralized in a new `isPermitRevoke`
helper (`utils/signature.ts`) that only honors the zero-`value` branch
when `value` is a **declared field** of the message's primary type
(checked against the EIP-712 `types` schema). Undeclared sibling keys
are ignored. The three affected call sites now delegate to it:

- `components/title/title.tsx` — main confirmation title
- `.../simulation/typed-sign-permit/typed-sign-permit.tsx` — Estimated
changes section
- `hooks/alerts/useAddressTrustSignalAlerts.ts` — trust-signal alert
suppression

Legitimate signatures are unaffected: EIP-2612 `Permit` declares
`value`, so a genuine `value: 0` still renders as a revoke; DAI revoke
detection (via `allowed`) is unchanged. This is a UI-only change — the
signed digest is byte-identical to baseline.

field in a Permit2 signature request could display a "Remove permission"
screen while granting a token allowance.

description:
## **Description**

This PR implements Polymarket CLOB v2 support for MetaMask Predict (7.74
target), introducing a clean coexistence architecture that keeps v1
working while v2 is toggled on via `predictClobV2`. During the temporary
CLOB host migration window, a companion rollout flag
(`predictClobV2UseLegacyClobHost`) can force v2 traffic onto the legacy
host for internal RC testing without turning v2 on for everyone by
default.

The implementation is designed with deletion in mind — after the v1/v2
coexistence window, v1 can be cleanly removed with minimal surgery. The
work follows the "data-first protocol definition" architecture from the
internal plan: a private `protocol/` module owns all version-specific
differences and is resolved once at the provider entry point.
Lower-level helpers never read feature flags directly.

**Key design decisions:**
- Primary remote flag: `predictClobV2` (default `false`) enables the v2
protocol
- Temporary rollout flag: `predictClobV2UseLegacyClobHost` forces v2 to
use `https://clob-v2.polymarket.com` during the migration window
- Canonical/default v2 host remains `https://clob.polymarket.com`
- Host selection is resolved once into `protocol.transport.clobBaseUrl`;
lower-level helpers never read raw flags
- v2 API key caching is host-aware to avoid reusing credentials across
host changes
- v2 `getBalance()` always returns `Safe USDC.e + Safe pUSD` — no
branching on upgrade state
- Trade path is **relayer-only**, **Permit2-only** fee collection on

- Deposit/withdraw use **release-time code choices** for preferred vs
fallback variant — not runtime flags
- Wrap: always wraps **entire current Safe USDC.e balance** (never
`MaxUint256`) when maintenance tx is already being emitted
- Unwrap: always unwraps **exact deficit** needed — no over-unwrapping

title: fix(card): value Money account balance via vmUSD share price and USD peg (#33021)
description:
The Card "Avail. balance" for the Money account read the raw vmUSD token
amount and re-priced it through mUSD's live market rate, so it drifted
below the Money tab balance — the gap being the yield-bearing vmUSD
share price (which grows over time) plus the market-vs-peg difference on
mUSD.

Convert the vmUSD share balance to mUSD using the vault exchange rate
(MoneyAccountBalanceService:getExchangeRate) and value mUSD at its 1:1
USD peg, mirroring how the Money account balance is derived. The Card
now matches the Money balance for the same vmUSD position, while still
respecting the delegation allowance clamp (min(balance, allowance)).

Adds Fill-and-Kill (FAK) order type support, feature-flagged OFF by
default via the `predictFakOrders` version-gated remote flag.

`predictFakOrders` flag is version-gated, so old app versions won't get

## **Description**

Adds Deposit Wallet support for the Predict claim flow.

Polymarket Deposit Wallet users still create a normal MetaMask claim
confirmation so the transaction is visible in activity, but the signed
confirmation transaction is not published directly. Instead, Predict
intercepts pending claim transactions in the publish hook, submits the

sign and publish the existing Safe claim transaction path.

claimable positions.

signed before signing.

soon as a transaction hash is available.
- Trigger best-effort CLOB balance-allowance sync after confirmed
claims.
- Wire Predict pending-claim context into `beforeSign` and `publish`.
- Add `skipInitialGasEstimate` to claim confirmation batch creation.

## **Description**
This PR fixes broken lending deposits for Ethereum mainnet USDT. The
USDT contract on mainnet doesn't support updating the token allowance
directly via the `approve` method. Instead, we must manually call
`approve` with a zero amount then we can increase it.

Mainnet USDT Approve Method from
[Etherscan](https://etherscan.io/address/0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831ec7#code)
```solidity
    /**
    * @dev Approve the passed address to spend the specified amount of tokens on behalf of msg.sender.
    * @param _spender The address which will spend the funds.
    * @param _value The amount of tokens to be spent.
    */
    function approve(address _spender, uint _value) public onlyPayloadSize(2 * 32) {

        // To change the approve amount you first have to reduce the addresses`
        //  allowance to zero by calling `approve(_spender, 0)` if it is not
        //  already 0 to mitigate the race condition described here:
        //  https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/20#issuecomment-263524729
        require(!((_value != 0) && (allowed[msg.sender][_spender] != 0)));

        allowed[msg.sender][_spender] = _value;
        Approval(msg.sender, _spender, _value);
    }
```

When a user links a Card to a Money Account, the approve transaction is
submitted by Sentinel on the user's behalf via a delegation. For
Sentinel to redeem that delegation without the Money Account itself
signing (and therefore without needing native MON on the account), the
Money Account must be EIP-7702-upgraded on the card token chain (Monad,
`0x8f`). Previously the linkage pre-flight would **hard-fail** with
`Money account is not 7702-upgraded on Monad` whenever the account had
not already been upgraded — most commonly for users who discover the
Money Account directly through the Card dashboard CTAs and have never
deposited mUSD before. The first revision of this PR attempted to fix
that by triggering the Money Account upgrade via CHOMP from the Card
controller and polling `isAtomicBatchSupported` until ready, but

that the `/v1/account-upgrade` endpoint only *stores* the signed 7702
authorization and only redeems it lazily on the first mUSD deposit — so
the poll could never succeed and the flow timed out at 60s.

This PR removes the explicit pre-flight entirely and relies on the
existing `Delegation7702PublishHook`
([`app/util/transactions/hooks/delegation-7702-publish.ts:215`](app/util/transactions/hooks/delegation-7702-publish.ts:215))
to bundle the 7702 authorization atomically with the same Sentinel relay
submission that publishes the Card approve. When `delegationAddress` is
undefined for the account on the target chain, the hook signs an
EIP-7702 authorization via `KeyringController:signEip7702Authorization`,
attaches it to the relay request as `authorizationList`, and Sentinel
submits both legs as one transact

title: fix: background bridge event leak (#29040)
description:
## **Description**

`BackgroundBridge` subscribes to seven controller messenger events in
its constructor but `onDisconnect()` only tore down three. After a
session disconnects, the leaked subscriptions kept firing — emitting
`chainChanged` / `accountsChanged` notifications and lock/unlock events
to dead sessions.

Root causes of the four leaks:
- `SelectedNetworkController:stateChange` — missing from
`onDisconnect()` entirely.
- `KeyringController:lock` / `unlock` — subscribed with
`this.onLock.bind(this)` / `this.onUnlock.bind(this)` inline, so each
call produced a fresh reference that couldn't be matched for
unsubscription.
- `PermissionController:stateChange` — subscribed with an anonymous
arrow function, same reference-matching problem.

Fix:
- Store stable bound references (`this._handleLock`,
`this._handleUnlock`, `this._handlePermissionControllerStateChange`) in
the constructor and pass them to both `subscribe` and `tryUnsubscribe`.
- Add matching `tryUnsubscribe` calls for all four events in
`onDisconnect()`.
- Make `onDisconnect()` idempotent: early-return on `this.disconnected`,
and convert the existing CAIP `unsubscribe` calls (which throw on a
missing sub) to `tryUnsubscribe`. `onDisconnect` is invoked from ~6 call
sites and could previously throw on a second call.

Affects both SDKConnectV2 and WalletConnect since they share this class.

## **Changelog**

CHANGELOG entry: Fixed a subscription leak in `BackgroundBridge` where
disconnected SDK and WalletConnect sessions could continue to receive
network, account, permission, and lock/unlock notifications.

- `handleAuthenticationTrigger` bulk-fetches OIS on account-group switch
but then silent-auths *every* account in the group without using that

already reported as not opted-in.

1. Gate the account-switch loop on the bulk OIS result — skip silent
auth (session mint via `mobile-login`) only when `ois[i] === false`.

`lastFreshOptInStatusCheck` (fresh OIS owns that timestamp).

`main` (enrolled users can still get a session; bulk OIS failure falls
back to per-account silent auth).

accounts while preserving main-like behavior on OIS outage.

title: fix: dedup chain change relay notifications over WalletConnect (#27978)
description:
## **Description**

WalletConnect reported 7,818 anomalous relay sessions from MetaMask
Mobile. A relay complexity limit takes effect April 15, 2026. Chain
change amplification is a major contributor — a single chain switch with
20 sessions generates ~80 relay messages instead of the expected ~40.

The root cause is two independent notification paths for chain changes:
1. **Store subscription path**: each `WalletConnect2Session` subscribes
to Redux and calls `handleChainChange()` → sends `updateSession` +
`emitSessionEvent` (2 messages)
2. **WalletConnectPort path**: `BackgroundBridge` emits `chainChanged` →
`WalletConnectPort.postMessage` intercepts and calls `updateSession()` →
sends another `updateSession` + `emitSessionEvent` (2 more messages)

This PR:
- Removes the duplicate WalletConnectPort `chainChanged` forwarding
(path 2 above)
- Adds a `lastEmittedChainId` dedup guard in `handleChainChange` to
prevent sequential duplicates from the `approveRequest` + store
subscription race
- Captures the `store.subscribe()` unsubscribe function and calls it in
`removeListeners()` to prevent leaked subscriptions

**Result**: 1 chain switch × 20 sessions = ~40 relay messages (2 per
session), down from ~80.

The app reset / "delete wallet" flow (`Authentication.deleteWallet` →
`resetWalletState`) restores the app to a fresh-install state and
already clears Rewards and Seedless Onboarding, but it never touched the
Card. As a result, a user who was logged in to the Card stayed logged in
after resetting the app (CARD-431). Card auth lives in four places, none
of which the reset cleared: `CardController` state, `CardTokenStore`

cardholder-check timer), and dispatches `resetCardState()` to wipe the
redux slice. Each step is independently guarded so one failure never

`KeyringController:unlock` and rebuilds the account tree, and because

title: fix(android): exclude x86_64 ABI from production AAB to resolve Play 16 KB warning (#30590)
description:
## **Description**

Google Play flagged two prebuilt `.so` files in our production AAB as
non-compliant with Android's 16 KB page-size requirement, both in the
`x86_64` ABI:

- `base/lib/x86_64/libconceal.so` — from `react-native-keychain` via
`com.facebook.conceal:1.1.3` (last released in 2016, archived upstream).
- `base/lib/x86_64/libsecp256k1.so` — from `react-native-fast-crypto`,
shipped as an `IMPORTED` prebuilt in its CMake config (not rebuilt from
source).

Neither library can be realistically rebuilt with 16 KB alignment:

- Facebook Conceal has been unmaintained since 2018; there is no
source-of-truth fork with 16 KB alignment.
- `react-native-fast-crypto` consumes `libsecp256k1.so` as a prebuilt
binary; the existing yarn patch already adds
`-DANDROID_SUPPORT_FLEXIBLE_PAGE_SIZES=ON` for the bridge code we
compile, but it does not regenerate the imported `libsecp256k1.so`
files.

x86_64 is only ever used by Chromebook ARC++/ARCVM and emulators — no
real phone ships with an x86_64 CPU. Dropping the x86_64 ABI from
production AABs silences the Play warning without affecting users.

### What this PR does

Two changes that need to land together:

1. **`android/gradle.properties.release`** — remove `x86_64` from
`reactNativeArchitectures` so React Native's own native libs (Hermes, RN
core) aren't built for that ABI in the production AAB.

2. **`android/app/build.gradle`** — add
`ndk.abiFilters(*reactNativeArchitectures())` inside `defaultConfig`.
Without this, AGP packages every ABI shipped in dependency AARs
regardless of `reactNativeArchitectures`, which is what put the x86_64
`libconceal.so` and `libsecp256k1.so` into the AAB in the first place.

A small refactor of the `reactNativeArchitectures()` helper to return a
`List` (via `.toList()`) makes the Groovy spread
`*reactNativeArchitectures()` into `abiFilters(String...)` robust across
AGP/Groovy versions.

### What this PR does NOT change

- `android/gradle.properties` (default) — local dev still gets x86_6

## **Description**

Reverts the architecture-narrowing changes from #30590 and #30642 that
were rushed in to silence Google Play's 16 KB page-size warning for
`base/lib/x86_64/libconceal.so` and `base/lib/x86_64/libsecp256k1.so`.
Google Play **extended their compliance deadline**, so we have time to
fix the underlying 4 KB alignment issue properly instead of shipping
fewer ABIs as a workaround.

The structural fixes are tracked separately:

- #30591 — replace `react-native-fast-crypto` with
`react-native-quick-crypto` scrypt (drops `libsecp256k1.so`).
- #30592 — drop the Facebook Conceal dependency from
`react-native-keychain` (drops `libconceal.so`).

Once those land, both `.so` files disappear for **every** ABI (including
arm64-v8a), which is the real fix Play actually cares about.

### What this PR restores

| File | After this PR (= pre-#30590 state) |
|---|---|
| `android/gradle.properties.release` |
`reactNativeArchitectures=armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a,x86,x86_64` |
| `android/app/build.gradle` | `reactNativeArchitectures()` back to its
original one-liner; `ndk.abiFilters(*reactNativeArchitectures())` block
removed from `defaultConfig` |

### Why revert rather than keep `abiFilters` for safety?

The `abiFilters` plumbing isn't harmful when paired with all four ABIs
(it would just resolve to all four), but keeping it adds non-obvious
build behavior tied to a workaround we're abandoning. Cleaner to fully
revert and re-introduce when (if) we narrow ABIs again as a deliberate
decision.

### Untouched (already untouched by the original PRs)

- `android/gradle.properties` (default, local dev)
- `android/gradle.properties.github` (CI E2E)

description:
## **Description**

# Root Cause of the Issue

`backupVault` unconditionally calls `setInternetCredentials`, failing
when `VAULT_BACKUP_KEY` already exists in the keychain due to repeated
`KEYRING_STATE_CHANGE_EVENT` triggers.

### The Engine class is initialized, setting up the vault backup
mechanism.
The `Engine` class constructor calls `this.handleVaultBackup()` to
subscribe to keyring state changes, initiating the backup process.
(See app/core/Engine/Engine.ts)

### The Engine subscribes to the KEYRING_STATE_CHANGE_EVENT.
This subscription means that whenever the keyring's state changes, the
associated callback function will be executed, potentially triggering a
vault backup.
(See app/core/Engine/Engine.ts)

### The keyring state changes, and the new state contains a vault.
This event signifies that the keyring's vault data has been loaded or
modified, prompting a backup. This could happen on unlock, account
creation, or import.
(See app/core/Engine/Engine.ts)

### The handleVaultBackup function is triggered, calling backupVault.
The subscription callback in `handleVaultBackup` is executed, leading to
the invocation of the `backupVault` function with the current keyring
state.
(See app/core/Engine/Engine.ts)

### The backupVault function attempts to store the vault in the keychain
without checking for existing credentials.
The `backupVault` function directly calls `setInternetCredentials` with
`VAULT_BACKUP_KEY`, `VAULT_BACKUP_KEY`, and the vault data, without

title: bug: clear MMKV on fresh install (#15244)
description:
<!--
Please submit this PR as a draft initially.
Do not mark it as "Ready for review" until the template has been
completely filled out, and PR status checks have passed at least once.
-->

## **Description**


When digging migration issue
[more](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/issues/13903). we've
come to realise that MMKV causing the issue with the EXISTING_USER flag.

- Right now, when the app starts, in App.tsx, in the second useEffect
the app checks for existing user: const existingUser = await
StorageWrapper.getItem(EXISTING_USER);
- If existing user exists, it calls Authentication.appTriggeredAuth(),
inside it, it tries to get credentials form the keychain. If there are
none, it will thrown an error. Which will be our case, on a new device.
- Error is caught and lockApp is called. This method navigates to the
login screen.
- The MMKV Storage gets restored via iCloud Backup-> app sees
EXISTING_USER and tries to auth -> Auth fails due to lack of actual
vault/credentials -> app shows login screen instead of onboarding.

**Solution:**

Creating a new migration that will move this flag from MMKV to
FileSystem storage, enabling it to not be backed up anymore.
 
Solution Progress Notion Page:
https://www.notion.so/metamask-consensys/Feature-to-better-handle-phone-migrations-1d5f86d67d688075b818fd2c8a291b14?source=copy_link
 
PR Review Recording:
https://consensys.zoom.us/rec/share/JKX_WCkihB9LyXo8USn1dtELH8PGFth31vJug16-gAePqqvHLb4c7prNfBxvWIqP.8UHtS5VF3yr-5kei
Passcode: LE8m.K*C

**Additonally: Optin Metrics Changes**

After moving EXISTING_USER flag from MMKV to Redux, it created a bug
with the OptinMetrics. Every time a user would unlock the app, the
OptinMetrics would pop up again and again.

I idetified two issues:
* Dependency array issue: Including isMetaMetricsUISeen in the
dependency array caused unnecessary re-runs of the authentication flow
(in App.tsx)
* Flag setting issue: The isMetaMetricsUISeen flag wasn't being set in
all completion paths

title: feat!: Allow manifest to extend another manifest (#3802)
description:
This is a follow up to #3793, which introduces custom manifests (e.g.,
one for production, one for development), allowing a custom manifest to
extend another manifest. Right now, the entire production manifest would
need to be copied to the development manifest. After this change it's
possible to do the following:

```json
// snap.manifest.dev.json
{
  "extends": "./snap.manifest.json",
  "initialConnections": {
    "http://example.com": {}
  }
}
```

With a base manifest like:

```json
// snap.manifest.json
{
  "proposedName": "My Snap",
  "other": "properties"
}
```

After which the manifests would be merged like this:

```json
{
  "proposedName": "My Snap",
  "other": "properties",
  "initialConnections": {
    "http://example.com": {}
  }
}
```

Right now this is mainly useful for local development, but may be used
for bundling production Snaps in the future.

## Breaking changes

- The `checkManifest` function now returns `ExtendableSnapFiles`, which
contains an `ExtendableSnapManifest`.

for all four in-range advisories (GHSA-6g55 / r28c / qx2v / 7fh5) via
`.yarn/patches`, scoped so the v8 tree stays on 8.5.21. See the
Validation Run.

### stylelint

- Of the 74 rules in `stylelint.config.js`, **60 no longer exist** in
modern stylelint — the stylistic rules deprecated in 15 and removed in
16. `oxfmt` and `prettier` already own formatting here, so they are
dropped rather than migrated, leaving the 14 that still express a real
constraint. Removing rules only narrows what is reported, so this cannot
introduce new violations.

direct devDependency, since stylelint stopped bundling syntaxes in 14.

is deleted rather than rebased — it patched `lib/syntaxes/index.js`,
which no longer exists.

regenerated MV3 policy gives the 6.x copy its own

title: feat: remove copy button from tx details item sender and recipient addresses (#39018)
description:
## **Description**

This PR removes the copy button and pointer cursor from the sender and
recipient address (when owned) in the transaction details view
(`SenderToRecipient` component).

**Reason for the change:**
Users are vulnerable to address poisoning attacks when copying addresses
from the transaction history. Attackers exploit the common UX pattern of
truncated addresses (showing only first/last characters with "...") by:

1. Monitoring the blockchain for victim transactions
3. Creating spoofed wallets with addresses matching the first/last
characters of legitimate recipients
5. Sending tiny transactions from the spoofed address to the victim
7. Victims then accidentally copy the attacker's address from their
transaction history

**Changes made:**
- Removed `onSenderClick` and `onRecipientClick` callback prop from
`SenderToRecipient` component and all its usages
- Removed the `Tooltip` wrapper and copy-to-clipboard functionality from
the sender and recipient address (this wasn't working for recipient
address in the first place)
- Removed the pointer cursor style for the sender address and the
recipient address when owned. When it's not an owned recipient address,
it shows the pointer cursor and Petname modal when clicked
- Removed related MetaMetrics event tracking for "Copied 'From' Address"
and "Copied 'To' Address"

title: fix: enhance `sanitizeString` to remove bidirectional and invisible Unicode (#37056)
description:
<!--
Please submit this PR as a draft initially.
Do not mark it as "Ready for review" until the template has been
completely filled out, and PR status checks have passed at least once.
-->

## **Description**

This PR improves the `sanitizeString` utility function to
comprehensively prevent text direction manipulation attacks by removing
all Unicode bidirectional control characters and invisible format
characters.

### What is the reason for the change?

Previously, `sanitizeString` only escaped two specific bidirectional
override characters (LTR Override `U+202D` and RTL Override `U+202E`) by
converting them to literal string representations. This approach had
several vulnerabilities:

1. **Incomplete coverage**: It didn't handle other dangerous bidi
control characters like Right-to-Left Mark (`U+200F`), which malicious
actors are actively using to hide numbers in messages and mislead users
2. **Ineffective escaping**: The characters were escaped to strings like
`"\\u202D"` rather than removed, meaning they could still potentially
cause issues
3. **Manual maintenance**: Required manually adding each new Unicode
character that could be exploited

### What is the improvement/solution?

The new implementation uses Unicode property escapes (`\p{Cf}`) to
automatically match and remove **all** Unicode Format category
characters in one pass. This includes:

- **Bidirectional control characters**: LRM, RLM, LRE, RLE, LRO, RLO,
PDF, LRI, RLI, FSI, PDI (`U+200E`, `U+200F`, `U+202A–U+202E`,
`U+2066–U+2069`)
- **Zero-width characters**: ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, ZWNBSP (`U+200B–U+200D`,
`U+FEFF`)
- **Other invisible format characters** automatically covered by the
Unicode Format category

```

path-to-Regexp is used in two files within react-router v5.1.2:

then passed to `pathtoRegexp`. The variables passed to `pathtoRegexp`
are dependent on props or parameters passed to react-router components
and/or methods explictly from the metamask code. So this vulnerability
cannot be exploited by an external actor.

'seed')](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-extension/issues/40226)
The error occurred during the Reset Wallet → Re-onboard with SRP flow:
- Social login onboarding creates a wallet with an HD keyring
- Wallet is locked, then login fails (intentional auth error) →
"connections removed" modal appears
- User resets the wallet — this clears controller state and removes the
HD keyring
- New onboarding begins — user creates a new wallet with SRP
- During re-onboarding, a background process (likely a preinstalled Snap
such as @metamask/message-signing-snap) calls
getKeyringsByType(KeyringType.hdKeyTree) to access the mnemonic seed
before the new HD keyring is fully created
- `getKeyringsByType()` returns an empty array [], so destructuring
const [keyring] = [] yields keyring = undefined
Accessing keyring.seed on undefined throws the TypeError.

## **Description**

This PR adds detailed wallet composition metrics derived from the
accounts controller. The goal here is to be able to answer questions
about...
1. how many SRPs users have
2. How many hw wallets user have
3. How many total account groups users have
4. how many hardware wallet accounts users have. 

Fixes account wallet composition user properties that were unreliable
when the wallet was locked.
Previously, several traits were derived from keyrings, which is
unavailable in locked state. This PR
migrates all wallet composition traits to use internalAccounts, which is
always available.

Root cause: #getNumberOfHDEntropies read from metamaskState.keyrings,
returning stale/empty data when
  locked.

Fix: Replaced with #getAccountCompositionTraits, a single O(n) pass over
internalAccounts.accounts that
  computes all wallet composition traits atomically.

  New/updated user properties schema


```┌────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Property │ Description │

├────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ number_of_hd_entropies │ Count of unique SRP (Secret Recovery Phrase)
sources — deduped by │

│ number_of_account_groups │ Count of distinct {entropy.id, groupIndex}
pairs; multichain │
│ │ EVM+BTC+SOL accounts from the same SRP slot count as one group │

├────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

## **Description**

`MetaMetricsController.trackPage()` always set `chain_id: this.chainId`
for every Segment page-view event. `this.chainId` is sourced from the
EVM `NetworkController` and only updates on
`NetworkController:networkDidChange`, so when the user is on a non-EVM
context (Bitcoin, Solana, etc.) the EVM chainId leaks into page-view
metrics — defaulting to `0x1` (Ethereum mainnet) if that's the last EVM
network selected. The most visible manifestation was during a Bitcoin
Send, where the route change to `/confirmation/:id` produces a `New
Confirmation Page` event tagged with `chain_id: 0x1`.

The companion `trackEvent` flow already implements the data-team
contract from PR #32586 (`metametrics-controller.ts:1343-1358`): when
`chain_id_caip` is set, `chain_id` is `null`. This PR extends the same
convention to `trackPage`. `MetaMetricsController` now calls
`MultichainNetworkController:getState` lazily inside `trackPage` and
emits:

- `chain_id: null` + `chain_id_caip: <CAIP-2 chain id>` when
`isEvmSelected` is `false`
- `chain_id: this.chainId` (no `chain_id_caip` key) when `isEvmSelected`
is `true`

A conditional spread is used (rather than `chain_id_caip: undefined`) so
the EVM payload has no `chain_id_caip` own property at all — `undefined`
values are handled inconsistently by Jest equality matchers and
downstream serializers.

**Why lazy lookup?** Page tracking fires only on UI route changes (a few
times per minute at most), so a per-call `messenger.call` is simpler
than caching state via a `:networkDidChange` subscription, and it avoids
the staleness window between a chain switch and the cached-state update.

whenever a non-EVM network is selected was wrong, not only `New

title: fix: filter undefined accounts from accounts selectors (#41834)
description:
## **Description**

Possible Cause (two defects):

1. Hardware wallet addresses in the keyring use checksummed format
(0xAbCd...) but `AccountsController` stores them lowercase (0xabcd...).
The lookup fails, producing an undefined entry
that spreads to {} — an empty object stored at
accountsById["undefined"].
2. `AccountTreeController` transiently stores undefined (not a UUID) in
group.accounts when an account without a valid id passes through during
account sync. This entry looks up `accountsById["undefined"] = {}`,
which passes the `!== undefined` filter since an empty object is not
undefined.

The empty object reaches `isEVMAccountForSend`, which has no guard for
missing `type` — crash.

How they combined: `getMetaMaskAccountsOrdered` could spread `undefined`
into `{}`, which `accountsById` stored under the string key
`"undefined"`. Tree iteration then resolved `accountsById[undefined]` to
that empty object, which passed the previous `!== undefined` filter and
produced account metadata with no `type`, leading to a crash downstream.

**Fixes:**  
- `selectors.js`: After the keyring address map, chain
`.filter(Boolean)` so undefined lookups never enter the account pipeline
(also avoids a secondary failure in snap deduplication when
`existing.id` would throw on `undefined`).
- `account-tree.ts`: In `getWalletsWithAccounts`, require `accountId !==
undefined && accountId !== null` before the `accountsById` lookup so
stale tree entries are dropped (defense in depth).

## **Changelog**

CHANGELOG entry: Fixed a crash that could occur when account ordering
briefly contained invalid entries during hardware wallet or multichain
account sync.

title: chore: centralize agent skills via public MetaMask/skills (+ private Consensys overlay) (#42488)
description:
## **Description**

Per [ADR #57](https://github.com/MetaMask/decisions/pull/162). Removes
committed agent skills/rules; switches install to the new **public**
[`MetaMask/skills`](https://github.com/MetaMask/skills) repo, with the
private [`Consensys/skills`](https://github.com/Consensys/skills) repo
available as an optional overlay for internal-only material.

### Why public

- Cloud agents (Cursor cloud, Codex cloud, Claude.ai web) can't `git
clone` a private repo or set engineer-managed env vars. The public repo
solves this with a one-liner curl bootstrap (no SSH, no auth).
- New engineers don't need Consensys SSO to start using skills — the
public set installs cleanly on its own.
- Out-of-the-box auto-sync via `postinstall`.

### Engineer experience (zero-config)

```
yarn install   # postinstall clones MetaMask/skills into .skills-cache/ and installs
yarn skills    # auto-detects the cache, no env var or shell rc edit needed
```

Override only if you keep a separate clone:
```
export METAMASK_SKILLS_DIR=~/dev/metamask/skills
export CONSENSYS_SKILLS_DIR=~/dev/Consensys/skills   # optional private overlay
```

### Changes

- `development/skills-sync.mts` — multi-source aware wrapper (was bash,
ported to node `.mts` to match `lint-changed.mts` / `lint-baseline.mts`
conventions and avoid WSL/CRLF issues at the wrapper layer). Resolution
order: `METAMASK_SKILLS_DIR` → `CONSENSYS_SKILLS_DIR` → auto-fallback to
`.skills-cache/metamask-skills`. When the cache is used, injects
`METAMASK_SKILLS_DIR=<cache>` so the bash sync underneath sees the
source.
- `development/skills-postinstall.mts` **(new)** — auto-clones
`MetaMask/skills` into `.skills-cache/metamask-skills` and runs the
installer on every `yarn install`. Layered with `CONSENSYS_SKILLS_DIR`
when set. Best-effort: skipped on CI, on `SKILLS_SKIP_POSTINSTALL=1`, or
when offline. Opt back in on CI with `SKILLS_FORCE_POSTINSTALL=1`.

public canonica

**Updated vulnerable packages to secure versions:**
- `lodash`: 4.17.21 → 4.17.23 (fixes prototype pollution in
`_.unset`/`_.omit`)
- `@babel/runtime`: 7.25.9 → 7.26.10 (fixes inefficient RegExp in
transpiled named capture groups)

**Regenerated patches with identical functionality:**
- `lodash-npm-4.17.23-50bdb1c01a.patch` - Firefox contentscript fix
(global → globalThis)
- `@babel-runtime-npm-7.26.10-fe8c62510a.patch` - Reflect.construct
optimization

**Updated lockfile and package references** to point to new patched
versions.

## Technical Notes

The patches are functionally unchanged - only applied to newer base
versions. LavaMoat policies likely don't need updates, but should be
verified post-merge.

title: fix: stop calling end in createDupeReqFilterMiddleware.ts, so that dapps get correct response to 'seenRequests' (#24672)
description:
## **Description**

This PR fixes the following problem:

1. Dapp sends a request to MetaMask shortly after the service worker
starts up, and _before_ the inpage provider receives the
`METAMASK_EXTENSION_CONNECT_CAN_RETRY` message from the content-script
(which happens after the metamask controller initializes and notifies
all connections of a `chainChanged` event)
2. The request hits the middleware created by
`createDupeReqFilterMiddleware.ts` and its id is added to
`seenRequestIds`
3. Before the necessary controller responds to the request, the inpage
provider _now_ receives the `METAMASK_EXTENSION_CONNECT_CAN_RETRY`
message from the content-script
4. The provider now retries the request. This happens without the dapp
doing anything; this is part of our MV3 retry logic to ensure requests
don't get lost under service worker stoppage / start-up conditions. (The
provider does this via the imported `createStreamMiddleware`
https://github.com/MetaMask/json-rpc-middleware-stream/blob/main/src/createStreamMiddleware.ts#L128-L130)
5. The new retry of the request hits the middleware created by
`createDupeReqFilterMiddleware`. (The original request still has not
been responded to.) The new retry of the request has the same id as the
original, so the middleware hits the `} else if
(!seenRequestIds.add(req.id)) {` condition and calls `end()`
6. The original request, which was being awaited by the dapp, now is
resolved but without a meaningful response (as the middleware just did
an `end()` call without the request being handled in any way)

This problem was discovered by some e2e tests which became very flaky
under MV3. Tests that involved the Simple Snap Keyring dapp would often
send a `wallet_requestSnaps` request, and then not get the necessary
response, due to the issue described above.

The solution to the problem presented in this PR is just to not call
`end` when seeing a duplicate request, because the original request
should be responded to eventually.

### Easy: Verify non-redirect domains still work

1. Install the extension (you should test mv2 and mv3)
2. go through onboarding if necessary
2. go to a phishing website, like `claimblast.lol` (these websites seem
to go down all the time, so you might have to grab one from
https://github.com/MetaMask/eth-phishing-detect/commits/main/ to test
with)
3. make sure it redirects to the phishing website

### Tricky: Verify domains that redirect are now blocked:

1. modify background.js by replacing `!phishingTestResponse?.result`
with `hostname !== "shorturl.at"` (since we test blocking my test URL
that is on a domain that isn't supposed to be blocked)
2. run `yarn start` (test both mv2 and mv3) 
3. install the extension
4. go through onboarding if necessary
4. navigate to `https://shorturl.at/6F2Zt`
5. you should see our phishing page. if you see evil.com it didn't work
:-(


Some notes:

* If MetaMask has not fully initialized yet (like on a browser restart)
redirect blocking won't work.
* The new phishing detection code kicks in _before_ our current
`content_script`-based blocking, so it works for redirect cases as well
as normal phishing blocking.

The seed phrase reminder will now be triggered if the user has eth *OR* if the user has added a token. This is to ensure that a user can't have a positive token balance without being reminded to backup the account.

Checking for the token in preferences was easier than checking the actual token balance, because the token balance is not yet in Redux. That would require a more substantial refactor.

description: Closes #5577 Closes #7493 This PR adds description text above the Reset Account in settings, pictured below. > Resetting your account will clear your transaction history. This will not change the balances in your accounts or require you to re-enter your seed phrase.

title: Adding mechanism to randomize seed phrase filename
description:
Fixes: https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-extension/issues/7687

(Follow up after talking with @danfinlay)

The filename is seeded by a simple use of `Math.random()` pulling from an alphanumeric character bank, as opposed to a more cryptographically random solution. This provides a simple layer of difficulty for bad actors to seek out the recovery phrase file.

title: Fix intermittent e2e test failure
description:
The 'can retype the seed phrase' test would fail sometimes when one of the words in the seed phrase was a subset of another word (e.g. 'issue' and 'tissue'). This is because the selector used to find the word looked for the first element that contained the text, rather than an exact match.

To simplify the selector and make it more reliable, test ids were added to each seed phrase word. The selector now uses CSS instead of XPath, and it only finds exact matches.

description:
The `confirm-seed-phrase` component extends PureComponent, so it doesn't need a `shouldComponentUpdate` function. The state is effectively immutable, as all state is either a primitive type or is updated with new instances rather than mutation.

Removing this function will silence a warning message printed to the console during e2e tests (React doesn't want you to set this function on `PureComponent`s).

title: Update Seed Phrase Functionality on Account Import
description:
I had the thought the other day that the seed phrase input should be treated as a password; any user using something like `pass` doesn't really need to have the seed phrase visible in the UI (and likely doesn't want it to be?).

**Rational**:

I keep my seedphrase in a password manager that has a "copy to clipboard" functionality. the idea being that I never want to display my seedphrase (or passwords) on screen (in plain text). the textarea is now a password field and you can toggle back to

title: Replace removed 'copy-to-clipboard' icon
description:
The 'copy-to-clipboard' icon was removed in #8190, and replaced with a new 'Copy' icon component. It was still being used in two places though, on the confirmation page for decryption and on the reveal seed phrase screen..

The new Copy icon is now used in these two places instead. It has been given a size of '17' to match the old icon size.

title: Make seed phrase import case insensitive
description:
The user-specified seed phrase during the first-time-flow import step
required the phrase to be entered in all lowercase. The case does not
add any extra entropy to the seed, so there's no reason to be case
sensitive. Flexibility here will improve the onboarding UX.

This commit makes the entered seed phrase case insensitive.

Fixes #8171

title: epee: abstract_tcp_server2: resolve CID 203919 (DC.WEAK_CRYPTO)
description:
The problem actually exists in two parts:

1. When sending chunks over a connection, if the queue size is
greater than N, the seed is predictable across every monero node.

>"If rand() is used before any calls to srand(), rand() behaves as if
it was seeded with srand(1). Each time rand() is seeded with the same seed, it
must produce the same sequence of values."

2. The CID speaks for itself: "'rand' should not be used for security-related
applications, because linear congruential algorithms are too easy to break."

*But* this is an area of contention.

One could argue that a CSPRNG is warranted in order to fully mitigate any
potential timing attacks based on crafting chunk responses. Others could argue
that the existing LCG, or even an MTG, would suffice (if properly seeded). As a

title: epee: add SSL support
description:
RPC connections now have optional tranparent SSL.

An optional private key and certificate file can be passed,
using the --{rpc,daemon}-ssl-private-key and
--{rpc,daemon}-ssl-certificate options. Those have as
argument a path to a PEM format private private key and
certificate, respectively.
If not given, a temporary self signed certificate will be used.

SSL can be enabled or disabled using --{rpc}-ssl, which
accepts autodetect (default), disabled or enabled.

Access can be restricted to particular certificates using the
--rpc-ssl-allowed-certificates, which takes a list of
paths to PEM encoded certificates. This can allow a wallet to
connect to only the daemon they think they're connected to,
by forcing SSL and listing the paths to the known good
certificates.

To generate long term certificates:

openssl genrsa -out /tmp/KEY 4096
openssl req -new -key /tmp/KEY -out /tmp/REQ
openssl x509 -req -days 999999 -sha256 -in /tmp/REQ -signkey /tmp/KEY -out /tmp/CERT

/tmp/KEY is the private key, and /tmp/CERT is the certificate,
both in PEM format. /tmp/REQ can be removed. Adjust the last
command to set expiration date, etc, as needed. It doesn't
make a whole lot of sense for monero anyway, since most servers
will run with one time temporary self signed certificates anyway.

SSL support is transparent, so all communication is done on the
existing ports, with SSL autodetection. This means you can start
using an SSL daemon now, but you should not enforce SSL yet or
nothing will talk to you.

  scan_from_height: 64 bit unsigned integer, optional
  password: string, optional
  viewkey: string, hex representation
  spendkey: string, hex representation
  seed: string, optional, list of words separated by spaces

Either seed or private keys should be given. If using private
keys, the spend key may be omitted (the wallet will not be
able to spend, but will see incoming transactions).

If scan_from_height is given, blocks below this height will not
be checked for transactions as an optimization.

title: Fix bug in mempool get_transaction_stats histogram calculation
description:
The 98th percentile position in the agebytes map was incorrectly
calculated: it assumed the transactions in the mempool all have unique
timestamps at second-granularity. This commit fixes this by correctly
finding the right cumulative number of transactions in the map suffix.

This bug could lead to an out-of-bounds write in the rare case that
all transactions in the mempool were received (and added to the mempool)
at a rate of at least 50 transactions per second. (More specifically,
the number of *unique* receive_time values, which have second-
granularity, must be at most 2% of the number of transactions in the
mempool for this crash to trigger.) If this condition is satisfied, 'it'
points to *before* the agebytes map, 'delta' gets a nonsense value, and
the value of 'i' in the first stats.histo-filling loop will be out of
bounds of stats.histo.

title: feat(ed25519): Add montgomeryToEdwardsPub for XEdDSA support (#197)
description:
* feat(ed25519): Add montgomeryToEdwardsPub for XEdDSA support

This commit introduces the `montgomeryToEdwardsPub` function, which converts an X25519 (Montgomery) public key into an Ed25519 (Twisted Edwards) public key.

This functionality is essential for implementing protocols like Signal's XEdDSA, where a single master key is used to derive both an X25519 key for key agreement and an Ed25519 key for signing. While the public identity key is the X25519 key, signatures are created with the corresponding Ed25519 key.

To verify these signatures, a recipient must be able to convert the public X25519 key back into a valid Ed25519 public key. This function provides that missing piece, enabling the full signature verification workflow for such protocols directly within noble-curves.

A test case has been added to ensure that a key can be converted from Edwards to Montgomery and back, and that a signature can be successfully verified with the recovered key.

title: Fix "Cannot load wallet for Trezor signing" in digital signature sign-in
description:
Signing the dummy transaction with a Trezor key during the sign-in via digital
signature flow failed with "Cannot load wallet for Trezor signing". Building
the Trezor Suite deeplink needs the full wallet, which was only loaded from the
local DB by wallet id. Before sign-in completes the wallet isn't in the local
DB, and the signin-dummy response returns no wallet id or BSMS descriptor, so
the lookup failed and the failure was silently swallowed. TapSigner/ColdCard
were unaffected because they sign the PSBT directly without the wallet.

Resolve the wallet from a BSMS descriptor instead: the server descriptor when
present, otherwise the BSMS the user pasted on the Enter XPUB screen
(userData/signInData). Applied to both WalletAuthenticationViewModel and
SignInAuthenticationViewModel, and added Timber diagnostics.

description:
* feat(cli): hardware wallet integration with session-based signer dispatch

Adds hardware-wallet support to the onekey CLI alongside the existing
bot-wallet flow. Core pieces:

Auth layer
- `onekey auth login --hardware` persists the active wallet (standard /
  hidden-on-host / hidden-on-device) to ~/.onekey/auth-session.json. All
  wallet commands (balance, transfer, swap*, wallet history) dispatch
  from walletKind in the session; no --hardware flag required at the
  command site.
- AuthLoginMethod and AuthWalletKind regain 'hardware' + DeviceInfo +
  PassphraseMode. ResolvedAuthSession grows optional device and
  passphraseMode fields; the session store validator accepts either the
  app_transfer/hd shape or hardware/hardware + required device +
  passphrase_mode.
- auth-logout clears KEYCHAIN_PASSPHRASE_STATE_KEY and
  KEYCHAIN_SESSION_ID_KEY in addition to the legacy mnemonic entries.
  AuthSessionResolver.silentlyClearEverything now clears all four keys
  so a corrupted hardware session cannot leak stale passphraseState /
  session_id into the next login.

Signer layer (kit-bg-style chain registry)
- signer/registry.ts holds a SIGNER_LOADERS map keyed by chain impl.
  Each entry is `() => import('./impls/<chain>')` — lazy so esbuild
  only bundles a chain's code path when some command actually asks for
  it. Adding a new chain is one new impls/<chain>/index.ts plus one
  line in SIGNER_LOADERS; factory.ts never changes.
- factory.ts becomes a thin dispatcher: getHdSignerByImpl (used only by
  AuthManager.persistHdWalletSession for fresh-mnemonic bootstrap) and
  getSignerFromSession (primary API, picks EvmHardwareSigner when
  walletKind === 'hardware' else EvmSigner).
- HardwareSignerBase owns all chain-agnostic hardware lifecycle: install
  passphrase provider, unlock device, preload session cache from
  keychain (skipped after unlock), and the 4-step getHwCommonParams
  resolve chain (in-process cache → keychain → fresh SDK → empty-
  passphrase fallback).

description:

* fix: fail Ledger chain call when fingerprint cannot be persisted

Post-success chainFingerprint generation used to be best-effort: when the
generation or DB write failed it was logged and swallowed, but the
original device call's result still flowed back to the caller. The
caller then persisted the returned address into the wallet record while
the device record kept its chainFingerprint slot empty. Subsequent ops
re-entered the "no fingerprint -> SDK skip verification" branch, so a
different physical seed could silently overwrite the wallet's address
and even leak to the destructive "address mismatch" dialog on verify.

Propagate the failure as DeviceMismatch instead of silently dropping it,
so the caller refuses to persist an unverifiable address.

  T4 429/Retry-After→keep+retry · T5 misaligned/over-long/short 206 →

title: fix(send): share recent recipients across same-mnemonic wallets via on-chain identity (OK-53307) (#11241)
description:
Switch SimpleDbEntityRecentRecipients storage key from
`networkImpl__accountId` to `(networkImplOrId, accountIdentity)` so two HD
wallets that wrap the same mnemonic share a single recent-recipient list,
instead of each maintaining its own per-accountId bucket as introduced by
PR #11186.

The accountIdentity is resolved via `serviceAccount.getAccountXpubOrAddress`
which returns the xpub (or address as fallback). EVM networkIds are still
collapsed to their impl (`evm--1` / `evm--56` -> `evm`) before keying so
recipients stay shared across all EVM chains, matching the pre-#11186
behavior. Non-EVM networkIds pass through unchanged.

This brings RecentRecipients closer to LocalHistory / LocalTokens / LocalNFTs
which already key on-chain data by identity via `buildAccountLocalAssetsKey`.
Resolves the divergence reported on Lightning where the API
`/transfer-recipient` doesn't index, leaving the local fallback as the only
source.

- Entity: take `accountIdentity` instead of `accountId`, expose
  `IRecentRecipientEntry` and `RECENT_RECIPIENTS_BUCKET_CAP` for callers,
  delete unused `deleteRecentRecipient` dead code.
- Service: resolve `accountId` -> identity via `getAccountXpubOrAddress`.
  On read, fan out across all derive-type xpubs
  (`safeGetAccountXpubsForAllDeriveTypes`) and merge so BTC/LTC merge-derive
  accounts see a unified list regardless of the currently-active derive
  type - mirrors `ServiceHistory.fetchTransferRecipients`.
- Logger: add `transaction.send.recentRecipientsSkipWrite` event for the
  near-impossible case where identity can't be resolved during a confirmed
  tx.

Feature is unreleased so no migration is needed; orphaned old-key data is
cleared by dev tools in test builds.

description:
* fix: improve keyless backend share migration

* fix: block keyless backend share owner rewrite during reset pin

When reset pin re-uploads the juicebox share under the new targetOwnerId
but the backend share owner differs, the backend share owner rewrite is a
consistency requirement, not an opportunistic migration. Running it as
fire-and-forget background work could leave the backend share under the
previous owner while juicebox lives under the new owner; a later restore
then reads the stale backendShareResult.ownerId and fails to locate the
juicebox share, with no self-healing path (passive migration only covers
v1 -> v2, not v2 owner mismatch).

Split the reset-pin migration decision:
- owner changed: await migrateKeylessBackendShareToV2 before confirming
  reset, so failures surface instead of being swallowed.
- pure v1 -> v2 with unchanged owner: keep it as background best-effort
  work that self-heals via passive migration.

Update tests accordingly and add coverage for the owner-unchanged v1 path.

title: fix: harden WalletConnect identity attestation against metadata spoofing (#11570)
description:
* fix: harden WalletConnect identity attestation against metadata spoofing

A WalletConnect peer that runs as a Node.js script (no browser origin)
can set arbitrary metadata.url in its SignClient.init, e.g.
"https://app.uniswap.org". OneKey rendered that attacker-supplied URL
as the connecting site and ran it through serviceDiscovery.checkUrlSecurity
unconditionally, which scored the claimed URL and surfaced the green
"Verified Site" badge plus a verified-checkmark icon on both the pairing
modal and every in-session signature/transaction confirmation sheet.

The fix consumes Reown's Verify API (verifyContext.verified.validation
and isScam) inside useRiskDetection and merges its identity-layer signal
into the existing reputation-layer score. Backend / Node.js peers
structurally can never produce validation === VALID per the WalletConnect
verify-attestations spec, so they are forced down to Unknown level and the
"Verified Site" affordance disappears. INVALID (origin mismatch) and
isScam are upgraded to High and reuse the existing critical UI.

No new UI components, no new i18n keys, no chain-provider changes.
The verifyContext is forwarded through the request.data envelope by
WalletConnectRequestProxy and hoisted back onto $sourceInfo by
ServiceDApp.openModal, so each WC-reachable modal consumes it via a
single useRiskDetection parameter.

Replaces the inline `(backendSecurityInfo ?? ({} as IHostSecurity))` cast
with a typed helper that produces a structurally complete IHostSecurity
baseline. Behavior unchanged — same merged level, same downstream UI —
but the hook no longer lies about the shape of objects it returns when
the backend security check hasn't resolved yet.

* fix: read replace-tx nonce precheck from custom RPC broadcast source (OK-55650)

When a custom RPC is enabled on a built-in network and the user has not
opted into the default RPC for the send, the tx is broadcast directly to
that node, whose nonce view can diverge from the wallet API. The nonce
precheck previously always read from the wallet API, so it could pass while
the node rejected the broadcast with a raw 'nonce too low' error that the
backend-40024 catch did not recognize, leaving the stale local pending
uncleaned.

  useDefaultRpc through from batchSignAndSendTransaction. Custom-RPC

description:
* fix(usePromiseResult): close all focus-gate audit findings (follow-up to #11681)

PR #11681 was squash-merged from `2cbba95` (cross-scope guard for
deps changes), which left two later audit rounds outside x:

Audit round 1 — symptoms exposed by the success-path focus-gate split:
- swrKey leak at setResult — swrKey is not part of runnerDeps, so a
  render-time swrKey swap (e.g. RecentNetworks switching wallet /
  account while deps stay [availableNetworks, showAllNetwork]) does
  not bump nonceRef. An in-flight A request still satisfied the
  nonce check and overwrote B's render-time swap. Add the captured
  swrKey identity check to the setResult site, not only the SWR
  cache write.
- isLoading stuck after blur-time resolution — setLoadingFalse was
  still gated by shouldSetState (focus-aware), so watchLoading
  spinners and onIsLoadingChange saw isLoading == true forever
  after a successful blur-time resolution.
- undefinedResultIfError silently dropped on blur — the catch
  branch still used shouldSetState, so blur-time rejections never
  reset the result for callers that opted in, and non-AbortError
  rejections were re-thrown as unhandled rejections instead of
  being absorbed.

- catch path missed swrKey scope check. AbortError fires
  unconditionally on cancelled IndexedDB transactions (search /

  opted into undefinedResultIfError. Now gated on scope identity;
  stale-scope branch also suppresses the re-throw — the abandoned
  request's failure must not surface under the new scope.

  so two phantom transitions could leak: a focus-gated no-op runner

title: feat: fee estimate stop/resume polling on server signal(OK-53769) (#11375)
description:
* feat: stop fee estimate polling when server returns stopPolling

Honor `stopPolling: true` on estimate-fee error responses (e.g. allowance
shortage, expired swap quote) so the failure message stays visible without
spamming the endpoint with retries that can't succeed.

- usePromiseResult: expose `setStopPolling`; finally-block bails before
  scheduling the next tick when set, and the runnerDeps effect clears the
  flag automatically so input changes resume polling.
- TxFeeInfo: detect `error.data.stopPolling` after gas-account fallback
  classification, and read errMessage from OneKeyServerApiError fields
  instead of the JSON-RPC path that never matched server API errors.
- IOneKeyAPIBaseResponse: declare optional `stopPolling` field.

* refactor: address stopPolling review feedback

- Reorder fee errMessage fallback chain so JSON-RPC inner errors
  ("execution reverted: ...") are no longer shadowed by the wrapper
  Error.message.
- Suppress global autoToast on stopPolling errors; the inline fee error
  already carries the same message and now stays visible without a
  redundant toast on top, matching the sponsor-fallback branches.
- Make EstimateTxFeeRetry callback clear stopPolling before re-running,
  so a manual retry actually resumes the polling loop instead of
  stalling at the finally-block guard.
- Drop the unused setStopPollingState in usePromiseResult — no consumer
  reacts to it via React state, the ref alone is sufficient.

* fix: resume fee polling when manual retry clears server-driven stop

setStopPolling(false) only flipped the ref flag, but the polling chain
had already exited via the finally-block guard and run() without a
pollingNonce never schedules the next tick — so clicking retry after a
stopPolling error fired one request and stayed silent forever, even
when the response went back to normal.

Bump the nonce and fire a run with it inside setStopPolling on the
true → false transition (same path runnerDeps uses), so polling
actually resumes;

* fix: assert legacy account identity before irreversible OneKey ID OAuth bind

apiBindLegacyOneKeyIdOAuth POSTs to /prime/v1/account/identities/oauth/bind
— an irreversible, one-time-per-identity server-side bind — using whatever
token occupies the shared legacy session slot, with only a truthiness check.

expand tab, so the popup can re-log the legacy slot in as another account

Always check for validity in ecdsa_read_pubkey.
description:
An invalid point may crash the implementation or, worse,
reveal information about the private key if used in a ECDH
context (e.g. cryptoMessageEn/Decrypt).

Therefore, check all user supplied points even if
USE_PUBKEY_VALIDATE is not set.

To improve speed, we don't check if the point lies in the
main group, since the secp256k1 curve does not have
any other subgroup.

title: Use bn_add instead of bn_addmod (#80)
description:
The bip32 private key derivation used bn_addmod to handle
wrap around.  This was never sufficient as bn_addmod uses only
bn_fast_mod, so an additional bn_mod is necessary.  The bn_fast_mod
helped when bn_mod was not side-channel safe.  Now that bn_mod uses
constant time code, we can get rid of the unnecessary bn_fast_mod
step and use bn_add instead of bn_addmod.

title: embed/extmod/modtrezorcrypto: add secp256k1_zkp module
description:
This includes the https://github.com/ElementsProject/secp256k1-zkp library
(which is a fork from sipa/secp256k1 used in Bitcoin Core) as a module. It
is currently not used in any app.

This commit the first step towards integrating Liquid (tracking issue #282).

Note that this creates a new 64 kiB read-only data section in .flash2 for
pre-computed tables (secp256k1_ecmult_static_context) which speed up
signature creation and related private key operations.

title: Faster PBKDF2 by reusing intermediate results.
description:
The old implementation needed 6 sha transformations per iterations:

- 2 for computing sha512 of seed,
- 2 for computing digests of ipads/opads,
- 2 for computing digests of intermediate hashes.

The first 4 transformations are the same in every iteration so we cache
them.  A new function hmac_sha512_prepare computes these digests.
We made sha512_Transform visible in pbkdf2 and prevent unneccessary
big/little endian conversions back and forth.

title: core: refactor keychain to only support one curve at a time
description:
also make a cleaner distinction between keychain, seed, path

This enables using `unsafe_prompts`, because with the original code, if
there was no namespace match, we wouldn't know which curve to use.

For ease of implementation, we use a LRU cache for derived keys,
instead of the original design "one cache entry per namespace".

SLIP21 is now treated completely separately, via `slip21_namespaces` and
`derive_slip21` method.
If more slip21-like things come in the future, we can instead hang them
on the keychain: put a per-curve Keychain object accessible by
`keychain[curve_name].derive()`, and the majority usecase will just pass
around `keychain[curve_name]` instead of having to specify the curve in
every `derive()` call.

Or alternately we'll just specify the curve in every `derive()` call,
whichever seems more appropriate.

title: timer: Fix non-critical integer overflow (#129)
description:
Every 4294967295 milliseconds (2 ^ 32 - 1), system_millis will overflow.
This means that every 49.71 days, system_millis will reset to zero.
Comparisons like `system_millis < (system_millis + 1)` would fail if the
latter had overflown and the former had not.

This is non-critical because the worst case is that one second could be
skipped or the screen could lock early.

This poses no threat to the exponential backoff used for protection
against brute force.

description:
* chore: checkpoint trezor ble integration

* refactor(trezor): align adapter with Ledger pattern, fix race + cancel

Brings TrezorAdapter onto the same IConnector-forwarding shape as the
in-prod LedgerAdapter and closes a series of gaps found via cross-audit.

- Delete redundant TrezorConnectorBase shell that conflicted with the
  canonical one in hwk-trezor-connector, plus its rawExchange/thp* surface
  on TrezorAdapter.
- Method dispatch: unknown methods throw MethodNotSupported (was
  UnknownError); BTC unified to 'btcGetAddress' (was bare 'getAddress').
- BLE physical disconnect now propagates: TrezorConnectorByteTransport
  gains optional onDisconnect, wired through TrezorRnBleConnector so
  TrezorConnectorBase can clean sessions and emit device-disconnect.
- dispose() unregisters connector listeners (was leaking handler closures
  and mutating state after teardown).
- _ensureSession dedupes concurrent first calls via per-connectId pending
  promise map; connectDevice routed through it for idempotency.
- cancel() releases pending UI waits via uiResponse(CANCEL); useful while
  connector.cancel() remains a TODO.
- Transport disconnect errors (reject/notify-timeout/ensureConnected)
  tagged with HardwareErrorCode.DeviceDisconnected so the adapter can
  distinguish them from UnknownError.
- getChainFingerprint uses features.device_id (Trezor's native stable
  seed identifier) instead of returning caller-supplied deviceId verbatim.
- searchDevices preserves currently-connected devices that a rescan missed.
- _call auto-retries once on DeviceDisconnected with a fresh session,
  mirroring Ledger's _retryWithFreshConnection.

Tests: hwk-trezor-adapter 16/16, hwk-trezor-connector 8/8,

title: Feat/kaspa tx parse (#839)
description:
* feat(kaspa): support streaming transaction signing

* feat(kaspa): support previous-transaction streaming verification

- Sync protobuf messages from firmware e6ffa3157: prev-tx request flow
  (KaspaTxAckPrevMeta/PrevInput/PrevOutput, KASPA_TX_PREV_META,
  prev_tx_id on KaspaTxRequest) and required-field tightening.
- Add optional refTxs param; answer device prev-tx requests from it and
  reject them clearly when the referenced tx is missing, instead of
  silently answering with current-tx data.
- Pin TonSignData.timestamp to UintType via protobuf-patches so clean
  regenerations keep the published type (hand-edited in #778).

* fix(hd-transport): decode absent optional sub-messages as null

Absent optional message-type fields are not own properties of the
protobufjs-decoded instance, so messageToJSON recursed into undefined
and threw a raw TypeError. Surfaced by the Kaspa streaming flow: the
device's first KaspaTxRequest legitimately carries no signature yet.
Decode them to null, mirroring the optional primitive-field convention.

* feat(kaspa): prefer blind signing when refTxs is absent

Streaming input verification needs the referenced previous transactions;
without refTxs the session would die on the device's first prev-tx
request. Send the plain legacy packet instead when blind signing is
available. A streaming-only tx (payload/gas or no scripts) still
streams — its only chance — and fails clearly if prev txs are requested.

Also condense comments and drop a redundant test case.

* fix(kaspa): fail loud when legacy sighash is missing a script

Replace `output.script ?? ''` (would silently hash an empty script into the sighash) and `input.output.script!` (crashes with an opaque TypeError) with explicit guards that throw CallMethodInvalidParameter. The supportsLegacy gate already guarantees scripts are present before serialize runs, so this never triggers today; it hardens the invariant against future gate changes.

description:
Three related fixes to how the SDK handles a degraded iframe connection:

Unknown iframe errors no longer clear the stored account. Only the
explicit not-configured/missing-entropy signals prove the iframe
evaluated the account; an unknown error is just as likely a transient
failure (failed storage read, network error mid-flow), and deleting the
account on those forced users through recovery with intact signer state.

Connection-health transitions are now surfaced as a new
ON_EMBEDDED_WALLET_CONNECTION_LOST event (reasons: rpc-timeout,
handshake-timeout, iframe-reloaded) so hosts can react — e.g. the React
Native SDK reloading its hidden WebView.

Buffered WebView messages are now flushed on a microtask instead of
synchronously inside messenger initialization. connect() initializes the
messenger before it registers its handshake handlers in the same
synchronous block, so a synchronous flush routed buffered messages (the
iframe's first SYN) to zero handlers and dropped them. The redundant
pre-connect initialize call in doInitialize is removed for the same
reason — it also installed a permissive validator that shadowed
connect()'s proper one.

description:

description:
The user is now able to add, delete, and in general manage multiple
wallets on the same instance of Phoenix. Each wallet can have its own
name and avatar. Internally, wallets are indexed by the hash160 of the
wallet's public node id.

The seed file now stores multiple mnemonics.

The PhoenixBusiness object managing the actual node and coroutines is
now stored by a BusinessManager singleton. Data can be accessed safely
from anywhere including the background service workers. Several
businesses can run concurrently, although this can affect performance,
which will be fixed in a later commit.

Preferences are now per wallet and are managed by a DataStoreManager.
A new global preferences datastore has been added for preferences that
are global to the application, and not a given wallet.

Several ambients assuming non-nullable objects have been removed.

The startup and screenlock mechanism have been reworked to handle
multiple wallets. Specifically, a wallet selector screen lets the user picks
a wallet when needed, though there's also a system to load a wallet
automatically when relevant.

The active wallet is displayed in the Settings menu screen, as well as 
the Receive and Send screen (with incoming liquidity or balance for
convenience)

The navigation graph has been reworked and split into several files for
improved readability.

* (ios) Removed obsolete CloseDatabase parameter when stopping business

This parameter was introduced and used only by the Android app because of
long standing issues with the background system, which have been fixed with
the multiple wallets support update.

title: Support background payment reception (#104)
description:
Support has been added for background payment reception, using Firebase
Cloud Messaging to wake up the app. The wallet register a FCM token with 
the peer and can wake up when the peer wants to send a fulfilled HTCL or an
incoming payment.

A service has been added, handling all interactions with the underlying nodes.
This service can be headless, in which case a foreground notification is 
displayed ; or it can be bound to the UI, in which case interaction with the 
node from the UI is done through the shared `AppViewModel`, using the 
`service` mutable.

The state of the kit is now set in the service, and can be observed from the shared
`AppViewModel`. When the service is not reachable a special state is used.

A new `EncryptedSeed.V2` object has been added, using the Android Keystore 
and the biometrics api to securely store the seed while allowing background 
processing. `WithAuth` requires user authentication to use the key and as such
the background processing features.

Most of the `EncryptedSeed.V1` code and PIN logic has been removed ; some 
of it has been kept for migration purposes. Migration from V1 to V2 is done
when users unlocks the app for the first time after update.

A `SeedManager` class has been added to abstract operations on the seed file.

The access setting screen has been reworked and is more simple. Authentication
errors at startup are now separated from the kit state, due to the fact that the app
can be started, but not unlocked yet.

First time user experience screens have been added to introduce the app to 
new users. 

Pay-to-open requests are now automatically accepted by default. Users can disable
this, in which case a system notification is displayed when a request is incoming.

A metadata database has been added, storing data about payments that are 
outside the scope of the underlying node db and should not be stored there. 
This include data about opening or closing channels, and data for swap-

title: Apply several iOS and Android hotfixes (#327)
description:
* Use full domain for lnurl-auth linking key

The login service domain is used to compute the signing key. Instead of
using the etld+1, we now use the full domain name. Any subdomain change
by the service will be dealt by the service. Backward compatibility is
ensured for services known to already use lnurl-auth, so that users can
login to their existing account. New services will use the full domain.

This commit affects the legacy android app and the ios app.
LNURL auth tests have been updated in phoenix-android, as well as 
unit tests for deserializing lnurl-pay metadata (including with data from 
older client).

* Use `KeyManager` to in `WalletManager` instead of using a special
purpose `Wallet` class that duplicated key derivation logic. This is cleaner
and lets us reuse methods that are already defined in lightning-kmp.

* (android-legacy) Upgrades for android 12+

Add Immutable flag to pending intent. Upgrade nav lib
for the same reason and upgrade navargs and work manager 
dependencies. Add exported flag to main activity.

* (android-legacy) Upgrade docker build

Note: those changes were already released in separate hotfix branches.

Co-authored-by: Robbie Hanson <robbiehanson@deusty.com>

title: Handle extra payments and local HTLC replay (#181)
description:
This commit fixes an issue where the wallet would not be able to discriminate 
between extra payments on an already paid invoice and local htlc replay, forcing 
the app to accept both just in case. As such, already paid payments could be 
paid twice (or more), without the database being able to properly represent that.

The https://github.com/ACINQ/lightning-kmp/pull/271 in lightning-kmp changed
the incoming payment object to now contain the detailed parts of the payments 
sent to that invoice, including for lightning payment the HTLC id and the id of the 
channel that carried it.

This commit builds upon this change and updates the received-with database
serialization: a new typeversion has been added and the serialized data is now a 
set of Parts (that can be htlc/newchannel).

Fixes #100

Adding the signature check without adding the chainId to txData
results in signature mismatch as the etherumjs library wrongly creates
a mainnet signer without the specified chainId

title: chore(yarn): auto-run allow-scripts via Yarn plugin (#7048)
description:
Running `yarn install` today silently skips postinstall scripts (due to our usage of `enableScript: false` and lavamoat allow-scripts), leading to missing binaries (e.g. Skia prebuilts) and cryptic build failures on the native projects, unless you remember to run `yarn setup` at the right times. 

This change improves the developer experience by making `yarn install` automatically run whitelisted postinstall scripts using the official [LavaMoat Yarn plugin](https://github.com/LavaMoat/LavaMoat/tree/main/packages/yarn-plugin-allow-scripts), matching developer expectations while maintaining the same security model.

From a security perspective this plugin is from LavaMoat (same team behind `@lavamoat/allow-scripts` we already trust). The code is minimal; it just runs `yarn run allow-scripts` after install. The checksum is recorded in `.yarnrc.yml` so any upstream changes would fail verification.

title: chore: replace bespoke Metro dependency guard with dependency-cruiser (#7628)
description:
We enforce two dependency rules today through a bespoke Metro babel transformer at https://github.com/rainbow-me/metro-plugin-anisotropic-transform: 
* no third-party package may import our own first-party code, and 
* only a package itself may import the capability-sensitive native modules (`react-native-keychain`, `@react-native-clipboard/clipboard`, `react-native-video`)

This change moves both rules to [`dependency-cruiser`](https://github.com/sverweij/dependency-cruiser), a standard dependency-rule linter, and deletes the transform.

The transform is the wrong tool in the wrong layer, and it has been quietly costing us:

* **It silently breaks Sentry**. On CI, Sentry wraps the transformer chain and passes the downstream transformer its component-annotate babel plugin as a top-level plugins argument. The transform's wrapper forwards only { src, filename, options }, so that plugins array is dropped before React Native's transformer runs. Every CI and release bundle has therefore shipped without React component annotations (data-sentry-source-file), leaving our Sentry component stacks missing source-file/component attribution on releases. iOS has never had it (Bitrise sets CI=true); Android loses it the moment release builds move to CI (WIP). Removing the transform restores annotations on both platforms.
* **It is brittle and blocks React Native upgrades.** The fork hard-codes which upstream babel transformer to load per RN minor version and already required manual fork surgery for the RN 0.73 transformer move; every future RN bump risks the same. A static dependency check should never be a gate on upgrading the framework.
* **It runs outside its own supported configuration.** Its README requires `inlineRequires: false`; we run `inlineRequires: true`, so even its stated guarantees are on shaky ground.

title: fix: allow private key import over damaged seed wallet (APP-3443) (#7254)
description:
* fix: allow private key import over damaged seed wallet (APP-3443)

When a user's seed wallet is damaged (keychain data lost after device migration),
re-importing via private key was blocked by the 'already imported' guard because
isPrivateKeyOverwritingSeedMnemonic was true.

Adding !alreadyExistingWallet.damaged exception allows users to repair a damaged
wallet by re-importing with a private key, consistent with the existing support
workaround of 'delete wallet and re-add with private key'.

Seed phrase re-import over a damaged seed wallet already worked correctly.

* fix: read damaged status from walletsStore instead of keychain

The damaged flag is only set in the Zustand walletsStore (via
checkKeychainIntegrity), never persisted back to keychain. So reading it
from the keychain-loaded wallet data via getAllWallets() always returned
undefined, making the damaged wallet exception ineffective.

Use getIsDamagedWallet() which reads from the walletsStore where the
flag actually lives.
